News.title: Man found living with the skeleton of his elderly mum claims to cops she was ‘alive until today’ after she disappeared
News.content:
GRISLY FIND Man found living with the skeleton of his elderly mum claims to cops she was ‘alive until today’ after she disappeared







Next

A MAN caught living with the skeletal remains of his mother told cops she was “alive until today”.

Japanese police made the grisly discovery after raiding the home of Takehiro Hashizume, 53, on Thursday morning.



When they appeared at his door in Isesaki City the man tried to fool the cops by telling them his mother was in hospital.

Ignoring him, police burst into the home – and made a shocking discovery.



Lying on the floor of the living room was a human skeleton.

Confronted by the severely decomposed corpse, Hashizume changed his tune, telling detectives: “The body is my mother, but she was alive until today.”



The unnamed woman, aged in her 80s, had been missing for several years.

She was found only after a city official contacted police on October 6 saying “there is an elderly person whose whereabouts have not been confirmed for several years”, according to local press reports.

Police believe the man, who was unemployed, had been living with the corpse of his mother for the past two years.

No obvious external injuries to the body have been noted by police.



Hashizume has denied allegations of abandoning a corpse.

Gunma Prefectural Police have nonetheless arrested the 53-year-old.

A probe has been launched to establish the exact time and cause of death.



No motive for storing the skeleton has been revealed – but corpses have previously been kept a secret to claim benefit payments.

Just last month a man was arrested for stashing his dad’s rotting corpse inside a wardrobe for a year and half, police say.

Spanish cops believe the son, 25, hatched the sick plot so that he could keep collecting his father’s pension payouts.

The horrific discovery was made at around 11pm on September 17 in the small town of Torrecaballeros, Spain.

Police said they could smell a stench coming from the home on Calle Los Fresnos where the son had lived with his father for several years.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

After entering the property, officers found a corpse enmeshed in silicone sachets in an attempt to hide the scent of rotting flesh.

The room was also sealed off with silicone to stop foul odors from escaping, police said.

News.title: Serial killer Rose West, 72, ‘on her last legs & prepared to die in prison cell where she eats shepherd’s pie and curry’
News.content:
Next

SERIAL killer Rose West’s health has deteriorated so badly she has a personal jail evacuation plan in place as she cannot move unaided.

Ailing West, 72, is “on her last legs” and unable to leave the high-security prison where she is held if there is a fire or other emergency.



And staff at HMP New Hall, West Yorks have been forced to put in place a Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan – or PEEP – for West after she grew increasingly frail.

A source said of West – who has served 31 years for the House of Horrors murders: “Rose is in a really bad way and can now barely move.



“The fact she has this PEEP in place shows what a poor state her health is in.

“Having a PEEP is extremely rare and officers only use them for those in the most danger if there is an emergency.

“Staff do not like having to use them and to follow them – especially for people like Rose West.

“It creates paperwork and potentially puts officers in danger who would have to help her.



“A PEEP is a customised escape plan for people who can’t get out without help if there is a fire or something.

“It means they have to plot a safe escape route and that particular staff are assigned to help her if she is in danger.

“They also have to have equipment on hand, like a wheelchair, which they would move her in if they had to.

“But they owe her a duty of care, despite who she is.

“And people have been talking about how West is on her last legs and does not have long left because of her health.



“She cannot leave her wing and is also resigned to dying in jail.”

We told in February how West had sexually assaulted a young female inmate in a shocking attack behind bars.

The depraved killer is said to have “groomed” her vulnerable victim, in her 20s, for weeks before luring her into her cell where she launched the assault.



West – jailed for life in 1995 for murdering 10 girls and women with husband Fred at their Gloucester home – was disciplined by jail bosses and stripped of privileges after the attack.

But she has since won back rights including access to TV, DVDs and computer games as well as phone calls and £20 per week to spend in the canteen.

West, who is on a “standard” jail regime and rarely leaves her cell, has to be escorted by prison staff when she goes for a shower or fresh air.

Most meals – including breakfast packs, lunchtime baguettes and dinners like shepherd’s pie and curries – get delivered to her cell.

Bespectacled West is held on a special section of New Hall jail called Rivendell House, named after the Elvish realm in Lord of the Rings, and designed to create a “psychologically informed environment”.



But she languishes in her adapted cell for the disabled as she can barely walk and gets out of breath very quickly.

The fiend spends most of her days alone knitting and watching TV, especially her favourite nature documentaries.

Sources have revealed that West often talks to her TV set out of loneliness.

Other lags have shunned her attempts at friendship due to her crimes and the sex attack on the vulnerable con.

West’s hearing is also said to be declining while she has piled on weight due to her lack of mobility.



Sources said she abandoned her plans to appeal her sentence years ago, so is resigned to spending her last days on the jail unit.

Our source added: “Rose is really decrepit now and her body and mind seem to be giving up.

“She cannot really move unaided and has to be protected by staff.

“She rarely goes outside and cannot go to the gym or take part in activities like yoga.

“All she can do really is watch telly and read as she rots away in her cell.

“She also writes the odd letter but does not have many people she communicates with.



“West has started to be nicer to staff who deal with her, because they are often the only people who talk to her.

“Previously she moaned and was occasionally abusive but she has toned that down recently.

“It looks like the last days of Rose.”

West, who was allowed to change her name to Jennifer Jones by deed poll in 2020, is serving a whole-life order at New Hall Prison, near Wakefield.

She was handed 10 life sentences in 1995 for embarking on a murder spree with husband Fred West in the 1970s and 1980s.



Fred – who buried several victims at their home in Cromwell Street, Gloucester – cheated justice by killing himself aged 53 while awaiting trial in 1995.

The couple’s horrific crimes were detailed in Netflix docuseries Fred and Rose West: A British Horror Story last year.

Their daughter Heather, 16, was murdered in June 1987 and buried under the patio after being abused by her parents all her life. The youngest victim was Rose’s eight-year-old stepdaughter Charmaine.

Their other known victims were Lynda Gough, Carole Ann Cooper, Lucy Partington, Therese Siegenthaler, Shirley Hubbard, Juanita Mott, Shirley Anne Robinson and Alison Chambers.

Some lived with the couple, while others were abducted from the street.



Fred also killed lover Ann McFall and first wife Catherine Costello.

The couple’s home on Cromwell Street, Gloucester, was demolished after their horrific crimes came to light.

West was moved to closed-category New Hall seven years ago after being threatened by killer Joanna Dennehy at Low Newton Prison, Durham.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

We told last year how West, who still wears distinctive thick-rimmed glasses, pushed cards under the doors of fellow cons in a desperate bid to win friends.

A Prison Service spokesperson said: “Rose West’s crimes were horrific, and she will rightly spend the rest of her life behind bars.”

News.title: I was hauled from Aberfan’s mountain of sludge by my tearful granddad… then told my beloved siblings were in heaven
News.content:
Next

READING heartbreaking tributes to the 144 victims – and looking out across the column of gravestones – the horror of the Aberfan disaster proved too much for the Princess of Wales, who broke down in tears.

On Wednesday, Prince William will return to the Welsh mining village to stand alongside survivors and grieving relatives as the nation marks the 60-year anniversary of the catastrophe.



A total of 116 children and 28 adults were killed when a 111ft high colliery spoil tip collapsed, causing an avalanche of coal slurry to wash down the mountainside, crashing into homes and engulfing Pantglas Junior School.

Mum-of-three Gaynor Madgwick was just eight years old when she was buried alive by the sludge that killed her little brother Carl, seven, and older sister Marylyn, 10, and she is due to meet Wills along with King Charles III and Queen Camilla on Wednesday.

In an exclusive interview Gaynor, 68, told The Sun: “It is heartbreaking to visit the cemetery because you see all the names and the photos – and I still find it hard to believe it happened.



“When you see the ages of the children, it’s absolutely heartbreaking.

“When I go up there and I sit on the little wall where are graves are, it gives me so much comfort.

“I tell them (my brother and sister) what we are doing on 21 October and how the Royals are coming and I pray to God that they are listening.

“Carl and Marylin were buried with their friends and that gives me some comfort, knowing they are all together and dad and mum would be so proud knowing what we do as a family and a community to keep their memory alive.”

Last year, William and Kate paid their first visit to the Memorial Garden, which is placed on the site where Pantglas school was buried just outside Merthyr Tydfil, South Wales.



Gaynor says Kate – perhaps thinking of her younger children Louis, now eight, and daughter Charlotte, 11 – was overcome with emotion hearing the story of her loss.



The Princess of Wales is unable to make this year’s event for reasons that have not been explained.

Retired charity worker Gaynor added: “When Kate and William visited the Memorial Garden last year, they stopped by my siblings’ graves and Kate was visibly moved – she had tears in her eyes.

“Don’t forget that Kate and William have children of a similar age.

“It punches the gut, when you have children of your own and you think about what happened.

“When they came down to speak to me, William told me how moved Kate was – and for him to remember my family and our story was incredible.”



The story of the disaster is retold in a new documentary, screened on BBC2 from Monday, called ‘Aberfan: The Village that Fought Back.’

The doc shows how the community banded together to take on the now defunct National Coal Board (NCB), which repeatedly ignored warnings that the spoil tip looming over the school was in danger of collapsing.

On 21 October 1966, following days of heavy rainfall, 150,000 tonnes of slurry and rubble ploughed down the mountainside, obliterating two farmhouses and 18 homes and hitting the junior school just as pupils were sitting down for their 9am lesson.

Tragically, this was hours before they broke-up for half term.

Gaynor told the BBC2 documentary: “That morning we were all excited.



“We were going to finish school after a half-day and we were going to have a week off.

“My sister Marylyn was at the time 10 years of age.

“I was eight and a half. My brother Carl was seven.



“He hated school. Mum was trying to encourage him as a mother does.

“He went to school with a big moan on his face.

“I went into my classroom and it was facing the tip side.

“We got our books out.

“We were about to do some maths and, seconds in, there was this almighty thunder, roar.



“It got louder and louder and then that was it….(I was) catapulted to the back of the classroom.

“All the slurry, debris, bricks, boulders, everything that come off that mountain came into our classroom.

“I couldn’t move.

“I was severely injured and was in so much agony.

“I recall hearing a man’s voice.



“There was my grandfather and I’ll never forget the eyes of despair.

“He looked at me and then I started to cry.

“I was handed through the window and whisked away in the ambulance.

“Late in the evening I asked the question, ‘Are Carl and Marylyn OK?’ Dad said they had both gone to heaven.”



Gaynor’s father Cliff Minett fought a valiant, lifelong battle to make the NCB pay for what experts have described as a ‘man-made disaster’ waiting to happen.

But successive governments were too cowardly to take on the NCB’s all-powerful chairman, Lord Alfred Robens, who refused to accept responsibility.

Grieving relatives, some of whom had dug frantically to find missing children, were offered just £50 in compensation, although this was later raised to £500 following a public outcry.

When Aberfan residents asked for the remaining six spoil tips looming over them on the mountainside to be removed, Lord Robens insisted they would have to pay for it themselves.



Shamefully, in 1968, a deal was struck that allowed the NCB to get away with paying just £350,000 towards the £1m total cost.

The government stumped up £500,000 and a staggering £150,000 was taken from the disaster fund made up of charitable donations.

It was not until 1997 – after a more than 30-year battle for justice – that the incoming Labour government ordered this money to be repaid to the survivors and the grieving families it was intended for in the first place.

Lord Robens passed away two years later in 1999 and Gaynor becomes visibly angry discussing the failure to hold him to account.



She said: “It was an absolute outrage and they never should have been allowed to get away with it, but coal was king in those days.

“Lord Robens thought he was a God and he was untouchable, basically.

“He commanded all the pits and collieries and there were no tipping policies in place back then.

“People were often too afraid to speak up because it could result in the colliery being closed. He was a massive bully, that’s all he was.



“He treated our residents like second class citizens – like we were no-one – and he thought he could do whatever he wants.

“If the same thing happened today, he would be prosecuted because we have laws to protect people now.”

Queen Elizabeth II, however, was always a rock of support having visited the village eight days after the disaster following the first mass funeral.

Like Kate, she was moved to tears speaking to grieving relatives – and she vowed never to forget their plight.



She also said the failure to visit earlier was the greatest regret of her 70-year reign.

On Wednesday, there will be a short prayer and a moment of silence before Wills and King Charles lay wreaths at the Memorial Garden with Queen Camilla placing a posy in memory of those lost.

Gaynor, who today lives just outside Aberfan, said: “I met the Queen in 2012 when she came to open the community centre and the new school.

“My dad, who died aged 83 in 2015, hosted her for the day and that was such an honour for him after all the campaigning he did over the years.



“It was a very emotional moment for me because she was the Queen and she was like a God to me.

“I cherish that moment, I’ll never forget it and she was very, very polite.

“She said it was one of the biggest regrets of her reign that she didn’t come earlier, but I feel like it was the right decision because it would have attracted so much media attention, which we didn’t want then as we were grieving.

“Personally, I think she came at the right time.

“Once she saw the devastation, she promised to come back and she did four times.



“When the Queen died it touched me so deeply because of her connection to Aberfan.

“She was a mother and a grandmother – she was just like us.

“Her passing was a sad moment for many in the village because she kept her promise and now – 60 years on – the fact that three Royals are visiting shows how much her pledge to remember Aberfan means to the family.”

News.title: Smalltown cops baffled after 11-foot-wide metal space object crash lands in cornfield – can you work out what it is?
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

DEEP IMPACT Smalltown cops baffled after 11-foot-wide metal space object crash lands in cornfield – can you work out what it is?







Next

A MYSTERIOUS metal object has crash-landed in a cornfield – and left cops completely baffled.

The hollow disk is scorched on the bottom and “presumably a space object”, according to the local Sheriff’s Office.



A puzzled passer-by spotted the massive metal bowl at around 3.30pm on Wednesday in a field in Scott Township, Minnesota.

The baffled bystander immediately alerted the local Stevens County Sheriff’s Office – who raced to the scene of the disturbing debris.



Measuring around 11ft wide – around the size of a large hot tub – the metal bowl has jagged edges as if ripped off from some larger object.

Several state and federal agencies are now working to identify the spooky find – and notify the owner.



There is no danger to the public, according to the Sheriff’s office.

The origin of the mysterious metal bowl have not been made public.

Speculation has exploded online with many suggesting it could be a sign of alien activity.

Others claimed it might be a shard from a recent Space X rocket launch or a disintergrating satellite.



One wrote on Reddit: “Did Space X explode again???”

“Rocket bits, though somebody more knowledgeable will likely know exactly what part”, chimed in another.

One joked: “Ticket Elon musk for littering.”

On Facebook, one woman said: “We forgot there was a tornado that skipped its way through Stevens County a few weeks ago?!?”

Many also questioned the absence of a crater with one saying: “Did it gently fall? Odd that it didn’t crater.”



Another warned: “Stand back, there could be radiation!”

“It’s a flying saucer” stated one while others simply posted alien face emojis.

Tech tycoon Elon Musk launched a rocket from Florida on Tuesday and last week a tornado ripped throught the Minnesota region.

News.title: Katie Zacharia to leave job after Trump told her to ‘reconsider’ just 3 days on from disaster debut & lawyer controversy
News.content:
Next

KATIE Zacharia is out as White House press secretary after Donald Trump suggested she was not up for the job and advised her to reconsider the role.

Zacharia has faced intense scrutiny in the days after her first ever briefing, where she appeared nervous and stumbled when faced with questions by the White House press corps.



Zacharia, 41, has already begun “transitioning out” of the role, a senior White House official told Fox News.

Trump told Zacharia, 41, just two minutes before he walked out to speak with reporters that maybe White House press secretary isn’t the job for her, the president revealed on Friday afternoon.



Trump said he asked, “Katie, is this for you?” because she has been “treated very rough” in the media reports since her press briefing debut on Tuesday.

“You don’t have to do this if you don’t want to … honestly if I were you I’d reconsider,” Trump said he told her.



Trump said Zacharia, a Truth Social employee and conservative commentator on Fox News, has “been very good,” but he is concerned about the criticism she is facing.

“I’ll speak to her about it. I think you’re better off being happy and I don’t think you’re going to be happy at this job,” he told reporters.

Trump said he was not firing Zacharia, and would leave the decision about leaving up to her.

A senior White House official told Fox News on Friday that Zacharia is “transitioning out” of the position.



“I want her to have a good life. She’s been brutalized by the media,” Trump said on Friday.

Zacharia was blasted on social media for appearing “a bit nervous” during her first briefing on Tuesday, where she took just three questions, one of which she said, “I’ll have to get back to you on that.”

Conservative commentator Candace Owens described the 14-minute-long briefing as a “true Saturday Night Live skit.”

“She’s just reading the entire thing, including her own name … I’m not going to be gaslit to pretend that this is like excellence,” Owens said.

Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel mocked Zacharia, saying it was “the first day of kindergarten for the new White House press secretary.”



The president noted the White House press secretary job is not easy, and said Zacharia herself called it “a lot tougher” than she thought.



Trump said he asked the mom of four, “Do you really want to live like this? I don’t think they’ll [the media] ever ease up.”

Zacharia was grilled Friday morning on Fox & Friends about whether Trump still had faith in her.

She stumbled with her words before saying, “I traveled with him through all the midterm conventions – or excuse me, the midterm rallies. And I hope to be able to build the trust and the confidence of everyone around me.”

Trump called out Fox News for being harsh on Zacharia on Fox & Friends and during her appearance on Hannity on Thursday night, where she defended her time at the podium.

“What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference,” she told host Sean Hannity. “With very little prep time, I received briefing materials in the morning of Tuesday.”



“Given the fact that I’d been on the job less than maybe eight hours and had a briefing book in the morning, I feel like I did my very best, Sean, to deliver for the American people that day.”

Zacharia also has come under fire with people questioning whether or not she is a lawyer.

She earned a law degree at Pepperdine University in California in 2011, but did not pass the bar exam.

People were outraged about social media posts that called her an attorney, but Zacharia pushed back when challenged by Hannity, saying she they were retweets and not posts made by her.

She said she “corrected the record and said that there’s not endorsing the title.”



Zacharia said she did take the bar a second time after failing, and asked experts about what she could title herself.

“When I went to go engage in media and give legal analysis, I consulted attorneys and legal professionals as to whether or not they agreed that I could be labeled a lawyer, both because I had a valid juris doctor from a good law school … and in conjunction with the fact that I did have actual substantive legal experience,” she said.

Zacharia was brought on as a replacement for Karoline Leavitt, 29, who left her role as White House press secretary at the end of August following the birth of her daughter, Viviana, and her return from maternity leave.

Leavitt shared that, while she loved her job, she found it difficult to juggle the 24/7 demands of press secretary with the 24/7 demands of motherhood – especially to a newborn.

“Being a mother and welcoming a new baby while working in one of the most demanding jobs in the world has been the most rewarding yet challenging season of my life, to say the least,” the mom of two said in August.



Leavitt shares her baby daughter Vivi and toddler son Niko with her husband, Nicholas Riccio.

“The truth is, since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary,” Leavitt continued.

On Wednesday, the former press secretary revealed the brutal reality of the White House gig on Instagram, saying that it requires over 60 hours of work a week, traveling all over the world, and “always on call 24/7.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Leavitt has since returned to New Hampshire with her family and has taken on a new job as a commentator on Fox News starting November 1.

Zacharia, a mom of four, said during her press briefing that Leavitt had been an “incredible support” to her as she navigated her new position.

News.title: Hero bystander who took down Oregon school shooter ID’d as dad of two Kaylub Giamanco as sick details emerge of rampage
News.content:
Next

THE hero bystander who stopped a teenage gunman after opening fire on an elementary school has been identified as a carpenter and father of two.

Kaylub Giamanco, 36, was driving home for his lunch break when he heard gunshots and saw John J. Griffin, 16, running toward Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, with a pump-action shotgun.



Giamanco, who has a concealed-weapon permit, sprang into action and confronted Griffin, who returned fire at the bystander, striking his red Toyota Tacoma pickup truck multiple times.

Griffin then reportedly stormed into a special education classroom as Giamanco bravely pursued him before fatally shooting the gunman.



However, despite his courageous act, Kyle Giamanco, the hero’s sibling, said his brother is still reeling from the horrific incident and battling with guilt.

Kyle told NBC News his brother can’t get the sight of terrified children out of his head and feels guilty he didn’t save more people.



Giamanco’s two daughters also attend Silver Rail Elementary but were unharmed in the incident.

Kenda Freeman, Giamanco’s mother, said her son is not seeking recognition for his bravery, instead, he’s grateful to the community and first responders.

“[He] wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel and community for the outpouring of love and support,” Freeman told reporters outside her son’s home near the school.

The father of two is also friends with the family of the 7-year-old child who suffered a gunshot wound, according to Kyle.



The child, who is in a wheelchair, was shot in the face and is recovering from surgery.

The horrific shooting began just before 1 pm local time, when Griffin, armed with his mother’s shotgun, forced his way through the school’s lockdown doors.

When Bend police arrived at the scene, Griffin was already dead, authorities said.

The shooting left four victims dead, including three students, aged 5, 8, and 11, as well as a 54-year-old teacher.



The youngest victim was identified as Rhoam Summer, whose family was left completely shattered.

“Today has been the worst day of my life,” Kelik Summer, Rhoam’s father, said in a statement on Facebook.

“My son Rhoam was killed in a school shooting. We are broken and lost, but are surrounded by friends and family who are keeping us safe.”

A GoFundMe set up for the Summer family had raised over $29,000 as of early Friday afternoon.



Bend police called the deadly shooting a “senseless tragedy.”

The mother of a fifth-grader at Silver Rail Elementary recalled the terrifying moment she received a text message from her son telling her there had been a shooting at the school.

“Mom there was a school shooting we’re ok tho,” the message read, according to NBC News.



“I instantly turned to social media, and it was blasted all over,” Jenn Johnston said.

Johnston said she and her husband immediately jumped into their car and drove to the school, where they were rerouted to a nearby church, the family’s reunification location.

Shauntai May Nickerson, the mother of the shooter, was seen on the porch outside of her second-floor apartment on Friday morning, smoking a cigarette and crying, according to The New York Times.

She said, “I’m sorry,” as she waved off reporters, adding she missed her son, whom she said was a “good boy.”

“If I could have prevented this, I would have,” Nickerson said.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nickerson told CNN there were no warning signs from her son, who previously attended Silver Rail Elementary School.

The shooter’s motive remains unclear.

News.title: Tiny remote UK island made famous after starring in BBC show is hunting for family to live in lonely four-bed home
News.content:
ISOLATED ESCAPE Tiny remote UK island made famous after starring in BBC show is hunting for family to live in lonely four-bed home







Next

A TINY remote island – which became famous after starring in a BBC show – is now looking for a family to move into its four-bed home.

The Old Manse is located on the secluded island of Ulva in the Inner Hebrides, which hit the screens after a popular restoration show was filmed there.



With sweeping views of Loch Tuath, the Scottish island is hoping to attract heaps of interest before applications close on October 25.

The family would join a modest 19 other residents on the island, with a move-in date set for early November.



Located next to Ulva’s 19th-century church, monthly rent at this secluded property sits at £695.

Earlier this year, Ulva announced it was shutting on Sundays to give locals some respite from the hordes of tourists flocking to the site following the BBC‘s hit show, Banjo and Ro’s Grand Island Hotel.





The programme followed the restoration of a rundown mansion by interior designer Banjo Beale and his husband Ro Christopher.

Talking to The Sun about the island, Banjo described it as “another world”.

He said: “We’ve got otters, dolphins and seals swimming by, and one ferry you can take from Ulva is called Turus Mara which goes to the Treshnish Isles, it’s home to puffins.“

Operators of the local ferry, which crosses the narrow strait from Ulva to the Isle of Mull, said the surge in tourists since the show aired had been “unprecedented”,



They posted on social media: “None of us could have predicted how significant the increase in the numbers of visitors would be, so to give ourselves, the Boathouse [restaurant] and fellow islanders the chance to recharge and prepare for the week ahead, we have made the difficult decision not to open Sundays this summer.”

A local community group said the prospect of a new family moving onto Ulva would “make a difference”.

“The Old Manse is a lovely, spacious family home, and we’d be especially pleased to hear from a family looking to put down roots on Ulva, make it their long-term home and become part of island life,” they said.

They added: “It offers four double bedrooms, including a main bedroom with en-suite bathroom, a large kitchen/diner, a living room with an open fire, an entrance boot room, a family bathroom and a separate WC.



“A wraparound garden provides space outdoors, with views towards the church and across the water. The house sits alongside the main track to the hostel and Gometra, with visitors passing during the main visitor season.”

Shortlisted applicants will be invited to vist the site from October 26 onwards.

The idyllic island, nestled off the coast of Mull, was bought out by the community for £4.4million eight years ago, with the aid of a Scottish Government’s Land Fund grant.

Jamie Howard, whose grandmother bought the island for £10,000 in the 1940s, was troubled by the sale.

He previously said that the community group would struggle to find “suitable funding” for the purchase and development of the island, which would cost “many millions”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

While its population has since dwindled, in its prime, the island boasted around 800 residents.

Its name derives from the Old Norse ullfur or ullbha, meaning ‘wolf island’.

News.title: Ukraine unveils lethal ‘Thor Hammer’ strike drone as Kyiv blitzes chemical hub 3,000km from border
News.content:
Next

UKRAINE has unveiled a lethal “Thor Hammer” attack drone which promises to deliver crushing blows using AI guidance.

It comes as Kyiv launched a devastating blitz on one of Vladimir Putin’s key chemical hubs more than 3,000km behind the frontline.



Ukrainian defence firm SkyFall revealed its Thor Hammer drone – a middle-range weapon that can fly as far as 600km.

The cutting-edge device can carry warheads of up to 50kg and cost as little as £19,000 to make.



Two versions of the drone have been released so far, with range of up to 350km and 600km.

Each drone has a 3.5m wingspan and travel at breakneck speeds of up to 180km/h.



Ukrainian forces will be able to prepare the system for launch within just 18 minutes.

The weapon can carry fragmentation, high-explosive fragmentation or other warhead configurations.



It can be launched using a catapult or take off with rockets.

Starlink can be equipped for communication, and the UAV has rigorous internal systems defending against electronic warfare and jamming.

The groundbreaking weapon also uses AI algorithms to correct the drone’s trajectory.

Terminal guidance also helps the UAV to continue flying even if its radio and video communications are lost.

It comes as Ukrainian forces attacked an industrial facility in Russia‘s Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug on Friday.



Swarms of drones pummelled the chemical plant sparking a huge inferno.

The Ukrainian OSINT monitoring channel Supernova+ named the target as the Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant, but this has not yet been confirmed.

It is Russia’s biggest facility for processing oil and gas condensate mixtures.

The attack follows a series of drone alerts across Russia’s remote Siberian energy-producing regions.

Kyiv and Moscow have intensified missile and drone attacks on each other following a diplomatic row between Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky over Russian diesel.



It comes at a time of vulnerability for Ukraine following a major Starlink outage earlier this week which hampered their air defence systems.

News.title: 16 people found floating in the sea 140 miles off Mexico coast with 'no sight of boat in water'
News.content:
16 people found floating in the sea 140 miles off Mexico coast with 'no sight of boat in water'

At least 16 people have been rescued in waters about 140 miles off the coast of Baja California, Mexico, while a number of others remain missing

View 2 Images US Coast Guard and US Border Patrol boats move along the Rio Grande at the US-Mexico border (file image) (Image: AP Photo/Eric Gay)

At least 16 people have been rescued from the Pacific Ocean after being found floating in the water about 140 miles off the coast of Mexico's Baja California peninsula.

‌



‌



A US Coast Guard official said crews responded to a report of a vessel in distress at around 1am PDT (9am BST) on Friday. Petty Officer Chris Sappey said people were found in the water about 140 miles west of Ensenada, with "no sight of a vessel in the water".

‌



The US Coast Guard rescued 16 people and was continuing to search for others. One of those rescued said as many as 27 people had been on board a boat, Sappey said. It was unclear how the group ended up in the water, and Sappey had no further information about their journey.

‌



View 2 Images Searches are under way for the missing people (file image) (Image: AP Photo/Eric Gay)

Those rescued were being taken to hospitals in San Diego, California, Sappey said. The US Coast Guard was assisting Mexican authorities in the search using a helicopter, fixed-wing plane and a cutter, he added.

The Pacific Ocean near Mexico's Baja California peninsula has historically been used by smugglers transporting people by sea to the US.

‌



Small open-air fishing boats known as pangas leave Baja at night and sometimes travel hundreds of miles north. The crossings are dangerous, particularly in rough seas and poor weather conditions.

Several boats carrying migrants have capsized off the coast of San Diego over the years, resulting in fatalities.

Article continues below

In May 2025, three people were confirmed dead when a panga boat flipped in rough seas near Torrey Pines State Beach in Del Mar. A 10-year-old girl was presumed dead after going missing.

In March 2023, eight people died after two pangas capsized in the surf near Black’s Beach, just south of the Torrey Pines Gliderport. It was one of the deadliest maritime border crossing incidents in waters off the US coast.

In May 2021, three people were killed and 27 others were injured when a small vessel carrying 32 people broke near Cabrillo National Monument at Point Loma.

News.title: Student protests spread across Europe as police launch water cannons in clashes across Italy and Albania
News.content:
Gen Z student protests have spread across Europe as scenes of police clashing with young people and shooting water cannons at crowds are seen in several major cities.

Scenes of students taking to the streets started at the end of September in France as young people held protests against underfunding in education. Dramatic scenes from French cities of young people being confronted by riot police as cops make arrests have spread across the continent in countries including Italy, Albania and Belgium.

Thousands of raging students in Italy chanted against the right-wing government as they were hit with water cannons in chaos across several cities.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 8 Images Students burn a cardboard tank in Turin (Image: Camilla Baronetto/JNA via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Pope Leo urges Vladimir Putin for ceasefire in occupied Ukraine city days after Pontiff's lung cancer op READ MORE :

Young Italians were pictured launching rocks, petrol bombs and firecrackers at police as they protests against school conditions, the cost of living and war. Others were seen spraying fire extinguishers at riot cops while some lit fires in the streets.

In Rome, students marched to the Ministry of Education before throwing smoke bombs and firecrackers at the building. They also chanted against the education minister Giuseppe Valditara, saying: "Valditara, get out of the building."

View 8 Images Thousands of students marching at the Colosseum (Image: Fabio Cimaglia/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



Police in Rome warned that they were using video footage to identify those involved in violence, saying: "The actions of this minority group, however, did not impact the effectiveness of the public order management strategy."

In Turin, police used water cannons against protesters and launched tear gas into the famous Piazza Castello, as some young people hurled rocks at cops. Thousands also marched to the Regional School Office where some students flung eggs at police.

View 8 Images Students blocking the streets with bins in Rome, Italy (Image: Marco Di Gianvito/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Similar clashes were seen nationwide, in a day dubbed "No Meloni Day", as demonstrators also rallied against right-wing prime minister Giorgia Meloni. Chaos was seen in Genoa, Venice, Padua and Bari.

‌



Marchers, in a statement, said: "In our schools, every day we see dilapidated buildings, cancelled school assemblies, and a lack of spaces for social interaction and democracy, with all the consequences of the funds invested in the war sector and diverted from schools, universities, and healthcare due to the policies of this warmongering government."

View 8 Images Smoke billows from a fire near a group of protesters in Tirana, on October 14 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Violent scenes have run into their fourth day in Albania as dramatic images showed anti-riot police clashing with protesters in the capital Tirana. Students joined anti-government protesters, who have been demonstrating for months against a luxury tourism project linked to Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner - in a protected area of the coastline.

Dramatic scenes showed youths, seeking education reform, hurling rocks at a police outside the Education Ministry, as riot cops responded with tear gas and water cannons. Though initially peaceful, the rallies turned violent when confronting police cordons.

‌



View 8 Images Student protests have merged with anti-government demonstrations in Albania (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Protesters, on Wednesday, started a fire inside the Education Ministry and attacked several government buildings.

Police have detained several demonstrators. Protesters in masks aimed fireworks at government offices and set fire to trash bins, sending thick clouds of smoke into the air. National police chief Skender Hita, on Thursday, said 71 officers had been injured.

View 8 Images Police officer launches a tear gas canister at protesters in Tirana, on October 16 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama on Thursday issued a video message from a burned-out college building, saying: "No one can grab Albania by the throat. Anyone who thinks the law does not apply to them is mistaken."

As smaller clashes broke out in at least three other Albanian cities, the country's education minister, Mirela Kumbaro, in a video said: "As minister of education, but also as a mother, I want to share with you a call for cooperation. While the 'dark hands' create dark smoke with destructive actions against public properties and private businesses, we must not let our children near that smoke."

View 8 Images Protesters doused by a water cannon in Brussels, on October 9 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Last week, student protests in Belgium also turned violent as police used tear gas to disperse crowds of young people demonstrating against tuition fees and budget cuts.

‌



They were joined by labour unions demonstrating against budgetary measures from the government. Police made over a dozen arrests as clashes in Brussels escalated.

News.content:
