News.title: Ukrainian Vampire drones drop food on town besieged by Russian army
News.content:
On Ukraine’s front lines, drones are the deadliest weapons in Kyiv’s arsenal, hunting Russian soldiers one by one with chilling precision.

But across the Dnipro River, the same machines have been given a very different mission: keeping trapped civilians from dying of starvation.

Since March, Ukrainian drones have been flying food and medicine into occupied Oleshky, on the river’s left bank, where residents are surviving on grass and weeds.

The town is less than three miles from Kherson, a city battered by Russian drones and shelling.

Since December, Oleshky has been under an effective blockade. Its roads are mined and shops have closed, with no food arriving by road since late May. Humanitarian agencies are blocked from entering, and the health system has all but collapsed.

Only around 2,000 of its 24,000 pre-war residents remain. For them, the drones are now their only lifeline.

“With the onset of winter, the situation is only getting worse,” said Elvina Osmanova of the Kherson regional military administration. “Food supplies are running out. People are facing a life-threatening choice: risk their lives trying to find food outside the city or remain without food.”

News.title: Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle
News.content:
When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

“And it’s a bit of a shame because it’s not happening.

“So I wouldn’t be shocked if he looks elsewhere to get a game.



“On the other hand, if you’re Chelsea, you think, what happens if Rogers or Palmer get injured? We need somebody.

“And it’s the classic difficult situation that players in the modern game find themselves in.

“But a player of that talent, don’t waste it on benches all your life. I get a feeling he won’t.”

Estevao has plenty of competition for minutes in the Chelsea squad with the likes of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto, Geovany Quenda and Jamie Gittens all jostling for time on the pitch.



The teenager was signed by Chelsea in a deal worth nearly £50million and on a contract running until 2033.

Sports.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick planning incredible £6m overhaul to Cheshire farm including own dressing room & plunge pool
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK would be forgiven for wanting to shut the door of his £6million Cheshire farm and forget about football.

But plans the under-fire Manchester United boss has submitted to the local council reveal that he’s still got the “beautiful game” on his mind – even when at home.



Carrick, 45, hopes to block off an open archway to turn it into a boot room complete with hooks for clothes, a long bench and compartments underneath it for shoes.

The potential final product will look remarkably similar to a football dressing room.



Like most megabucks modern Premier League players, they expect the finest facilities.

Carrick – who is battling to keep his job at Old Trafford after United’s worst league start in 40 years – is also asking Cheshire East Council for a garden room at the bottom of his estate complete with a cold plunge bath, yoga space and a “hot box”.

The ex-England international wants to install a 22-foot by 16-foot timber outbuilding, which will also include a sauna and log burner.

This would not be out of kilter at United’s state-of-the-art Carrington training facility, which was upgraded last year and went through a £50m revamp.



Ice bath and saunas are standard territory in the facility.

Among the range of other benefits at the players’ disposal are altitude chambers, a sports science hub live-tracking training data, a barbers and even smart urinals to detect if a player is dehydrated.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS



The Red Devils legend needs consent from the local council because his historic pad, which he shares with wife Lisa and their two children, is Grade II-listed and lies on green belt land.

Carrick’s rural retreat boasts a five-bedroom farmhouse and two converted barns, one with four bedrooms, four reception rooms, a dressing room, music room, study and office.

The sprawling estate also includes a luxury stable block for seven horses, wash area, tack room, tea and office room and laundry area and outdoor riding arena and “muck truck”.



He first bought the two adjoining barns for £1.5million and £1.4million, described by estate agents as “tastefully refurbished and re-modelled in a quiet and secluded setting”.

Carrick and United will be looking to put the fallout from Lisandro Martinez’s explosive attack behind them when they travel to bitter rivals Leeds on Sunday, and register their first win in six games.

DANIEL FARKE launched a fierce defence of Michael Carrick – despite being desperate to check him into the Heartbreak Hotel.

And the Leeds boss channeled his inner-Elvis Presley to squash talk of his in-form side being favourites ahead of the latest chapter in the Roses Rivalry on Sunday.



German Farke won over the tough Elland Road crowd by leading them to safety last term following promotion.

Fans Can’t Help Falling in Love with him more and more with the Whites’ fine start to the Premier League campaign sparking dreams of European qualification.



Meanwhile, down the M62, it feels like a crisis at Old Trafford with defender Lisandro Martinez publicly attacking the club’s hierarchy while results have piled the pressure on Carrick.

Farke has come up against the ex-Middlesbrough boss six times – losing once – during his three-and-a-half years at Leeds. And he cannot understand why the knives are being sharpened.



He said: “When I think about Michael, we don’t have too many young British coaches and managers in the Premier League.

“Right now we have someone, a really young, promising manager who’s done an excellent job at Middlesbrough and he came in last season in a situation and helped a lot to stabilise the club, helped a lot to steady the ship, and has done an amazing job.

“After six game days, when they didn’t have a horrendous start but, of course, by their perception they want to fight for the title, the criticism starts already. I don’t like it.

Leeds, narrowly beaten 2-1 at champions Arsenal last week, are heavily fancied to pile even more pressure on Carrick this weekend.

While Farke is desperate for his boys to keep on rocking and rolling, The King of LS11 refuses to get Caught in a Trap by buying into that favourites tag.

BABY-FACED Lionel Messi was forced to wait his turn when he made his competitive Barcelona debut 22 years ago.

At just 17 years, three months, and 22 days, the Argentine came off the bench in the 82nd minute for Deco in a 1-0 victory over Espanyol on October 16, 2004.



The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner would go on to play 778 competitive games for the club.

Ronaldinho was already the star attraction, while Xavi Hernandez and Andres Iniesta still had their best years ahead of them.



But in the 22 years following, one star spent his birthday behind bars, while another has got into the cycling business.

SunSport has tracked what happened to the players who featured in Messi’s FIRST game.



#1 Victor Valdes

Victor Valdes went from a glittering Barca career to a relegation scrap with Middlesbrough, with a stint with Manchester United in the middle.

Since hanging up his boots, the 44-year-old briefly returned to his former club to coach Barca’s youth set-up before a short spell at Real Avila in 2025.



#2 Juliano Belletti

Juliano Belletti’s name will haunt Arsenal fans after scoring the winner in the 2006 Champions League final, before switching to Chelsea where he won the Premier League and FA Cup double in 2010.

The 50-year-old is back at the club to coach Barcelona Atletic, or Barca B, and is leading them in the 2026/27 season.

#4 Rafael Marquez

After a seven-year stint at the Camp Nou, Rafael Marquez headed for New York Red Bulls before spells with Leon and Hellas Verona.

Then, after a stint coaching Barca Atletic, the 47-year-old became Javier Aguirre’s assistant before taking over Mexico’s national team after their 2026 home World Cup.



#5 Carles Puyol

Carles Puyol was born for Barca – he made 593 competitive appearances before knee problems forced him to retire in 2014 – walking away with six LaLiga titles and the World Cup with Spain.

And with his flowing curls, the 48-year-old is a LaLiga Ambassador, participating in various events and promotions, while reportedly living a quiet life in Andorra with his partner and two daughters.

#12 Giovanni van Bronckhorst

Giovanni van Bronckhorst boasts quite the resume since hanging up his boots, winning the Dutch title as Feyenoord boss in 2017 before taking Rangers to the 2022 Europa League final.



He also had spells at Besiktas and on Liverpool’s coaching staff.

This summer, the 51-year-old ventured back to familiar surroundings for a second spell at Feyenoord in June, replacing Robin van Persie on a two-year deal with the option of another season.

#6 Xavi

Xavi Hernandez has won pretty much everything… eight league titles and four Champions Leagues at Barca, plus a World Cup and two Euros with Spain.

An Al-Sadd switch followed, before becoming their manager. He then returned to Barcelona and won La Liga from the touchline in 2023.

The Brazilian revealed later that he had been shocked to learn the documents were illegal.

Nonetheless, he was forced to spend his 40th birthday behind bars, where he stayed for 32 days before they were shifted to a luxury hotel under house arrest after posting about £1.2million bail.

After more than FIVE months in detention, Ronaldinho agreed to pay £68,000 to settle the case and left without a Paraguayan criminal record.



The football legend popped up at the summer’s World Cup joining Madonna’s half-time show, alongside Brazil’s Ronaldo driving a cart into the MetLife Stadium, New Jersey.

Now, the 49-year-old is back in his old digs as Barca’s sporting director after his appointment in 2023.

Henrik Larsson only spent two seasons at Barca, but he walked away with two LaLiga titles and a shiny Champions League medal.

The 55-year-old served his time at Man Utd before revisiting Helsingborg and retiring in 2009.

The former Celtic striker later returned to Barca as part of Ronald Koeman’s coaching team in 2020 – but left in October 2021.

Samuel Eto’o collected the treble with Barca in 2009 before leaving for Inter Milan – only to do it all again the next season.

The 45-year-old, who played at Chelsea, Everton, and Qatar SC before retiring in 2019, is now at the head of Cameroon‘s football federation.

In 2021, he was first elected president before winning another four-year term last November – winning 97.7 per cent of the total 87 votes.

Sports.title: United States GP: UK schedule as F1 returns to COTA
Sports.content:
Following an extended stint across Asia, Formula 1 heads to America for the United States Grand Prix at the iconic Circuit of The Americas in Austin, Texas.

After the previous triple-header saw Kimi Antonelli move closer to a maiden F1 title, the Mercedes driver enters three more back-to-back races knowing he has every chance of sealing a historic triumph.

The Italian is 102 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell at the top of the standings, with the first two victories of the year for Red Bull and Max Verstappen only having helped Antonelli move clear of the pack, leaving him with a small chance of being crowned champion in Austin.

While both Antonelli and Mercedes are in remarkably strong positions in the championships, the competitive picture has rarely been more exciting during the 2026 season, with each of the top four teams entering each weekend with genuine hopes of victory.

Many eyes will be on Antonelli, but Verstappen's quest to complete a hat-trick of wins, along with Lewis Hamilton's attempts to bounce back from a tough Sunday in Singapore promise to provide plenty of entertainment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore.

United States GP track - Circuit of the Americas

Of the newer permanent circuits to have joined the calendar over the past couple of decades, the Circuit of the Americas is certainly one of the very best.

The undulating 3.4-mile, 20-corner layout built on the outskirts of Austin quickly proved a hit with drivers when it made its debut in 2021 as F1's first made-to-measure home in the USA.

There was also a sense of familiarity given its track design took inspiration from some of Europe's most famous tracks.

An Esses section reminiscent of Silverstone's legendary high-speed Maggotts and Becketts complex at Silverstone makes up Turns Three to Six, while a reverse triple-apex challenge in the style of Istanbul Park's Turn Eight and a Hockenheim-style arena section all feature in the exciting anti-clockwise lap.

The circuit even has its own signature feature in the form of a steep uphill run to the first corner, which has been the scene of numerous overtakes and controversial incidents over the past 13 years when drivers go wheel-to-wheel into the wide braking zone before powering back downhill towards the Esses.

United States GP weather in Austin

Temperatures are expected to climb above 30 degrees Celsius on all three days of track action, but the wild card is whether rain is going to play apart.

The latest forecast suggests there's a 50 per cent chance of rain falling during the race, with showers also possible on Friday and Saturday.

Sports.title: The All Blacks' Haka explained - plus rugby's other rituals
Sports.content:
One of the most intriguing and anticipated moments in the sport of rugby union: the sight of New Zealand's All Blacks performing their world-famous haka as the opposition stands before them.

But how much do you know about the haka? And also of the three other ceremonial war dances which take place in rugby: the Cibi, Siva Tau and Sipi Tau.

Find out everything you need to know below...

History of the haka in sport - When did it start? What does it mean?

An ancient traditional Māori practice, there is no single recorded date for the haka's first-ever performance owing to this very reason. It has been practised by indigenous Māori communities for centuries.

The earliest point at which Europeans witnessed the haka was the 18th century: Joseph Banks and James Cook on their first voyage to New Zealand in 1769 recorded the haka as "vigorous and ferocious".

In terms of its introduction into sport, New Zealand's first rugby union side visited Australia in Sydney in 1884 and performed the haka. During 1888/89, a 'New Zealand native team' toured the UK for the first time, performing the haka on October 3 1888 against Surrey in a tour match.

The year 1905 saw the birth of the 'All Blacks' as they toured Britain with a team which came to be known as 'The Originals.'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The All Blacks perform a spine-chilling haka at Ellis Park ahead of the opening Test against South Africa in the four-match Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series

The All Blacks performed their famous "Ka Mate" haka before Tests against Scotland and Wales, with it having been composed in 1820 by Māori chief Te Rauparaha.

Yet, the tradition of the All Blacks performing the haka on home soil and before every Test they played did not become custom until 1986.

Ahead of rugby's first World Cup in 1987, All Black Buck Shelford set about reforming the haka in order for pre-match performances to be organised, in sync and executed properly.

"If we're going to do it, we're going to do it right. Either perform the haka properly or not at all. Vote on it and decide which way you want to go," Shelford is said to have told team-mates at the time.

Shelford and team-mate Hika Reid subsequently taught and trained the All Blacks squad correct pronunciation of words and actions, and of the haka's importance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New Zealand captain Codie Taylor leads a spine-tingling haka for the first time against South Africa

At the 1987 World Cup in New Zealand, with Shelford now captain, the All Blacks performed the haka in New Zealand for the very first time, en route to the All Blacks clinching the trophy.

In terms of what the haka means, "Ka Mate" is the recitation of a traditional Māori poem about life, death and resilience.

The more common haka performed by the All Blacks today is the 'Kapa o Pango', first performed in August 2005 before a Tri-Nations Test against South Africa in Dunedin.

The haka featured an extended and aggressive introduction by team captain Tana Umaga, highlighted by a drawing of the thumb down the throat.

Famous haka responses - how should teams respond?

There have been a number of famous haka responses from opposition sides over the years.

In 1996, Australia famously (or infamously?) decided to totally ignore the haka altogether in Wellington, turning their backs on the All Blacks, following on from Wallabies great David Campese choosing to ignore the haka and do kicking drills ahead of the 1991 Rugby World Cup semi-final between the sides, which Australia won.

In 2019, England adopted a V-shaped formation in Yokohama ahead of their World Cup semi-final against the All Blacks. Once the haka started, English players progressed beyond the halfway line and held their ground as officials tried to move them.

Image: Facing the haka ahead of their 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final in Japan, England stepped forward in a V-shaped formation

Image: England captain Owen Farrell smirked as the All Blacks performed the haka in Yokohama

England were later fined £2000 by World Rugby for breaching World Cup 2019 rules relating to cultural challenges, which stated no players from the team receiving the challenge may advance beyond the halfway line. England won the match 19-7 after a sensational performance.

World Rugby rules on haka responses World Rugby rules limit how close opposing teams can get to each other when facing the haka, a Maori war dance, and prevent them from crossing the halfway line. If both teams plan to perform a cultural challenge, a coin toss determines field positions. The winner can move up to the halfway line, while the other team must stay behind their own 10-metre line. If only one team is performing a challenge, the other team can't cross the halfway line, and the performing team can't cross their own 10-metre line. Teams that breach these rules can be fined. For example, in 2019 England were fined £2,000 for crossing the halfway line while facing New Zealand's haka in the Rugby World Cup semi-final. In 2011, France were fined £2,500 for advancing on New Zealand while they performed the haka before the World Cup final.

At the 2007 World Cup, France faced the All Blacks in a World Cup quarter-final in Cardiff, and memorably walked up in a line of opposition to the All Blacks, coming within a metre of the haka. France won the match 20-18.

France also marched forward in an arrow-formation facing the haka ahead of the 2011 Rugby World Cup final in New Zealand, before controversially losing 8-7 at Eden Park.

Image: France and New Zealand came within a metre of one another in a haka response before their 2007 World Cup quarter-final

Image: France also marched forward in an arrow-formation facing the haka ahead of the 2011 Rugby World Cup final

In 2005, the All Blacks agreed to a request from the Welsh Rugby Union to repeat the sequence of events from the original match a century before in 1905, which involved the haka taking place after the New Zealand national anthem but before the Welsh one.

A year later in 2006, Wales demanded a repeat of the sequence, which the All Blacks refused, ultimately performing the haka in the dressing rooms and not in front of the watching fans. Then All Blacks captain Richie McCaw defended the decision by stating the haka was "integral to New Zealand culture and the All Blacks' heritage" and "if the other team wants to mess around, we'll just do the haka in the shed."

Two years later in 2008, another memorable Wales vs New Zealand haka situation unfolded, as following the conclusion of the haka in Cardiff, Wales refused to break and move until the All Blacks did. Neither side did for nearly a minute-and-a-half despite urging from referee Jonathan Kaplan, until McCaw instructed the All Blacks to break off. Wales led 9-6 at half-time but were eventually well beaten 29-9.

Image: Wales and New Zealand held their ground for over 80 seconds following the conclusion of the haka in 2008

Image: Referee Jonathan Kaplan attempted to make both sides move in Cardiff in 2008, but failed

In 2016, Ireland faced the All Blacks in Chicago seeking a first-ever win over New Zealand in 111 years. Just weeks prior, Munster coach Anthony Foley had died in his sleep in Paris at the age of 42 ahead of a European Cup contest against Racing 92.

Facing the haka, Ireland lined up in a figure of eight in memory of Foley, a former Ireland and Munster No 8 in his playing days. Ireland went on to clinch a stunning 40-29 maiden win over the All Blacks.

Before their 2023 Rugby World Cup quarter-final, Ireland repeated the same haka response, but lost to the All Blacks in Paris 28-24.

Image: Ireland lined up in a figure of eight to face the haka in memory of the late Anthony Foley ahead of victory in 2016 and defeat in 2023

In 2008, a uniquely stirring haka response took place at Thomond Park in Limerick as Munster quartet Doug Howlett, Rua Tipoki, Lifeimi Mafi and Jeremy Manning stepped forward to perform a haka facing the All Blacks with the rest of their Munster team-mates stood behind them.

Image: Munster's Rua Tipoki (left), Doug Howlett (centre) and Lifeimi Mafi (right) stepped forward to perform a memorable haka against the All Blacks at Thomond Park in 2008

A similar event took place recently in 2026 when All Blacks great Ma'a Nonu performed a solo haka facing the All Blacks while a player for South African club side the Sharks, ahead of New Zealand's tour match in Durban.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ma'a Nonu gave his former All Blacks team-mates the ultimate show of respect by responding to their haka with one of his own

Are New Zealand only nation that perform the haka?

While the haka is rugby's best-known and most famous traditional pre-match ceremonial war dance, the island nations of Fiji, Samoa and Tonga all also perform their own versions.

Fiji perform the Cibi, which sees the team stand in formation and led by a vocal soloist, before dropping into a synchronised low crouch or knee-bend while making aggressive arm and hand gestures, concluding with an explosive jump or step-up.

Image: Fiji perform the Cibi during an Autumn Nations Series 2025 Test against Scotland at Murrayfield

Image: Australia watch on as Fiji perform the Cibi at the 2023 Rugby World Cup

Samoa perform the Siva Tau, with the ritual led by a designated chanter and players starting in a lowered or kneeling stance before rising into synchronised movements that include chest-slapping, foot-stomping, aggressive gestures, and intense vocal chanting.

Image: Samoa's players perform the Siva Tau at the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France

Tonga perform the Sipi Tau, which begins with the team huddled or kneeling in a circle led by a central caller, before breaking into a structured formation on the field featuring deep squats, chest-pounding, rhythmic foot-stomping, and aggressive synchronised gestures.

Sports.title: Lions forward Andrews dies suddenly ahead of match in France
Sports.content:
Hyron Andrews died suddenly in France at the age of 31; the Lions say their Champions Cup game on Saturday against La Rochelle will go ahead in honour of the forward; Andrews previously played for English club Sale Sharks

Lions player Hyron Andrews has died suddenly in France, where the team were preparing for a Champions Cup fixture.

A statement from SA rugby said that Andrews "passed away tragically, following an accident" and that he had "died after falling" at the team hotel.

Following French media reports that a Lions player had passed away, the Lions released a separate statement in the afternoon that named Andrews.

The 31-year-old South African second-row forward had spent the previous two years of his career playing for Sale Sharks in England before returning home this summer to join the Lions.

The Lions said Saturday's match against La Rochelle will go ahead "in honour of Hyron".

"Our deepest and most heartfelt condolences go to Hyron's wife, Maiglin, their young sons, and the entire Andrews family. We hold them in our thoughts during this time of unimaginable grief and ask that their privacy be respected as they mourn."

The Lions said that "an appropriate tribute" would be planned for a later date.

Sports.title: 'I'm telling you the truth' - Carrick insists Martinez situation resolved
Sports.content:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick insists he is telling the truth when he says the club have moved on from Lisandro Martinez's post-match outburst earlier this week.

In a press conference dominated by questions about Martinez, Carrick revealed that the defender would be included in Sunday's squad for the trip to Leeds United despite him calling out director of football Jason Wilcox over a lack of investment in the transfer window.

Martinez, whose outspoken comments came after Tuesday's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox. CEO Omar Berrada and Carrick, on Thursday before making an apology over the timing and public nature of his criticism.

Asked about Martinez on Friday ahead of Sunday's trip to Leeds, live on Sky Sports, Carrick said: "He's released his statement and realised he made a mistake.

"That's enough for us to move on with. From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what's been done is enough to move on."

'I'm telling you the truth' - Carrick insists case closed

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.

United's record goalscorer Wayne Rooney, who was Carrick's teammate at Old Trafford for more than a decade, said Martinez's comments had the potential to "rip the dressing room apart".

But Carrick, who is under mounting pressure with United on a five-game winless run, was adamant that the spirit of the group remains strong ahead of two tough away games against Leeds and Como.

Questioned why people would believe that with everything that has been said, Carrick added: "There's a lot of people saying a lot of things. Pros and ex-pros, that doesn't mean they know what's going on here.

"The players totally believe me. Just because people talk on the outside doesn't make it the truth. I am telling you the truth.

"The squad [on Friday] was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while, actually. It's plain and simple. It's not affected [the spirit], I'm telling you. We're in a good place."

He added: "As a group we've moved on. It's really not a drama for the group. The squad have trained really well and they are in good spirits.

"It was pretty simple. We understood the situation. Licha understood he made a mistake. We have a really good feeling from the club. We can see in the group we want to do something with this situation.

"We've moved on. Genuinely. There is a freshness about the group."

Should Wilcox speak more often in public?

Martinez directly called out United's "technical director" in his post-match interview in Madrid, putting director of football Wilcox firmly in the top spotlight.

Since replacing Dan Ashworth to assume his current role, Wilcox has only done one extended interview, which came nearly a year ago after a run of three wins, and it was with the club's in-house media.

Asked if Wilcox, who has been criticised by fans for his lack of communication, should speak up more, Carrick said: "I don't think it's for me to say whether he should or not.

"I've got no problem sitting here, talking to you guys and leading the group, leading the team, leading the football club from this position. We're all in it together."

Analysis: Carrick handled situation well – but talking needs to be on the pitch

Sky Sports' Pete Gill:

"As a player, Michael Carrick was unflustered and calm. In Friday's press conference, he has been no different.

"He offered a straight bat to the inevitable questions about Martinez and only seem ruffled when it was suggested that he needed a result against Leeds - "we need a result" interjected the United head coach.

"Ultimately, though, United's talking needs to be on the pitch. And if there was one jarring note in the presser, it was Carrick's insistence that all is well at United that stood out.

"United are not, in his words, "in a good place". They can only be if they arrest their alarming slump in form, starting at Leeds on Sunday."

'Doubts over Martinez future'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Dave Reed updates fans on which Manchester United players will be out of contract in the summer.

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

Manchester United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Sky Sports News has been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Sports.title: 'One of the best weeks of my life' - Kartal feeling fresh ahead of Wuhan semi-finals
Sports.content:
British star Sonay Kartal says she is due a couple of new tattoos after enjoying "one of the best weeks" of her life by reaching the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open.

Kartal claimed one of the biggest wins of the career as she beat world No 6 Elina Svitolina on Friday.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, seized her first match-point opportunity to complete another stunning victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open quarter-final between Sonay Kartal and Elina Svitolina

Kartal, who made her breakthrough by reaching the fourth round of last year's Wimbledon, advanced to the last four of a WTA 1000 event for the first time.

"Definitely one of the best weeks of my life," she said. "You could say, results-wise, that is definitely the best for me so far.

"I'm very happy to be backing up the level each day. I think it's pretty easy for a player to come out and play a blinder for just one match. I'm very happy that I managed to keep the consistency. I've got some of my best wins this week."

Kartal added she is due a couple of new tattoos. She had one booked in but was forced to make a last-minute cancellation after heading to the Billie Jean King Cup with Great Britain.

Asked if she would get one done if she won in Wuhan, the Brighton-based star replied with a smile: "I would have to have a think. I can't make a rush decision."

Back injury and protected ranking

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the match between Kartal and Jasmine Paolini

Kartal, using a protected injury ranking to play, has previously peaked at No 44 in the rankings and started the Wuhan Open at No 170, but she has skyrocketed 83 places to No 87 in the live rankings with her run to the semi-finals.

She is assured of adding 390 points to her total, meaning she is guaranteed to be the new British No 2 behind Katie Boulter (No 58), moving past Fran Jones (No 98) and Emma Raducanu (No 109).

Having missed more than six months, Kartal admitted she would not be able to walk without some form of pain but found it "pretty smooth sailing" after a couple of months.

And now she is feeling fit and healthy again.

What is a protected ranking?

A protected ranking is a provision that allows tennis players to enter tournaments using a frozen or averaged ranking after a long-term absence from the sport



A protected ranking can only be used to gain automatic entry into a tournament's main draw or qualifying rounds



On the WTA Tour, it is typically based on their exact ranking at the official start of their absence



The player must be physically sidelined and unable to compete in any tennis event for a minimum of six months



A protected ranking is not permanent. It is only valid for a specific timeframe or a limited number of tournaments



"My back is great," Kartal said. "I wouldn't have made the return if it wasn't great.

"I think the body is feeling it having not played a tennis match for six months, and when you're on tour, your body gets used to the aches and pains and demands of matches each week. I'm definitely more sore in areas.

"I think if there's one thing I've learned in the six months - it's sometimes patience is the better option. And the heroic thing to do is not play every single week. I feel great and I'm ready to get going for the remainder of the year."

The challenge of Ostapenko

She'll next face Latvian world No 34 Jelena Ostapenko, who beat Diana Shnaider in her quarter-final.

The pair have met twice before, with both matches coming on grass in the space of six days in June 2025 - Ostapenko won at Eastbourne, but then Kartal came out on top at Wimbledon.

Image: Jelena Ostapenko faces Kartal for a spot in the Wuhan Open final

"I've enjoyed playing her," said Kartal. "I think we're equal on the scoreboard. But I think there's a level of respect that she shows me.

"She's playing great this week having had a few tough matches, so she's definitely on form. I'm excited for another battle.

"I feel it's going to be a completely different game style to the people that I've played the past few days. I'm ready for a long one if it's needed."

Sports.title: Arteta: Arsenal will take new team photo including Saliba
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta says Arsenal will take a new team photograph including William Saliba after the defender's surprise absence from the one published this week.

Arsenal supporters were left baffled by Saliba's omission from the official 2026/27 picture as the club revealed he was unavailable to attend due to a medical appointment.

Saliba is yet to play this season because of a back injury but the 25-year-old remains a key player, having made 184 appearances for the club, which heightened the intrigue around his omission.

"What happened was that we have tried to do that picture three times already and we had to cancel it last minute for different reasons," explained Arteta ahead of Arsenal's away trip to Nottingham Forest, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

"We had some commercial obligations, we had some people who flew over to do that, so we decided to do that picture.

"We will have another picture with the whole family.

"Hopefully we can get them all together at some point one day, and we'll announce that as well."

Arteta replied "yes" when asked to confirm that Arsenal planned to retake the picture and insisted Saliba was "completely fine" about the situation.

He said: "Well, it wasn't in his hands. But Willy is normally happy about everything. He knows how loved he is. He was taking some banter from the players and he is completely fine."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Predictions for this weekend's games on Sky with Kevin Davies, who makes some bold calls

Saliba resumed training on the grass earlier this month and Arteta added that he is progressing positively, with a scan scheduled for next week as he edges closer to a return to action.

"I think next week we have another MRI with him to see how the healing process is going," he said.

"But every sign so far has been very, very positive. It will be good to have him."

Arteta added that Martin Zubimendi is in contention to return against Forest after injuring himself in the warm-down following the Leeds game along with Piero Hincapie, who will be out for another one or two weeks.

Christos Tzolis, meanwhile, underwent an MRI scan on Thursday to assess his recovery from the hamstring injury he suffered on international duty with Greece.

"It's progressing really well," Arteta added of the winger. "Another one that hopefully we can have back in a few weeks."

Arteta 'far from happy' about photo gaffe

Sky Sports News reporter Gary Cotterill at Arsenal's training ground:

When it comes to facing tricky questions, Mikel Arteta has things easier right now than his counterparts on both sides of Manchester, but it's not all plain sailing at Arsenal.

In a week of warm-down injuries, incomplete team photos and job-cut announcements, the Arsenal manager knew there would be some tricky issues to deal with.

As if that wasn't enough, the off-field issues continued as the tough questions started.

A few minutes into the news conference the microphone under Mikel's mouth stopped working.

It meant his answer underlining that Arsenal are no longer the set piece kings - 20 of their 21 goals so far this season have come from open play - had to be repeated.

Arteta went into detail about how it happened. But is clearly mystified as to why it happened. And, I understand, far from happy about it behind the scenes.

Nevertheless he spoke with good humour and a smile on his face, saying Saliba was fine about what happened.

Sports.title: The Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool?
Sports.content:
Is Wirtz struggling at Liverpool as badly as most outside observers believe?

Some criticism has been OTT and a fee rising to £116m heightens demands but, yes, compared with his performances in Germany and for Germany Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool. The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In the Champions League rout of Lask he was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition. In the previous game against Manchester City, however, when Andoni Iraola needed big players to step up in the absence of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, Wirtz was ineffective, wasteful and withdrawn when his team were chasing the game at 0-1. It also did not help his cause that Rayan Cherki, a cheaper alternative whom Liverpool considered and passed on, completed City’s victory with a sublime goal. AH

What are the main reasons for this?

The physicality and intensity of the Premier League appear to be Wirtz’s biggest issues. He can be swamped, knocked aside, leaving Liverpool’s central midfield exposed. Iraola this week rejected the notion that the playmaker is struggling with English football, although his answer almost veered in support of the argument. “It’s not about whether they are foreign teams or English teams,” the head coach said. “It’s about different kinds of games. Some games are more comfortable, with more time to think, sometimes less. It’s not about the competition.” But, as Brentford are likely to demonstrate on Saturday, there is less time to think and little opportunity to get comfortable in the Premier League. Wirtz produced three assists in 11 Champions League games last season, the same amount as he did in 33 Premier League matches. His passing accuracy this season – from an admittedly small sample – is 80% in the Premier League and 91.5% in the Champions League. AH

Does he have the ‘on-pitch personality’ to succeed at Liverpool?

That is a question that can be levelled at many of Liverpool’s signings since the 2025 title win. The shift towards acquiring expensive “finished products” has left many pining for the hunger and spirit of emerging talent that characterised the club’s re-emergence under Jürgen Klopp. Wirtz does not have an ego to match his price tag. He is a conscientious, dedicated professional who Iraola, like Arne Slot before him, has found to be a good listener willing to put team instructions first. He is also, it seems easy to forget, only 23. Wirtz may not be a demonstrative force but he shows personality on the ball, always looking to receive it and take responsibility. His talent is clear but has not been seen consistently enough in a Liverpool shirt. AH

What needs to happen tactically, and in general, for him to thrive at the club?

Wirtz was sold on Slot’s vision for him as the central, creative force of a new-look Liverpool attack that would turn the slender wins of the title-winning season into dominant, emphatic victories. It never happened, and Slot was sacked without finding a position that best suited Wirtz. Iraola immediately confirmed Wirtz would be his No 10 and got to work on him building a close rapport with Isak. There were some promising signs before Isak got injured again. Wirtz can justifiably argue that forces beyond his control have conspired against him at Liverpool and that, as his relationship with Bradley Barcola and Isak improves, so will his end product. He would also be helped by the addition of an out-and-out defensive midfielder who could offer Wirtz licence to roam and greater protection to the Liverpool defence. Monaco’s Lamine Camara, whose proposed move to Chelsea collapsed on deadline day, is of interest. AH

How good was Wirtz at Bayer Leverkusen?

Unbelievably so. In his final two seasons in the Bundesliga you could make the case that he was the best player in it. He racked up goals and assists in European competition too (he was excellent in the Champions League in 2024-25 before injury halted him in the knockouts) but you can’t just describe it in terms of numbers. He dominated the big matches and acted as the conductor of Leverkusen’s orchestra. Teams who tried to kick him out of games almost universally failed, making the idea he can’t hack the Premier League physically a flawed explanation for his difficulties. AB

How much of his success was down to ‘on-pitch personality’?

Partly it was, but on a technical and tactical level his success was also partly down to the freedom Xabi Alonso allowed him. As Alonso said in November 2023 (during Leverkusen’s unbeaten double-winning season) every player had responsibility to patrol an allotted zone “but Flo is different” – he was given licence to prod opposing defences as he saw fit. Alonso’s rotation of him made sure he remained fresh and impactful, his hat-trick in the 5-0 win over Werder Bremen that clinched the title in 2024 coming after he was brought on as a half-time substitute. AB

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Is the Bundesliga being weaker than the Premier League a factor?

I don’t think we can say that isn’t a factor – but this is something Wirtz himself predicted. Many in his entourage thought he would be better served by joining Bayern Munich instead of Liverpool and he acknowledged he was taking the tougher option. He knew it was a risk but was determined to challenge himself. Another point is how different the Bundesliga is tactically; it has a similarly high tempo but is far more chaotic, which is perfect for a player with his sang froid to exploit. AB

He shone recently for Germany. Is he being used in a notably different way?

He has been given greater freedom (and a little less responsibility off the ball), more akin to his Leverkusen role, but what has been important is having Klopp cheerlead for him. The manager has not missed an opportunity to say how great Wirtz is or how his good international form is “good for Liverpool”. Klopp also gave him the captaincy for the last game (and a half), showing Wirtz and the world that he believes not only in his talent and influence but in him as a leader. It feels like the more contact he has with Klopp, the better for him and his club. AB

Do you have faith in Wirtz being a success at Liverpool?

Wirtz can be a class act, a lovely footballer to watch, and it would be premature to write off a gifted talent who – as the previous answer about Isak and a defensive midfielder suggests – has not had the platform to fully express himself at Liverpool. But the question of whether the Premier League suits him and whether he suits this Liverpool team continues to gnaw away. Wirtz needed a strong start to the season after the difficulties of his debut campaign at Anfield and, with one assist and no goals in six Premier League appearances, that has not materialised. There was encouragement in his overall performance and in his understanding with Barcola against Lask, as there has been on several Champions League nights, but Iraola needs his playmaker to produce a repeat in games such as Brentford away. Wirtz will remain categorised as a luxury player if another difficult Premier League assignment passes him by. AH

Maybe. The deck has been largely stacked against him since he arrived: there were too many changes to a champion team in the summer he arrived, plus he was expected to pull the strings in a side that still had Mohamed Salah. He has overcome big setbacks before, such as the 2022 anterior cruciate ligament injury that took a long while to get over, so he has the character to go with his class. Wirtz has the ability to succeed at Anfield but unless the conditions around him change I think it will be very hard to do so (I can imagine him being great for Bayern in a couple of years, post-Michael Olise). AB

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta defends job cuts at Arsenal to help club ‘evolve and create success’
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal’s decision to cut up to 60 jobs and insisted it was felt to be necessary to ensure they can continue achieving success.

The Premier League champions are understood to have informed the staff whose positions are at risk after a consultation process started by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) before the end of last season. Arsenal hope the number of redundancies can be reduced and will attempt to redeploy affected employees wherever possible, although some job losses may be unavoidable.

It is understood the catering and travel departments are among the affected, and that the men’s and women’s first-team performance and coaching staff will not be impacted. The academy, Arsenal Women, Arsenal in the Community, the Arsenal Foundation and site security teams are also exempt, although other areas of the wider football operation are included in the review, which was overseen internally by the managing director, Richard Garlick.

The timing of the proposed cuts has attracted scrutiny after last week’s announcement of Arteta’s new contract, worth more than £20m a season. Arsenal say the restructuring process began before the deal was announced and the manager said he was not the appropriate person to answer questions about the redundancies.

“It was explained to me about the exercise, and the analysis that has been done across the club, and with the intention always to evolve to improve,” he said. “Some decisions have to be taken, to put people in the right roles, and keep investing to achieve what we want to achieve on the success that we want to create. So that has been explained. Obviously I am not the right person to answer that question. That’s for sure. And hopefully everybody will respect that.”

The club refused to allow Arteta to answer any more questions on the subject. Arsenal’s most recent financial accounts, for the 2024-25 campaign, show that operating costs rose from £148m the previous year to £201m, with the owner, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, keen to cut costs despite winning the Premier League title in May.

Arteta was instrumental in reshaping Arsenal’s medical department over the summer, when the former Aston Villa team doctor Arnaldo Abrantes arrived, and is believed to have bolstered his backroom staff in other areas.

Arsenal travel to Nottingham Forest on Sunday – the first of four away games in their next five matches – and Kai Havertz is again expected to start ahead of Viktor Gyökeres. The Sweden striker has yet to find the net for Arsenal this season and struggled against Lille in midweek after scoring four goals on international duty.

“These are moments in a player’s career, or in a season, I would say,” Arteta said. “And we are trying to help him as much as possible. The other day, I think he had some very good moments. He’s three or four times in front of goal with no keeper and the ball should arrive to him and it doesn’t. But these are the strikers. It’s very small margins. Scoring or not scoring changes the narrative, for sure, not the perception of how much he can help the team.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
Sports.content:
‘I’M STILL STANDING …’

There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house.

Having already made four managerial appointments in 2026 and 28 since the Pozzo family purchased the club in the summer of 2012, the owners have shown uncharacteristic restraint despite Watford winning just three of the last 21 Championship games (even Oxford United have more victories in the division during that time despite being relegated to League One in April). Pressure on Dionisi has now increased after John – which feels like an inappropriately underwhelming way to refer to one of the most talented and flamboyant pop singers of all time – admitted he was “upset” at the club’s form in a now-deleted post on a Social Media Disgrace on Sunday.

“As a lifetime supporter of Watford FC, I am very upset and disappointed at the decline over the past few weeks – I really feel for the supporters who have to watch this,” Elton crooned after the 4-0 home defeat to Burnley. “I’ve called the chauffeur, you little chancer”, he didn’t add. Things worsened for Dionisi on Tuesday with struggling Cardiff romping to a 5-1 win to leave the Hornets in the Championship relegation zone, with some reporting – incorrectly, as it turned out – the Italian had been sacked during the game. But despite the unconfirmed reports of his demise, Dionisi remains very much in post.

“There is good news, bad news or fake news probably. In this case for the moment, it is fake news [that I have been sacked] but I don’t decide,” he told the BBC on Friday, not wholly convincingly. “For Elton John, I am sorry because I don’t know him. But football is wonderful because everyone speaks [their mind]. I have been a coach for 14 years, and it is normal. In my past there was negative and there was positive moments. At the moment it is a negative moment. Inside the training ground there is only one mentality, only one street for everyone.” Absolute goosebumps, Alessio. Cheers for that. We know not of the cryptic road you speak – Vicarage? Yellow Brick? The road to nowhere? – but we’ll have to see if Dionisi becomes the latest Watford manager to find himself out on the street, kicked to the curb through a front door marked ‘Do One’, following Saturday’s visit of Charlton Athletic.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I think I have an angel on my shoulder. I’m actually fortunate to be alive at all. I was 20 and playing for Dortmund when three pipe bombs went off right next to our bus on the way to a Champions League match. A lot of young people probably would not even believe that it happened, or how bad it was, but it marked us all. There was a deafening noise, and then I remember the bus nearly tipping over. I looked behind me and saw blood on the floor. Smoke, screams. I remember being at the hospital later that night, waiting for Marc Bartra, who had his wrist badly cut up. The next day, someone told me that a huge piece of shrapnel was lodged in the headrest of the seat next to Marc. My usual seat. That day, the seat was empty. My legs were feeling a bit tight, and the seats in the front reclined. So I sat up there instead, and it may have saved my life” – Mikel Merino recalls how a last-minute change of seats on the Borussia Dortmund coach that was hit by explosives on its way to the home leg of their Champions League semi-final against Monaco in 2017 may have saved his life in a wider interview with the Player Tribune.

Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid.
