Sports.title: Carrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director Wilcox
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick brushed off Lisandro Martínez’s failure to offer Jason Wilcox a public apology after the defender criticised Manchester United’s director of football in the wake of Tuesday’s defeat at Atlético Madrid.

Martínez referred directly to Wilcox after the 2-0 Champions League loss, saying: “I expect more from our technical director.”

On Thursday Martínez issued an apology that did not mention Wilcox or withdraw the essence of his outburst: the need for more squad investment. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise,” he said.

Carrick was asked whether he respected Martínez for not saying sorry to Wilcox. “He’s released his statement, he’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough for all of us to move on with,” United’s manager said.

Carrick was pressed on whether it would have been better if Martínez had apologised to Wilcox and for his wider comments about investment, rather than just saying sorry for the timing and location of his interview. “From our point of view, the acknowledgment of what’s been done has certainly been enough, we’ve moved on and we’re definitely not looking back at it now,” he replied.

Carrick said Martínez was available for Sunday’s trip to Leeds, where Manchester United go having taken only six points from their opening six league games. They were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton last month and have one win and a defeat in the Champions League. Poor form has increased the pressure on Carrick, who was asked whether Martínez’s comments were an unwanted distraction that had annoyed him.

“No, I understand emotion at times,” he said. “We ask for passion, we ask for emotion, we ask for fire and we ask for players to care. There’s a way of doing that, and that’s already been acknowledged, but we need to carry that intensity and that willingness and that togetherness and that spirit. As a group, we need to use it, and we’ve got to use it in the right way.”

Wayne Rooney, United’s record goalscorer, claimed Martínez’s comments “will rip the dressing room apart”. It was put to Carrick that they may have an opposite, unifying effect.

“There’s a lot of things that can affect the group in all sorts of different ways,” said Carrick, who went on to highlight his players’ reaction to conceding inside a minute at Atlético. “It’s one of the toughest places to play in the Champions League, so to go a goal down so early, and the way we responded shows an underlying belief and spirit and a togetherness,” he said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He indicated that events on and off the pitch this week had brought the squad together. “Certain situations can galvanise the group, and it’s certainly galvanised the group as this week’s progressed. The boys are in a really good place right now.”

Carrick was asked why anyone outside the club, including former players such as Rooney who have criticised Martínez, should believe there is unity. “There’s a lot of people that say a lot of things, and ex-pros or not ex-pros, it doesn’t necessarily mean you understand what’s going on here,” he said. “I’m telling you the truth. The squad today [Friday] was in a fantastic place, better than I’ve seen it for a while.”

Carrick said Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo faced fitness tests.

Sports.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga president resign over Goebbels comparison
Sports.content:
Real Madrid have again demanded the resignation of the president of La Liga after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees with the propaganda techniques of Nazi Germany.

Javier Tebas lashed out at Madrid on Friday on social media with a long post that criticised how its club television channel says referees hurt its chances of winning. The channel regularly runs reels of what it considers gross errors by match officials who are set to work upcoming games for the 15-time European champions.

Tebas compared the tactic with those used by Joseph Goebbels, the minister of propaganda in Nazi Germany during the second world war.

“The executive of Real Madrid has an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid leads the way,” Tebas wrote. “Its script is always the same: select plays that favor it, repeat the alleged affront, increase suspicion and name enemies. It reminds one of the propaganda techniques that Goebbels used.”

Tebas added: “The comparison is with the techniques, not with the ideology or, of course, with Madrid fans.”

Madrid responded by saying in a statement that Tebas, who has clashed several times over the years with the club president, Florentino Pérez, was unfit to hold his job representing Spain’s top clubs. Madrid also demanded his “immediate resignation”.

“Javier Tebas’s repeated conduct demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect, and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities,” it said. “His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those demanding transparency and regeneration represent, in our club’s view, a genuine scourge for Spanish football.”

The head coach, José Mourinho, has also voiced complaints that Madrid, who hold a record 36 Spanish league titles, are regularly hurt by referees.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho watches Real Madrid in action. Photograph: Ivan Romano/Getty Images

In September, Madrid demanded Tebas step down after he criticised the club for attacking the refereeing team in the 2-1 loss at Atlético Madrid.

In Friday’s statement, Madrid repeated the complaint that Tebas has not done enough over the ongoing judicial probe into Barcelona’s alleged payments to an official on the refereeing committee of the Spanish soccer federation.

Meanwhile, Spain’s football federation will take its ⁠case to the court of arbitration for sport after Fifa rejected its appeal against sanctions imposed over Islamophobic chants by supporters during a match against Egypt ⁠in March.

Fifa fined the ⁠federation $20,000 (£15,000) and ordered ​it to close at least 15% of the available seats for Spain’s next home friendly. The sanctions relate to incidents at the RCDE Stadium near Barcelona, home ⁠of La Liga club Espanyol, where some Spain fans chanted, “If you don’t jump, you’re a Muslim” during a World Cup warm-up match that ended in a 0-0 draw.

The RFEF argued that the word Muslim was “neither insulting nor pejorative”, adding the fans’ conduct should be assessed under Fifa’s article 17, which covers political, ideological, religious or offensive messages, rather than article 15, which deals with discrimination and racist abuse.

However, Fifa’s disciplinary committee rejected that argument, saying article 15 does not require the explicit use of a ‌slur and that a term can be discriminatory when used in context as “an insult, taunt or marker of inferiority”.

Sports.title: The WSL so far: goal-shy Arsenal, underrated Brighton and more data pointers
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League table is taking shape for 2026-27. The defending champions, Manchester City, have five wins from five games but more intriguing stories lie elsewhere. Why are Arsenal struggling, who is performing better than results suggest, and in which way are two promoted teams smashing expectations? Here are three key data points.

Arsenal have two major flaws

Opta made Arsenal third favourites to win the WSL before a ball was kicked. Their win at Brighton combined with Chelsea’s draw against Aston Villa in week one meant Renée Slegers’ side rose to narrow favourites. The four games since, from which Arsenal took two points, have torpedoed their title chances.

One reason for their slump is a continuation of a problem from last season. The stats section of our Arsenal pre-season preview highlighted draws in 2025-26 that they deserved to win based on expected goals. That trend has continued this season with positive xG margins of 2.2 and 1.2 in their home games against Crystal Palace (0-0) and Manchester United (1-1) respectively.

Had Smilla Holmberg not scored with her only shot of the campaign in the 95th minute against United, the situation would be even worse. While players inevitably have a small sample of shots at this point, Arsenal’s finishing woes are a collective problem. Only Lisa Baum and Alessia Russo have also scored, with the latter 1.28 goals below her expected goal tally. Scoring three goals in the international break may help Russo’s confidence.

A physical deficiency may also be contributing to Arsenal’s struggles. Gradient Sports award players an athleticism score, a single metric which incorporates stamina, explosiveness and game context. There are 125 WSL players with a score who have played at least 270 minutes this season. Steph Catley is Arsenal’s highest-ranked player, at 31st, and their only representative above 59th. Every other club has at least two players in the top 50, with Chelsea having five. West Ham possessing seven shows this is not a decisive factor in success but Arsenal fans may wonder whether their side need to increase the physical intensity.

Brighton are ones to watch

Brighton were predicted by Opta to finish seventh. As they are ninth, that forecast looks reasonable enough. Yet the underlying data suggests they deserve to be third, 0.1 expected points behind City. The Seagulls endured a case of wastefulness more extreme than anything Arsenal have offered up when they drew 1-1 with Villa. Despite an expected goal count of 3.17 to 0.03 in Brighton’s favour, Lynn Wilms’s 89th-minute goal robbed them of a victory.

Brighton also drew at Birmingham when leading the expected goals by 1.5 and missed four Opta-defined big chances in their 2-0 defeat at London City Lionesses. If they can make their dominance count, Brighton look capable of at least matching the fifth-place finish they secured in 2024-25.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Two promoted teams have an unexpected weapon

Productive pressing tends to belong to better teams. Opta’s high turnover metric records when a team win the ball to begin a new sequence of open-play possession within 40m of the opposition goal. If you sort the 2025-26 WSL by the number of high turnovers that led to shots, the five clubs with the fewest were those that finished in the bottom five. The standings were slightly more jumbled if you looked at the percentage of high turnovers that generated shots, to assess effectiveness and efficiency, but the top four teams for this finished in the WSL top five. Promoted London City had the fourth-least productive press by this measure.

Two of their successors are upending these correlations. Palace are third for shot-ending high turnovers, with 12, behind Chelsea (17) and Tottenham (15). The percentage of their possession regains in the final 40m that led to shots is the highest in the division (33.3%), with their fellow promoted side Birmingham (28.6%) next in line.

The West Midlands club are tied with Tottenham for most goals from high turnovers, on three (while Palace have two). Birmingham’s goals were all scored by Océane Hurtré, helping propel her to joint-first in the golden boot race, with five goals.

The 22-year-old French attacker won the ball for two of the three high-turnover goals, including one at Manchester City. Hurtré’s others came in the first and eighth minutes of matches against Palace and Brighton respectively, illustrating the benefit that pressing opponents early can bring.

Sports.title: Premier League news: go bananas: Maresca loving fans’ show of defiance; James injury blow for Blues
Sports.content:
1. City manager says 'we need to make our noise’ Enzo Maresca has called on Manchester City fans to bring inflatable bananas to help inspire the team in their first Premier League home game since being found guilty of financial breaches when they take on Ipswich on Saturday. Supporters packed the away end at Liverpool with the novelty items as a nod to the club’s history last weekend. Blow-up bananas became popular among City fans in the 1980s and 1990s when they spent time in the second and third tiers, and have been revived in reaction to the threat of being sanctioned with relegation and to show there is plenty to reflect on before the 2008 takeover. “Very nice,” Maresca said of the inflatables. “I didn’t know the history behind the banana. I hope tomorrow I can see many bananas in the stadium. I think it creates a nice environment for the fans and for everyone that is in the stadium. I have four kids, they already asked me [for bananas], but tomorrow they’re going to be at the stadium and we’ll see.” It comes after Maresca dropped points for the first time as City manager, losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. City are three points clear of second-placed Arsenal at the top of the Premier League and victory would make Maresca the first manager to win their first seven Premier League games with a club. City are playing against a backdrop of being the focus of anger around the country. “We need to try to make our noise,” Maresca said. “And to make our noise means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow. And this is the way we can make our noise. The different kind of noise, we are not able to control that. I think Rúben [Dias] said that people don’t like the City win. But we like to win. So I think that is a good message for everyone. Probably since the noise, we can see, I can see from my personal point of view, the fans, the club, the team, more together for sure. But we’ll see.” Will Unwin

2. James could be sidelined until after Christmas Xabi Alonso said Reece James will not be hurried back from injury following knee surgery, with Chelsea set to be without their captain possibly until the new year. The 26-year-old was injured in training before last weekend’s 5-1 win at home to Bournemouth and has undergone successful surgery, described by the club as a “minor” operation. James played 29 times in the Premier League last season, the most appearances he had made in a league campaign since 2020-21, having previously sustained a succession of injuries. “We’re all disappointed for him,” said Alonso. “He wanted to have a good start after the international break, but in the last training he picked up an injury. We wanted to be cautious and to wait for the results of the tests, but now the surgery has been successful. We’ll keep supporting him. He’s a great influence even when he’s not available. We wish him the best recovery. “It’s not going to be short, it’s not going to be two or three weeks, it’s going to be longer. We’ll see before Christmas, after Christmas. Time will tell. Things have to be done properly.” View image in fullscreen Reece James has had surgery on a knee injury picked up in training before last weekend’s 5-1 win against Bournemouth. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters James was not one of the five players to withdraw from England duty during the break, though he does now look set to miss the next international window when England will face Croatia at Wembley and an away game against Spain. Moises Caicedo made his first start of the season against Bournemouth and made an immediate impact in helping the team to control the game, something that the side had struggled with during Alonso’s first few matches. Jordan Henderson started alongside Caicedo and scored his first two Blues goals, while Romeo Lavia, another player to have suffered badly with fitness since joining Chelsea, has made an injury-free start to the season. “I think we’ll be able to manage well with the players we have, the ones who have been playing and who are available,” said Alonso. “Reece is still a very important player. He’s the captain, a great influence. He has a good mentality and we need him.” Press Association

3. Lampard will keep driving Coventry revival Frank Lampard is not prepared to relax after watching his Coventry side record back-to-back wins in the Premier League. The Sky Blues looked to be in for a long season after losing their opening four games without scoring a goal on their return to the top tier, but they have kickstarted their campaign with wins against Nottingham Forest and Newcastle and Lampard wants to keep the foot on the gas. “Keep driving it,” he said. “It’s very important to look at the good things out of the game, also the things we can improve. But when we talk about the good things, I’m not overly patting them on the back because we have to work hard to get better. “Every game brings different challenges, so I think the players understand me and my approach and the staff’s approach here. We never want to rest. I don’t. I’m always fearful of resting on something and thinking that you’ve made it. This league’s too difficult for that. “So one of my first jobs is to keep pushing from that front, and the players need to feel that.” Press Association

4. Iraola has faith in teenager Nyoni Andoni Iraola, the Liverpool head coach, has every faith in Trey Nyoni as the 19-year-old looks set for his first Premier League start. The teenager put in a composed display in the 6-3 Champions League win over LASK in midweek, and with Ryan Gravenberch suspended and Dominik Szoboszlai still struggling with a hamstring injury, it is likely he will line up alongside Alexis Mac Allister at Brentford. Nyoni has made 26 appearances since his debut in February 2024, 10 of which have been as a substitute in the top flight, but after playing 85 minutes on his first Champions League start in the midweek win, Iraola has no doubts about the youngster’s quality. “Trey is a player that is very young with not a lot of minutes in the first team, but is very mature, he understands the situation very well, he understands the game very well and tactically he is very smart,” Iraola said. “But he has to continue doing the steps in the right direction, I am confident with him. “He has been involved in most of the last games but he has to keep this level of performance, of training, he has to play as a six, as an eight, he has to start and play a game like LASK, putting pressure on the other midfielders. It is very good for us that we can put in these young players with not a lot of experience and they can perform in a competition like the Champions League or the Premier League.” View image in fullscreen Trey Nyoni is likely to make his full Premier League debut for Liverpool at Brentford. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA Liverpool are in a run of six games in 18 days and Iraola knows he will have to call on Nyoni regularly. “In this period, especially, where we are basically playing every three days, less than three days, you need more players,” he said. “That’s why we changed the team [in midweek] and we need to change again at the weekend and change again when we face Villarreal in another three days. “We will need everyone in one moment or another, everyone has to be ready because we will need him probably. But this is the challenge of playing, no? It’s competitions like the Champions League and it’s not going to just happen this week, it is going to be a constant thing this season so we have to adapt.” Press Association

Sports.title: Álvaro Arbeloa’s push to make Fulham free-flowing is floundering already
Sports.content:
Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions.

Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices.

The worrying shift under Arbeloa was evident during Fulham’s collapse against Ipswich last weekend. The west Londoners were 1-0 up and looking good for their first league win of the season when Arbeloa weakened his midfield by replacing Shea Charles with Manuel Ángel in the 70th minute.

It was a strange way to shut up shop. Charles is physically imposing, has impressed since joining from Southampton and was doing well alongside Sander Berge. The 22-year-old Ángel is 5ft 7in, was making his Premier League debut and has little experience of senior football. Ipswich’s comeback to win 2-1 was not a surprise, particularly when Arbeloa’s other rejigs included bringing on Rodrigo Muniz and switching from a 4-2-3-1 system to a flat 4-4-2 in an attempt to defend the lead.

The subsequent floundering felt inevitable. Emile Smith Rowe, another late substitute, was slow to close down Abdoul Ouattara when the Ipswich right-back equalised. Fulham have dropped eight points from winning positions. They are managing games badly and their physical shortcomings were exposed by Ipswich, whose winner came from a poorly defended free-kick and left Fulham in last place before facing Hull at home on Saturday.

Arbeloa needs a win. Relegation fears are growing and there are whispers that the Spaniard’s job is under threat. Fulham had a tricky start – they have already faced Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United – but the Ipswich game was supposed to mark a turning point. It was the first of three consecutive meetings with the promoted sides and, with Coventry, Hull and Ipswich surpassing expectations, it is easy to see Fulham’s aim to move to a more expansive style under Arbeloa backfiring.

Questions have to be asked over the decision by the Khan family to appoint someone whose experience of management was limited to an interim spell in charge of Real Madrid last season. Fingers will be pointed at the succession planners. Tony Khan, director of football and son of patriarch Shahid, has faced fierce criticism in the past. Silva offered stability. There was always a fear the project would fall apart once the Portuguese was gone.

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García struggled to make an impression at Ipswich. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters

It does not help Arbeloa to lean on his time at the Bernabéu. He responded to a question about pressure after losing to Ipswich by saying: “I played for the best team in the world … I have coached the best team in the world.” But the optics are awkward. Arbeloa did not win anything as Madrid’s manager, his comments risk making it seem his current employers should be grateful to have him and eyebrows have been raised at three of the 43-year-old’s summer signings coming from his former club.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ángel, César Palacios and Gonzalo García were all promising young Real Madrid players, all share representation with Arbeloa and are now adapting to a new league. Palacios, an inventive passing midfielder, is 21 and Garcia, a nimble forward, is 22. They deserve to be given time, although the clock is ticking. García, signed for £40m, has one league goal from 18 shots and struggled against Ipswich, winning few duels and pressing ineffectively.

Supporters are growing restless. They wonder why Kevin, the Brazilian winger, is being used on the right rather than the left. They feel Arbeloa is chopping and changing too often. They worry about the team conceding costly late goals against Sunderland, Crystal Palace and United. Fulham were ridiculously open in their opening game, the barmy 3-2 defeat by Chelsea, and their expected goals against is 10.3 in six games. They have lost two of their main goalscorers, Raúl Jiménez and Harry Wilson, and are struggling to fill the void.

Equally there is an argument that Arbeloa needs time to implement a new style. There are suggestions some players are unsure about the manager’s tactics. Some stalwarts have been sidelined – Joachim Andersen, the influential Denmark centre-back, is not suited to playing a high line and has lost his spot to David Affengruber – but perhaps a refresh was required. Fulham have looked to lower the age of their squad, in part because of a need to comply with financial regulations, and there is nothing intrinsically wrong with trying to play more exciting football.

There have been encouraging spells. After flirting with European qualification in each of the past four seasons, only to fizzle out and finish in the bottom half, Fulham can be forgiven for wondering how to take the next step. At the same time the fear for supporters is that a club operating with one of the league’s smaller budgets have forgotten what it takes to survive. Silva’s teams could attack but were gritty and streetwise. At the moment Arbeloa looks naive. Fulham lost £45m in the past financial year and spent a lot on the Riverside Stand refurbishment. The Khans need Premier League survival. Arbeloa has big ideas but might not make it past this month without a huge improvement.

Sports.title: Nicolas Jackson backed to achieve career first at Aston Villa as pressure is less than Chelsea
Sports.content:
Nicolas Jackson backed to achieve career first at Aston Villa as pressure is less than Chelsea

Nicolas Jackson will set a personal goalscoring record this season with Aston Villa following his strong start for the club.

That's according to Villa legend Gabby Agbonlahor, whilst Alex Crook claims he is facing less pressure there than he did at Chelsea.

3 Jackson has already scored five goals in eight appearances for Villa since becoming their record signing Credit: Getty

Jackson joined the Villans in a club-record £65million deal from Chelsea in the summer as Ollie Watkins left for Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

He has scored five goals in eight appearances since, with two of those coming in their 6-0 Champions League thrashing of Fenerbahce.

The Senegalese forward hit a career-best of 17 goals in all competitions during the 2023/24 campaign, his debut year at Chelsea.

However, Agbonlahor, who is second in Villa's all-time Premier League scoring charts on 74 goals behind Watkins' 91, believes Jackson is set to break his personal record this season.

Jackson tipped to break scoring record

Sam Matterface asked him if Watkins did Villa a favour by leaving, but he replied: "I wouldn't say he did them a favour because it would have been nice to have both of them, pushing each other as far as they can. Ollie Watkins was a great servant for the football club.

"Nicolas Jackson is younger, worked under the manager before, he's come to Aston Villa and looks like he's polished his game a lot. His first touch looks a lot better, his movement.

"What he does that Ollie Watkins never did, he takes on players. He receives the ball, likes to get past the player and run with the ball, and some of his goals have been outstanding.

"His goal against Spurs, that touch, that turn, quick finish into the corner. Two goals against Fenerbahce from just outside the box, just inside the box.

"Three in the Champions League, two in the Premier League. I think he's going to be on 20 goals in all competitions at the end of the season. You need a quick striker in the Premier League, I feel."

Agbonlahor's talkSPORT colleague Crook then noted that Jackson has an advantage at Villa as he worked with manager Unai Emery during a spell at Villarreal.

3 Jackson has a strong enough start to convince Agbonlahor he will score 20 goals this season, which would be his best tally in a single campaign Credit: Getty

He also hinted that the 25-year-old is thriving now that he is playing for a club with less pressure for consistent success on his shoulders.

At Chelsea, his 30 goals were short of past heroes including Didier Drogba and Diego Costa, who scored 164 and 59 respectively.

And during his loan stint with Bayern Munich last season, he bagged 11 whilst Harry Kane netted 61.

Crook explained: "I just think that move to Chelsea probably came too early in his career. If you remember, he was close to joining Bournemouth at that stage; there was a medical issue.

"Then in the following summer, he ended up at Chelsea instead, so it was a big leap that he made.

"The big bonus for him at Aston Villa is he's playing under a manager who knows him, having worked with him in Spain.

3 Jackson scored 30 goals in 81 appearances at Chelsea, but the pressure may well have held him back Credit: Getty

"And there is less pressure when it comes to playing for Aston Villa than there is at a club like Chelsea.

"Even Bayern Munich, where he didn't pull up too many trees on loan last season."

Sports.title: Why Arsenal were forced to take team photo without William Saliba as Mikel Arteta issues re-take update
Sports.content:
Why Arsenal were forced to take team photo without William Saliba as Mikel Arteta issues re-take update

Arsenal are set to re-take their team photo for the 2026/27 season after William Saliba missed out.

The Frenchman was absent from the image, leading to many Arsenal fans demanding the club do it again with their star defender.



4 Saliba was absolutely nowhere to be seen as the Gunners gathered with the Premier League and Community Shield trophies Credit: Getty

And ahead of facing Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Mikel Arteta was asked about why Saliba missed the photo at the pre-match press conference.

Arsenal explained that Saliba was missing due to a medical appointment.

The French international is currently out of action with a back injury.



Saliba managed it throughout the majority of last season before it got too much during the World Cup.

The 25-year-old had to go off during the semi-final against Spain, indicating his back had given out.



The club and player opted not to have surgery with a period of rehabilitation instead, and that is why Saliba missed the photo.

And Arteta has confirmed that a new picture will be taken with Saliba front and centre.



He said: "What happened was that we have tried to do that picture three times already and we had to cancel it last minute for different reasons.

"We had some commercial obligations, we had some people who flew over to do that, so we decided to do that picture.

"We will have another picture with the whole family.

4 Saliba has yet to kick a ball for Arsenal this season Credit: Getty

"Hopefully we can get them all together at some point one day, and we'll announce that as well."



On Saliba's reaction, he said: "Well, it wasn't in his hands. But Willy is normally happy about everything. He knows how loved he is. He was taking some banter from the players, and he is completely fine."

Road to recovery

After the injury happened, Saliba and Arsenal were left with two choices.

One was for the player to have back surgery and be out for well over six months.

The other was to rest the back and hope that it didn't flare up again, with the aim for him to return in three to four months.



4 Saliba played a vital role in Arsenal winning their first Premier League title in 22 years Credit: Getty

Arteta revealed that Saliba is set to undergo an MRI to assess how far along he is, with the player back training on grass earlier in the month.

He said: "I think next week we have another MRI with him to see how the healing process is going.

"But every sign so far has been very, very positive. It will be good to have him."



Other Arsenal injuries

The Gunners are expecting to have Martin Zubimendi back, with the Spanish international recovering from his minor knock.

Piero Hincapie also suffered an injury at the same time as Zubimendi.

4 Arteta's injury woes are easing Credit: Getty

But after initially looking like it was bad, it turned out to be not so much of a problem.

He still faces another two weeks on the sidelines, though.

But Christos Tzolis is close to a return.

The Greek international suffered a hamstring injury while away with his country, but Arteta has revealed he's recovering well.



He said: "It's progressing really well.

"Another one that hopefully we can have back in a few weeks."

Sports.title: Alan Brazil reveals he’s heard ex-Premier League owner with $14b net worth wants to invest in Everton
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil reveals he’s heard ex-Premier League owner with $14b net worth wants to invest in Everton

Alisher Usmanov is potentially interested in resuming his investment at Everton, according to Alan Brazil.

Less than two years after their takeover at the Toffees, the Friedkin Group are considering a sale of their controlling stake.



3 talkSPORT's Brazil has heard rumours that Usmanov is looking to invest in Everton again as the Friedkin Family eye a stake sale Credit: Getty

They bought 99.5 per cent of the Premier League club in December 2024 in a deal worth more than £400million.

It brought an end to the unsettled tenure of Farhad Moshiri, during which Everton came close to being relegated from the top flight.

Russian-Uzbek businessman Usmanov, who has a $14billion (£10.5b) net worth as per Forbes, worked with Moshiri and the pair once owned a 14.58 per cent stake in Arsenal.



The former then completed a $15m (£11m) deal for the naming rights at Everton's Finch Farm training ground via USM Holdings in 2017, and later sponsored the women's team with MegaFon as their co-owner.

But after Russia invaded Ukraine in March 2022, Everton suspended their sponsorships with USM and Megafon, both Russian companies.



Usmanov was also sanctioned by the United Kingdom Government, similar to the former Chelsea owner Roman Abramovich.

However, talkSPORT Breakfast host Brazil explained on Friday's show that he has heard whispers of the 73-year-old returning to Everton.



"I can't confirm it, but I hear that Usmanov is trying to get back into Everton," he said.

"He has got some serious, serious money...

"Mr Usmanov, who was behind Moshiri, it appears that he's trying to get back in, if he can, to plough a load of dough into Everton."

3 Usmanov invested in Arsenal and Everton with Moshiri, who oversaw a turbulent spell at the Toffees from 2016 to 2024 Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Could Usmanov reinvest in Everton?

As part of the UK Government's sanctions, Usmanov was issued with a travel ban and had his assets frozen.



He and Igor Shuvalov, who fronted Russia's successful bid to host the 2018 World Cup, were adjudged to be associates of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Usmanov and Shuvalov were removed from the European Union's sanctions list last month.

However, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was opposed to the decision, according to Bloomberg.

Burnham was speaking to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and also said that the UK will not lift their sanctions.



Therefore, as it stands, Usmanov is unlikely to be allowed to invest in Everton amid a potential change to the structure of their ownership.

3 The Friedkin Family are looking for external investment at Everton less than two years after their arrival Credit: Getty

Usmanov is the 213th richest person in the world according to Forbes.

His global conglomerate, USM, owns 100 per cent of Metalloinvest, a Russian mining company whose reported revenue is worth around $5.2b (£3.9b), as per 311 Institute.

Sports.title: Robbie Savage hires EFL cult hero to backroom staff in Peterborough reshuffle
Sports.content:
Peterborough United boss Robbie Savage has added club legend Craig Mackail-Smith to his new-look backroom team.

Mackail-Smith joins the set-up as an attacking coach as he aims to impart his predatory wisdom on the club’s forward line.



3 Craig Mackail-Smith netted 104 goals over three spells with the club Credit: Getty

The former striker scored 104 goals for Posh and currently stands as the club’s sixth all-time leading scorer.

He played a key role in firing Peterborough to three promotions in four seasons under ex-boss Darren Ferguson between 2007 and 2011.

Mackail-Smith played 231 times for Posh during three separate spells.

He spent four years at the club in the late 2010s before returning for two further loan spells.



The striker also enjoyed spells at Brighton, Luton and Wycombe before calling time on his career in 2023.

Mackail-Smith represented Scotland at international level, clocking seven caps, scoring once.



Savage’s staff shake-up

The Peterborough boss has chosen to recruit internally for his backroom team, with academy director Dan Robinson appointed as his new assistant manager.

Former Posh winger Ryan Semple will take up a role as first team coach, having already worked across the Academy and first team.



Harry Hogg, who was the academy head of goalkeeping, becomes the club’s new first team goalkeeper coach.

Taewoong Kim makes the step-up as first team sports scientist, having helped in the development of Academy players.

3 The ex-striker is held in high esteem with Peterborough fans Credit: Getty

"I have got such a good connection with people inside the building already,” Savage told the club’s website.



“I came alone, and I was thinking of bringing somebody with me, but the connection I have got already - as seen on the bench Saturday and after the game - is already so good. There is already so many good people at this club.

"I have promoted from within at all of the clubs I have been at. Trust is huge and so is people that know the club. I want to give them a pathway. So the next generation of coaches coming up will see where they started and that they were able to move up to the first team.

“It’s the right thing to do and the chairman is onboard. It’s a great signal to the whole community that there’s pathways for staff members as well as players. I’m really happy with it as they all have Peterborough in their DNA and an alignment with the academy."

Savage has taken a proactive approach to his new role, and it appears to be paying off.



The 51-year-old is unbeaten in his first two games as Posh manager.

3 Savage was delighted with his side's display in last weekend's win at Leicester Credit: Getty

He oversaw a 4-1 win over Ipswich in the Football League Trophy earlier this month before masterminding a 3-1 win at Leicester City in League One last weekend.

Up next for Savage’s side is the visit of Burton Albion on Saturday lunchtime.

Posh sit 20th in the table, one place above the drop zone, with Savage hoping his influence can help continue the team’s upturn in form.
