Sports.title: Ex-EFL and Premier League star reveals how snus addiction got out of hand
Sports.content:
Ex-EFL and Premier League star reveals how snus addiction got out of hand

Former Premier League striker Fraizer Campbell has opened up about his addiction to snus during his playing career.

Campbell enjoyed a 16-year stint in the professional game, making 446 appearances for the likes of Manchester United, Sunderland and Crystal Palace before hanging up his boots in 2022.

3 Fraizer Campbell scored 104 goals in his professional career Credit: Getty

A Red Devils academy graduate, the 39-year-old made just four senior appearances at Old Trafford before leaving to join Sunderland permanently in 2009.

He went on to spend four years in the North east before joining Cardiff in 2013, helping them win promotion to the Premier League.

The forward managed six top-flight goals as the Bluebirds were relegated in the 2014/15 campaign, which earned him a move to Palace in the summer that followed.

And Campbell has now revealed it was during his three-year stint at Selhurst Park that he began taking snus.

Originating in Sweden, snus is a smokeless tobacco product made from ground or pulverised leaves, packaged similar to a teabag sachet, which is placed under the top lip.

Campbell opens up on snus use

In an appearance on The Sports Agents podcast, Campbell revealed he started taking snus whilst at Crystal Palace to help him wind down after matches.

He said: “I felt relaxed, and it just chilled me out more than anything.

“It was after a game as well, and after a game, it’s one of those things that it’s quite hard to relax after.”

Detailing his habits, Campbell admitted he gradually became more addicted to snus, which only got worse when he retired in 2022.

He continued: “Well, yeah. I definitely was addicted. But obviously, when I had more time on my hands when I retired, I had more time to have the snus.

3 Campbell scored eight goals in 50 games for Crystal Palace, during which time he began taking snus Credit: Getty

“So obviously, in the morning, while I was playing, I might have one in the morning or two in the morning and then for the next couple of hours I’d be out on the training pitch.

“I would never have them on a match day because it chilled me out too much, and I was someone that… I’m a pretty chill person as it is.

"If I was more chilled, I’d struggle to get into a jog.”

Campbell isn't the only former player to talk openly about his use of snus in his playing career, with former Liverpool and Tottenham star Danny Murphy also admitting to it after his retirement.

With the use of snus increasingly common among footballers, Murphy called for it to be banned in 2023.

And Campbell too revealed he only became fully aware of the negative effects of snus while playing, as he explained how it came to impact his day-to-day life.

3 Campbell began his career as a promising youngster at Man United Credit: Getty

He said: “It got a lot worse after I finished playing football, but I didn’t really see the negative side of it while I was playing.

“But it’s a familiar story. I’ve been to house parties, I’ve been on nights out, like you said, and I’m seeing lots of professionals doing these things. And I just don’t get it.”

However, Campbell finally revealed: “I am clean, six months clean now.

“I got to a stage where I just felt constantly fatigued, and I couldn’t put my finger on it. And obviously it was the snus. So, I packed it in, because it was giving me no benefits.”

After leaving Crystal Palace in 2017, Campbell spent the last five years of his career in the Championship.

He enjoyed a two-year stint at Hull, scoring 18 goals in 77 games, before seeing out his career at Huddersfield between 2019 and 2022.

Sports.title: FIFA could scrap controversial Peace Prize won by Donald Trump after just one year
Sports.content:
FIFA could scrap controversial Peace Prize won by Donald Trump after just one year

FIFA could scrap their controversial Peace Prize just 12 months after creating the award, talkSPORT understands.

U.S president Donald Trump was the recipient of the inaugural award at the World Cup draw held in Washington DC last December.

2 Donald Trump was handed the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize in December 2025, with Infantino lavishing praise on him Credit: Getty

But a FIFA Council meeting held in Zurich on Thursday concluded that its football social responsibility committee will now decide what meets the conditions of an annual prize.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino awarded the Peace Prize to Trump ahead of the 2026 World Cup.

However, it was not signed off by the FIFA Council, the governing body’s decision makers.

FIFA launches new decision-making process

The changes will see former Inter and Argentina defender Javier Zanetti lead a 22-person committee to ascertain whether or not the award should remain.

The assessment could see committee members ban the awarding of the Peace Prize to politicians, should the award remain.

Reports claim that the idea of having a Peace Prize was not completely dismissed during the meeting although questions were raised on its future.

A final outcome is expected in December when the football social responsibility committee meets at the next FIFA Council meeting, in Doha.

Debbie Hewitt, FIFA vice-president and president of the English Football Association further detailed the committee’s task.

“There’s a decision taken to look at the peace prize and to take that through the social committee,” she told reporters.

“That was another issue that was raised: whether there should have been one, how the decision was taken to award it, and whether there should be another one. And those questions will be answered through the social committee.”

2 Infantino has been under intense scrutiny for various issues since the award's inception last December Credit: Getty

FIFA previously announced that the yearly prize will ‘reward individuals who have taken exceptional and extraordinary actions for peace’.

The award would also represent those who have ‘united people across the world’.

FIFA further claimed that it ‘will be presented to individuals who, through their unwavering commitment and their special actions, have helped to unite people all over the world in peace and consequently deserve a special and unique recognition’.

The awarding of the Peace Prize to Trump was later heavily criticised after the U.S. President launched air strikes in Iran.

Trump was given a golden trophy, a medal and a certificate as part of the presentation.

The voting procedure behind his award has never been revealed.

Sports.title: Alan Brazil names two new contenders Man United should consider if they sack Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil names two new contenders Man United should consider if they sack Michael Carrick

Manchester United should consider two former Premier League bosses should they decide to part ways with Michael Carrick.

talkSPORT’s Alan Brazil believes the Red Devils should look no further than Mauricio Pochettino and Kieran McKenna if they are looking for a successor to Carrick in the near future.



3 Michael Carrick is struggling to replicate last season's heroics Credit: Getty

The Manchester United boss is under increasing pressure after an underwhelming start to the season.

United were beaten 2-0 by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, leaving them with just two wins from nine games across all competitions.

The defeat was followed by defender Lisandro Martinez’s bombshell post-match interview in which he slammed director Jason Wilcox for a below-par summer transfer window.



Carrick was handed the permanent reins at Old Trafford in the summer after taking over from Ruben Amorim on an interim basis.

He revamped United’s fortunes, leading the club to a third-placed finish and crucially, Champions League qualification.



He also inspired United to wins over Manchester City and Arsenal.

While reports claim that Carrick retains the support of the club’s board, the Manchester United boss knows that he must pick up points quickly to turn his side’s fortunes around.

Failing that, two standout names should be at the top of the list, according to Brazil.



Ex-Prem duo top Brazil's list

“There are some names about,” the Sports Breakfast host said.

“Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte. Pochettino – would he come back?

3 Mauricio Pochettino has been sounded out by Brazil as a good fit for United Credit: Getty

“He's still a big Tottenham man but he would come back in my opinion.

“Kieran McKenna’s about, he knows about United.”

Pochettino is currently manager of the United States Men’s team.

He has been heavily linked with a return to the Premier League with Manchester United a possible destination for the Argentine.

Pochettino previously confirmed that United had shown a strong interest in him in the past.

The 54-year-old even recalled a famous lunch meeting requested by Sir Alex Ferguson during his time as Tottenham boss.



3 Kieran McKenna has close ties to Manchester United Credit: Getty

He later claimed that the ‘ideal scenario’ to take the job failed to materialise at the right time.

Meanwhile, McKenna is currently taking a career break from football management whilst working as a UEFA technical observer.

McKenna stepped down as Ipswich manager in June after guiding the club back to the Premier League – a third promotion in five years.



Despite stepping away from management, he has continued to be linked with managerial vacancies, including interest from Fulham.

Prior to his time at Portman Road, McKenna spent over five years at Manchester United between 2016 and 2021, progressing from the youth academy to first-team assistant.

Sports.title: South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dead aged 31: Former Sale Sharks star suffers heart attack at team hotel in France on eve of Champions Cup clash with La Rochelle
Sports.content:
South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dead aged 31: Former Sale Sharks star suffers heart attack at team hotel in France on eve of Champions Cup clash with La Rochelle

Tributes have been paid to ‘funny’, ‘charismatic’ and ‘brilliant team-mate’ Hyron Andrews after the former Sale Sharks lock died of a suspected heart attack in news that has shocked the rugby world.

On Friday morning, French media reported a playing member of the Lions – one of South Africa’s four big domestic teams – had been found unresponsive in a shower at the Atalante-Relais Thalasso Hotel just outside of La Rochelle – the venue where the side is preparing for European Champions Cup game on Saturday which will go ahead as planned.

Just a few hours later, the Lions confirmed the passing of Andrews, 31. Emergency services arrived but were unable to save him and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Andrews only returned to his native South Africa to join the Lions this summer after departing English club side Sale for whom he made 45 appearances. Of those, 19 came for the Sharks last season. Andrews' former club boss, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson, said: 'Hyron was just a brilliant guy and team-mate. He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with.

'He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him. It was a big move for Hyron and his wife Maiglin to come to England but he truly made a second home in Manchester and it was incredible to see how he and his family embraced the club and area.

'Most importantly, he was a loving husband and a doting father to his two gorgeous boys. It was an absolute privilege to get to know him. It’s just absolutely devastating for everyone.'

Lions player Hyron Andrews, 31, has died of an apparent heart attack in La Rochelle, a day before the two sides were due to meet in the European Champions Cup

Hyron and his wife Maiglin along with one of their sons are pictured here

Confirming Andrews’ passing, the Lions said in a statement: ‘The Lions Rugby Company is deeply saddened by the passing of player Hyron Andrews while on tour with the 10bet Lions ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and Vodacom United Rugby Championship fixtures.

'This devastating news has sent shockwaves through the international rugby community. The former Sharks and Sale Sharks lock forward was a valued member of the Lions family and his loss will be felt profoundly by his team-mates, coaches, supporters and all who had the privilege of knowing him. Our deepest and most heartfelt condolences go to Hyron’s wife, Maiglin, their young sons, and the entire Andrews family. We hold them in our thoughts during this time of unimaginable grief and ask that their privacy be respected as they mourn.’ The Lions have confirmed that their scheduled clash with La Rochelle will go ahead with the team’s players keen to pay tribute to Andrews on the field.

Reports in the French media said a psychological support unit had been set up for the Lions franchise's players and staff, as well as the hotel personnel.

Rudolf Straeuli, Lions chief executive, said: ‘We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family having recently joined us this season.

'On behalf of our chairman, Mr Altmann Allers, the board and everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to Maiglin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect.’

The Lions added: ‘The Lions Rugby Company will communicate further details regarding an appropriate tribute in due course. In honour of Hyron, the 10bet Lions will fulfil their opening match of the Investec Champions Cup against La Rochelle tomorrow evening South African time. May Hyron rest in peace.’

Andrews' former employers Sale said: 'Everyone at Sale Sharks is devastated to learn of the death of our former player Hyron Andrews. Hyron was a much-loved member of the squad during his time with us and everyone at the club is united in sending their love, thoughts and heartfelt condolences to his wife Maiglin, their beautiful boys and the rest of his family and friends and everyone at Lions Rugby.'

PREM Rugby also said in a statement: 'Everyone at PREM Rugby and our clubs is deeply saddened by the passing of Hyron Andrews and we extend our heartfelt sympathies to his family and friends.

'Our thoughts are also with Hyron’s team-mates past and present, everyone at the Lions and Sale Sharks, and the wider South African rugby community at this very difficult time.'

Hyron Andrews career Andrews spent the majority of his career playing in his native South Africa with the lock having joined the academy of Durban-based the Sharks in 2014. He made his debut for the Sharks in 2016 and made 83 appearances for the team, scoring three tries. Andrews was part of the Sharks side that reached the quarter-finals of the Champions Cup in 2023. The 6’8 lock joined Sale Sharks on an initial short-term deal in the 2023-24 season. He ultimately stayed at the PREM Rugby side for a further two seasons, playing 45 times in total. Andrews left at the end of last season to return to South Africa with the Lions. Internationally, Andrews represented South Africa at the 2015 World Rugby Under 20 Championship in 2015. The junior Springboks were beaten in the semi-finals by England, but won the third place match against France.

Andrews was a former South Africa Under-20 international.

Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union, said: 'This is terrible and distressing news. Our hearts go out to Hyron’s family and the whole Lions rugby community.

'There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maiglin and for his extended family, friends, team-mates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow.

'Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness.

'His untimely passing is a devastating loss and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.

'The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maiglin and all those mourning his loss. May they find strength, comfort and peace in the memories they shared with him and in the support of those around them.'

In a bizarre coincidence, Andrews’ tragic passing occurred on the 10-year anniversary of the death of Munster legend Anthony Foley. A former Munster coach and captain, Foley died in his sleep on October 16, 2016, at the age of 42 in Paris on the eve of a European tie against Racing 92 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs.

Ronan O’Gara, the current La Rochelle head coach, was an ex-Munster team-mate of Foley’s. Reports have suggested O’Gara headed to the team hotel of the Lions to offer the team’s grieving players and support staff emotional support. La Rochelle said they had learned of Andrews’ death with ‘immense sadness.’ They added: ‘The club extends its deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, team-mates, staff and the entire Lions family.

South African star Andrews played for Sale in England before leaving at the end of last season

‘To honour the memory of their team-mate and out of respect for La Rochelle and its fans, the Lions players and staff have decided, despite the circumstances, to play the match.

‘A minute's silence will be observed before kick-off. La Rochelle invites its supporters to join in this moment of reflection with the utmost respect.

‘La Rochelle remains by the side of the Lions in this ordeal.’

European Rugby organisers said: ‘It is with deep sadness that EPCR has learned of the tragic passing of 10bet Lions player Hyron Andrews while on tour ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and URC fixtures.’

The organisation’s chairman, Dominic McKay, said: ‘The thoughts of everyone at EPCR and the wider international rugby community are with Hyron’s wife Maiglin, his young sons, wider family, friends, team-mates, the 10bet Lions and all those who knew and loved him at this incredibly difficult time.’ In memory of Andrews, a moment’s silence will be held ahead of every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match this weekend.

Those tributes began when Gloucester hosted French giants and current European champions Bordeaux on Friday night.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta defends Arsenal's decision to cut 60 jobs - just days after he signed a bumper £20m-a-year contract... and confirms club WILL retake squad photo after missing William Saliba
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal’s plan to axe 60 members of staff, saying the job cuts are being done to ‘achieve the success we want to create’.

The redundancies will not affect the men’s and women’s teams coaching or backroom staff, the club’s community operation, the Arsenal Foundation and security staff. Instead, the cuts will focus on off-field areas.

It comes just a week after Arsenal announced Arteta had signed a lucrative four-year contract worth around £20million per year.

He said: ‘This question is not for me. It was explained to me about the exercise and the analysis that has been done across the club, and with the intention always to evolve to improve.

‘Some decision has to be taken to put people in the right roles, and keep investing to achieve what we want to achieve on the success that we want to create. So that has been explained. Obviously I am not the right person to answer to that question, that's for sure. And hopefully everybody will respect that.’

When pressed further on the matter, the club's press officer interjected to say the question was one for CEO Richard Garlick and not Arteta.

Meanwhile, Arteta said Arsenal’s official 2026-27 squad photo will be retaken after the omission of William Saliba.

Arsenal released a squad picture this week without William Saliba, who was at a doctor's appointment on the day of the shoot

The club confirmed afterwards that the Frenchman was away at a doctor’s appointment on the day of the photoshoot.

Arteta said: ‘So what happened was that we had tried to do that picture three times already. We had to cancel it last minute for different reasons and we have some commercial obligations. So we decided to do that picture at least. Yeah (we will retake it with Saliba in).’

On if Saliba was happy being missed out, he added: ‘It wasn't in his hands. But normally he's happy about everything.

‘And he knows how loved he is and they were taking some banter (about it). He's completely fine.’

Sports.title: Real Madrid demand resignation of La Liga president for comparing club's media strategy to that of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels
Sports.content:
Real Madrid demand resignation of La Liga president for comparing club's media strategy to that of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels

Real Madrid have called for the resignation of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he compared methods used by the club's management to Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.

Tebas had accused select journalists of acting as an 'official mouthpiece' of the club to air grievances, suggesting they were promoting views of high-ranking Real Madrid officials.

The La Liga chief claimed their approach was to create a narrative that casts the Spanish giants as a victim of referees and La Liga's decisions.

'Real Madrid's management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing,' Tebas wrote on social media.

'Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

'That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative.

Real Madrid have called for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he suggested the club have employed techniques used by Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels

'The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase. Real Madrid TV is a central piece of that machinery. Where is the full match analysis for each round of games?

'Where are the possible errors that harm other clubs or those that favor Real Madrid? If they applied the same magnifying glass to every match, the result might ruin their script. But the script demands that Real Madrid always appear as the victim.'

Real Madrid responded in a lengthy statement with the club declaring Tebas's reference to Goebbels, who served as the Third Reich's Minister of Propaganda between 1933 and 1945, was 'deeply offensive' and 'morally repugnant.'

'The repeated conduct of Javier Tebas shows a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities,' a club statement read.

'Real Madrid CF considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone who occupies two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football should resort to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television.

'His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those who demand transparency and regeneration constitute, in the opinion of our club, a real scourge for Spanish football.

'Consequently, Real Madrid C. F. demands his immediate resignation as president of LaLiga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation.'

Real Madrid also said it was 'especially concerning' that Tebas's post referenced the ongoing Negreira case.

The La Liga president claimed Real Madrid have tried to cast themselves as a 'victim' with complaints over officiating and scheduling of matches

The Spanish giants sent 50,000 pages of evidence to European football's governing body UEFA earlier this month, with the club accusing arch-rivals Barcelona of making illicit payments to an influential referees' chief.

The allegations in Spain are that Barcelona paid more than £7million in a series of payments over 17 years from 2001 to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira when he was vice president of Spain's technical committee of referees.

Barcelona have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing, claiming the money was paid for scouting and technical reports provided by a company belonging to 81-year-old Negreira since the story broke in 2023.

La Liga claimed they were unable to investigate because of the time elapsed since the alleged offences were so far in the past, but UEFA did launch an investigation which remains ongoing.

Real Madrid and Tebas have frequently clashed in the past, with the latest incident coming with the Spanish giants having complained about refereeing decisions in recent matches.

Tebas had claimed last month the club were creating a 'permanent conspiracy' about officiating.

Responding to Real Madrid's demand for his resignation, Tebas again hit out at 'Real Madrid TV and its lapdogs' and claimed the club was trying to destroy La Liga.

'I've lost count of the times that, in thirteen years, Real Madrid's leaders have demanded my resignation or tried to disqualify me: complaints to the CSD, directly or through third parties, criminal lawsuits… Today's is just another one,' he wrote.

'What still hasn't arrived are the responses. They confuse neutrality with independence. My position demands independence, not passivity in the face of injustice or silence in the face of the continuous, disproportionate, and insulting attacks from Real Madrid TV and its lapdogs on our competition.

'The LaLiga president must defend it. Including against Real Madrid's leaders.

'My conclusion: they seek to DESTROY the national competition. What they haven't achieved so far with the Superliga, they're trying with a distorted narrative from their media and their lapdogs. They call it regeneration while attacking the prestige of the competition they participate in.'

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca insists Man City have been galvanised by guilty verdict, Morgan Gibbs-White a doubt for Forest's clash with Arsenal... and Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa remains defiant
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca insists Man City have been galvanised by guilty verdict, Morgan Gibbs-White a doubt for Forest's clash with Arsenal... and Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa remains defiant

Managers up and down the country will be speaking to the press ahead of the latest weekend of Premier League action.

Daily Mail Sport will bring you all the key news here...

Maresca: City galvanised by guilty verdict

Enzo Maresca has told Manchester City's rivals that the whole club has been galvanised by the guilty verdicts handed down for serious breaches of financial rules.

City are three points clear at the top of the Premier League going into Saturday's home game against Ipswich Town and possess a 100 per cent domestic record this season.

Their case with the league is going to appeal after an independent commission found the club guilty of all substantive charges, with calls for the leaders to be expelled from the division.

Enzo Maresca believes the guilty verdicts handed down to Manchester City for serious breaches of financial rules have galvanised the whole club

City have won at Anfield and lost a Champions League classic against Paris Saint-Germain since the judgment and Maresca has seen a change in his players.

And it appears that the squad are leaning into the idea that the majority of top-flight followers want them to lose – something Ruben Dias recently suggested has spurred them on for some time.

'Ruben said that people don't like City winning,' Maresca said. 'But we like to win. I think that is a good message for everyone. Since the noise, I can see from my personal point of view the fans, the club, the team more together for sure.

'From my point of view, the wise way to judge a situation is always to wait for the final words. But I can understand that now people need to speak about this situation. I don't need people from outside the club to (help) understand the situation.

'I don't feel any kind of stress about the outside situation, because it's something that I don't control.'

Daily Mail Sport revealed last week that in a meeting ahead of Liverpool, Maresca's motivational address was focused on how they have a title to battle for. The Italian has reiterated publicly that they must 'make their own noise'.

City maintain their innocence and insist they will prevail on appeal, with ex-manager Pep Guardiola's attendance in midweek a show of support for his former employers.

Guardiola is thought to have entered the dressing room but Maresca said he didn't speak to the players.

And Guardiola's successor has been fascinated by the influx of inflatable bananas brought to matches by supporters over recent days in a throwback to a craze first introduced in the 1980s.

'I didn't know the history behind the banana,' Maresca added. 'I hope tomorrow I can see many bananas in the stadium.

'I think it creates a nice environment for the fans and for everyone that is in the stadium. I have four kids and they already asked me about them. Tomorrow they're going to be at the stadium and we'll see.'

By Jack Gaughan

Arbeloa not distracted by sack talk

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa maintains he cannot allow speculation over his job to distract him from keeping everyone focused on beating Hull.

The Spaniard's position has come under the spotlight with his side bottom of the Premier League table and only having secured two points from six games following last weekend's late defeat at Ipswich, where they had been 1-0 up with three minutes left.

Former Real Madrid boss Arbeloa, who took over at Craven Cottage in the summer, insists his only focus has to be on Saturday's showdown with newly promoted Hull – a game which he had previously described as a 'final'.

Arbeloa said at a press conference: 'I am focused on tomorrow's game, on my players, on my team. That for me is the most important thing.

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa won't let speculation over his future distract him from beating Hull

'It is not about me. It is about the club, it is about the players. It is about the supporters. And like I said before, we are waiting for the game where the performance turns into a result.'

Despite reports he would be sacked if Fulham do not beat Hull, Arbeloa again stressed it was business as usual. 'For me, it has been a normal week where we have been working hard, where we were preparing a difficult match against a very difficult team,' he said.

'They (players) did (execute the game plan) for many minutes against Ipswich. We did against Man United, we did against Liverpool, so for me, we need to try to keep that level for 90 minutes.

'I saw the commitment of the players this week, how they have been training, and they are so focused on tomorrow's game. I saw them how they can play and for me, it is the most important thing: the performance of my players.'

Gibbs-White a doubt for Forest's clash with Arsenal

Nottingham Forest are sweating on the fitness of Morgan Gibbs-White ahead of Sunday's clash with Arsenal.

The England international picked up a calf injury in last weekend's defeat at Crystal Palace and has not trained all week.

He is expected to train with the squad on Saturday and will be assessed before the visit of the champions.

Nottingham Forest are sweating on the fitness of Morgan Gibbs-White ahead of Sunday's clash with Arsenal

'Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt, he couldn't train the entire week with us,' boss Oliver Glasner said. 'But it looks like he can join tomorrow's session.

'He had an individual session today with our rehab coaches, and he suffered a minor muscle injury at Palace. Then we have to see how he reacts today and how he deals with tomorrow's session, and then how we take the final decision.'

Forest will also assess Nikola Milenkovic, who has returned to training after a bone bruise.

'Milenkovic trained for the first time today,' Glasner said. 'Let's see now how he reacts.

'He could be in the matchday squad, but let's see, because he's been out now for several weeks.'

Farke: We're not favourites

Daniel Farke does not accept his side are favourites to end the club's long wait for a home win against Manchester United in Sunday's Roses battle.

Leeds, who have not beaten the Reds at Elland Road since 2002, are riding high in seventh place, while Michael Carrick's side have won only two of their nine games in all competitions this season, with the club heavily criticised in midweek by their own defender Lisandro Martinez.

Farke said: 'I'm not sure if we're favourites. I know how the perception is. We we had a brilliant start to this new season and are in a really good position.

'And yes, perhaps Man U have found it tough to win their last matches, but nevertheless, if you have a look at the squads, if you have a look how long they have spent at Premier League level, you have to say that they are definitely not the underdog in a game against Leeds United.

'If you look at their transfer value and the quality they have, and also the options, it's still a very dangerous opponent, and even more dangerous when they come off the back of a few games without a win. So I'm very respectful and know we have to be at the top of our game.'

Farke refused to comment on Martinez's outburst after Tuesday's Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid when he called out the club's hierarchy for lacking ambition.

'No comments about any anything in their camp,' Farke said, before adding: 'I just rate it in a different way when the perception is also a bit negative.

'There's always a chance, a bit like a hurt boxer more or less, to also change the momentum again.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists Man United have 'moved on' from Lisandro Martinez's 'mistake' - and claims squad is in a 'fantastic place' despite defender's explosive rant at club chiefs
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick insists Man United have 'moved on' from Lisandro Martinez's 'mistake' - and claims squad is in a 'fantastic place' despite defender's explosive rant at club chiefs

Michael Carrick believes Lisandro Martinez 'realised he has made a mistake' over his extraordinary outburst in Madrid, and insists the controversy will not distract Manchester United from turning their season around.

Martinez will be in United's squad to face Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday after he apologised for criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and club bosses in a television interview which landed the 28-year-old defender with a fine.

Carrick, who was in the meeting with Martinez and Wilcox at Carrington on Thursday, said: 'You're after some kind of big information about big discussions, but it was pretty simple.

'We all understood the situation and what it meant. Lisandro obviously made his statement, and he acknowledges that it was a mistake from him, and that was it really. It's really not a drama for us as a group. We've genuinely moved on.

'From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what's been done has certainly been enough. He's released his statement and he's realised he's made a mistake. I think that's enough for all of us to move on with. We're definitely not looking back at it now.'

Former United captain Wayne Rooney claimed that Martinez’s criticism of United’s transfer policy in the summer could rip the dressing-room apart, but Carrick believes his team’s performance in a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid – and the mood in training over the last two days – suggest the opposite is true.

Man United boss Michael Carrick has given his verdict on Lisandro Martinez's explosive rant

Martinez ripped into United's hierarchy on TV after their defeat by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday

'The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while actually,' added the United boss.

'We're living it every day, we know what it feels like. We're emotional, we're passionate, we care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that maybe they shouldn't say at a certain time, but that doesn't distract us from what we're creating here and the environment and the spirit within the group.

'It's not affected. I'm telling you as it is. We're in a good place, and I'm really happy with the boys today.

'Results-wise, it hasn't gone to plan of late, but today was one of the best training sessions we've had. You can see there's a real sense and a feeling within the group that we want to do something about this situation.

'There's a lot of things can affect the group in all sorts of different ways. Certain situations can galvanise the group, and it's certainly galvanised the group as this week's progressed.'

Carrick also suggested that emotion got the better of Amad Diallo after the Ivorian posted a message on Tuesday night, saying 'f***ing disgrace, I have no words'.

'Again, it's a situation where there's ways of doing it,' said Carrick. 'In one way, it shows the boys care an awful lot. But yes, of course, there are ways of doing it as part of learning a little bit. I think we've just got to show that emotion in the right manner and channel it in the right manner.

'We ask for passion, we ask for emotion, we ask for fire, and we ask for players to care. There's a way of doing that. As a group, we've got to use it in the right way.'

Carrick desperately needs a reaction from his players at Elland Road after a run of four defeats and two wins in nine games this season has put him under pressure.

Old rivals Leeds will be relishing the chance to pile on more misery, but Carrick said: 'I don't need results, we all need results. It's not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual: bigger than me, bigger than any player or anyone else who works at this football club.

'I don't go into every day at work in this situation thinking about me. It's about the football club: what we stand for, what we live for, the history, the things that we need to live up to, and that's what drives us.

'So whatever is best for the football club and for the team on Sunday is the most important thing. It's a great rivalry. There's big history between the football clubs, and I think that's what makes these type of games special.

'You've got to embrace the history, you've got to embrace what it means, and you've got to embrace the past of certain games that are a little bit different. This is certainly one of them, and we'll be ready for it.'

United technical director Jason Wilcox (left) was on the receiving end of Martinez's anger

Martinez had taken aim at the United hierarchy in the wake of a fourth defeat in nine games in Madrid when he was asked if the club have backed Carrick enough.

'I don't think so,' he said. 'He does his best. You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager.

'What about other areas? Tonight it is easy to say the coach and easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas.

'I expect more (investment) 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

'I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.'

On Thursday evening, after talks with United, Martinez shared a social media post apologising.

'Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager,' he said: 'It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

'Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

'The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.'

Sports.title: Billy Loughnane on realising his dream at just 20 as he gets set to be crowned youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century - and your best bets for big Flat finale Ascot
Sports.content:
Billy Loughnane on realising his dream at just 20 as he gets set to be crowned youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century - and your best bets for big Flat finale Ascot

With typical humility and understatement, Billy Loughnane adeptly recalls the formative stages of his career: 'My aim was to just have a few winners.'

The affable 20-year-old, who will be crowned the youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century on Saturday, has swiftly left behind those modest early ambitions with his career winners' tally currently standing at more than 700 and rising quicker than the price of diesel.

As Loughnane takes dead aim at the record held by the legendary Sir Gordon Richards of 269 winners in a calendar year – he equalled his personal best of 223 on Tuesday at Wolverhampton – comparisons are inevitably drawn with a similarly precocious jockey of days gone by, Frankie Dettori.

While the now retired Italian is widely regarded as one of the finest and most natural riding talents to grace British racing, Loughnane has, at this embryonic stage of his career, three Group 1 wins to Dettori's sole success at the age of 20, while it took Dettori eight years to reach 1,000 winners, whereas Loughnane has approximately 750 in half the time.

'If someone had said to me back then, that I would be Champion Jockey in four years I would have said they were absolutely crazy and asked them, "what have you been drinking!" joked Loughnane who has beaten five-time Champion Oisin Murphy to the title.

'I put a little pressure on myself, having come so far not to let it slip in the last little bit of the season, but the last two weeks have been enjoyable. It's a dream that is beginning to come true.

'At the start, I wanted to achieve becoming Champion Apprentice, I didn't for one minute think it would snowball as it has. My aim was to just have a few winners.

Billy Loughnane will be crowned the youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century on Saturday

'It has been an extraordinary couple of years really and I'm lucky that I've been able to team up with a lot of good trainers who have propelled me forward.'

One of those connections has been with Newmarket handler George Boughey for whom Loughnane has ridden nigh on 180 winners in those four seasons, including that golden trio of elite successes aboard Bow Echo this season.

As well as being a masterful trainer, Boughey has a keen eye for a talented rider and this year his Craven House Stables on Hamilton Road will house not only the Champion Jockey in Loughnane, but Champion Apprentice Jack Callan and younger brother Henry, who looks set to be crowned Champion Amateur rider.

The symbiotic relationship Loughnane shares with Boughey and the unadulterated joy the duo shared in the now retired Bow Echo's successes has been one of the most heart-warming aspects of the summer.

'George is a very good mentor as well as a very good trainer and he's become a very good friend,' reveals Loughnane.

'It was a dream come true to find a horse like Bow Echo – unbeaten in six starts, a winner of the Guineas, at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes, it was an amazing journey.

'It was gutting that injury meant we don't get to see him next year, but winning the Guineas was the best buzz I've ever had on the racecourse.

SAM TURNER'S TIPS FOR CHAMPIONS DAY AT ASCOT 12:55 – Arapaho Gold 1:30 – Highwayman 2:05 – Almeraq 2:40 – Lilt (ew) 3:20 – More Thunder (Nap) 4:00 – Calandagan 4:35 – Scoville (nb)

'There was six or seven months of him keeping us warm through the winter and when I was in Dubai, I was getting pictures of him off George all the time.

'That build up made the Guineas win extra special.'

While Loughnane is comfortable at Meydan, Longchamp or Saturday's royal venue Ascot, his love of racing was nurtured in more humble surroundings during his time 'assisting' father Mark, himself a trainer, based in Kidderminster.

'Every Saturday, between the age of six and 12, I would go racing to Wolverhampton with my dad and I would be distraught if he didn't have a runner!

'When I started dealing with the horses more at home, I didn't go racing as much as I was working in the yard then.

'My dad's work ethic is second to none – he works so hard every day and growing up alongside him and working with him, that was instilled in me from an early age.

'Wolverhampton and Ascot are my two favourite courses, but Wolves will always have a special place in my heart for obvious reasons.'

While parallels have understandably been drawn with Dettori, Loughnane's infectious manner, professionalism and joyous personality are arguably more in keeping with the legendary rider whose record he may strive to hunt down this year.

Sir Gordon Richards was born within hailing distance of Loughnane's beloved Dunstall Park at Donnington Wood in Telford, Shropshire, overcoming tuberculosis as a 22-year-old just months after becoming Champion Jockey for the first time.

Loughnane, who has been compared to Frankie Dettori, was Champion Apprentice in 2023

In a career which stretched from 1920 until his retirement following a fall at Sandown in 1954, Richards partnered 4,870 winners and was crowned Champion Jockey a staggering 26 times.

The son of a miner, Richards was not only a colossus in the saddle but earned a reputation as a rider of integrity and professionalism while those who knew him well described him as a warm, generous and modest man.

Humility and Dettori were not always comfortable bedfellows, but Loughnane's effervescent demeanour has quickly earned a sincere affection from the British racing public who welcomed him back to the winner's enclosures of Newmarket, Ascot and Goodwood this summer with the fervour reserved for champions.

'I love my job and I love riding horses – it's all I've ever wanted to do,' enthuses Loughnane with an endearing simplicity.

'It's amazing I've found something that is a passion of mine and I'm able to do it as a job. It's all I have ever wanted to do, and I've never looked another way.'

Referring to the fact Richards was Champion Jockey an incredible 26 times, he quips: 'I don't think I'll be riding in 26 years' time to be honest!

'It (the record) is in my sights. I'm just going to take the rest of this month and November (as normal) and then assess in December to see if it's possible.'

The last word goes to mother Clare, arguably the most important cog in the family training business, to whom her son credits his meticulous attention to detail and professionalism.

Loughnane rode the golden trio of elite successes aboard Bow Echo (yellow silks) this season

'I think the day it all changed was on Champions Day three years ago,' revealed Clare.

'Billy had enjoyed a fairly smooth year winning the Apprentice Jockey's Championship and when we turned up at Ascot that day and saw a giant poster of him hanging there, we said to ourselves "wow, this is a big thing".

'It was then that we said to him, well done, you've had a brilliant year, but now the hard work starts for real.

'We helped him when he was starting at the lower level, but we couldn't prepare him for what was to come at the top level.

'He has had to deal with that himself and he has changed from a young boy to a young man since.

'As parents, we couldn't be any prouder of him as he's been exceptional in his conduct from day one and has maintained the same persona throughout.

'He even comes home occasionally!'

Sports.title: Adam Wharton's family embroiled in clash with French football fans ahead of Crystal Palace's defeat in Lyon - with England star's mum and dad playing peacemakers
Sports.content:
Adam Wharton’s family were caught up in an altercation before Crystal Palace’s defeat by Lyon on Thursday night.

In a video posted on X, a group of Lyon supporters chanted La Marseillaise, the French national anthem, at Palace fans on a metro platform while station staff tried to keep them apart.

One Palace fan called it on, urging the provocative Lyon crew to square up to him before being dragged away. Meanwhile, the Wharton clan were front and centre with Adam’s brother, Simon, hurling abuse while pointing and probing at rival fans.

Wharton’s mum and dad, Helen and John - who are regulars in the Palace away end and even have their own chant - played peacemakers during the trouble.

Helen, a PE teacher, drew on her playground conflict-resolution tactics, restraining Simon and urging the other Palace fan to calm down as she tried to stop the skirmish.

The account that posted the video on X suggested the clip was the ‘start of a fight’ in the Metro but ‘everyone was quickly separated by security and law enforcement ’, with the incident beginning with someone ‘barrelling down the stairs’.

Adam Wharton's family were caught up in an altercation with rival fans on Thursday night

Crystal Palace have been contacted for comment.

Palace lost 3-2 in Lyon, where Wharton captained the side, and his parents were spotted drinking with fans on the afternoon of the game.

Wharton joined Palace from Blackburn Rovers in 2024 for £18 million and has made 105 appearances for the Eagles, winning three trophies.

The 22-year-old has been capped four times by England and was in the Euro 2024 squad but has been named in just two squads during Thomas Tuchel’s reign.

Sports.title: Reece James set for THREE months on the sidelines after knee surgery in major blow to Chelsea - as club give update on injured captain after he missed 5-1 win over Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Reece James is set to be out of action for around three months after having surgery on a knee injury sustained in training. James, 26, missed his side’s 5-1 Premier League win over Bournemouth after the international break. While he usually still travels with the squad on the team coach when injured, he did not do so for that victory, sparking concerns that there was more to his latest setback. Now, Chelsea have confirmed that James has had a ‘successful minor’ operation, and will be without him for their league trip to Everton on Saturday and beyond. In a statement, Chelsea said: ‘Captain Reece James has undergone successful minor knee surgery. 'The 26-year-old was absent from Saturday’s 5-1 victory over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge while medical assessments took place following the injury suffered in training. Reece James has undergone knee surgery after missing Chelsea's 5-1 win over Bournemouth ‘Those assessments confirmed surgery would be the required course of action. Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club's medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase. ‘Everyone at Chelsea wishes Reece a speedy recovery and will support him on his road to return.’ Levi Colwill captained Chelsea against Bournemouth in James’ absence. Xabi Alonso said on James: 'It's not going to be short. It's not going to be two or three weeks. It's going to be longer. We will see. Before Christmas, after Christmas, time will tell. 'But things have to be done properly, so that he feels right, and that means in the best possible condition. Yes, is it a disappointment for everyone, for him. But we have a squad for that to deal with injuries.' On whether James' injury will force Chelsea to use the January window, Alonso added: 'No, I don't think so. We expect for that time that he is back. It doesn't affect (transfer business).' James has an unfortunate history of injuries, largely due to hamstring issues. With that, Alonso had been morphing him into a midfielder rather than a right back. In fact, James has missed 842 days of action, as per Transfermarkt, since he broke into Chelsea's first team during the 2019-20 season. That is the equivalent of 2.31 years or 99 games for club and country. Given that record, Daily Mail Sport understands that Chelsea won't rush the 26-year-old back prematurely and will ensure he recovers fully before returning to action. James suffered the injury in training and is set to miss around three months of action James’ new problem robs Alonso of another midfield option, at a time when there were already concerns surrounding numbers in that central area. Moises Caicedo is now back from being sidelined, which should help until January, when Chelsea are likely to try to add at least one reinforcement. They are known to admire Alex Scott, though Bournemouth say they want more than £100million to sell him this winter. Other midfield options for Alonso include the injury-prone Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco, Jordan Henderson, full-back Malo Gusto and youngster Reggie Watson. The Blues face Everton on Saturday lunchtime, before league games against Tottenham, Man United and Sunderland ahead of next month's international break.
