World.title: UK PM adviser’s wife expresses ‘support’ for Palestine Action
World.content:
British police are reviewing a social media post by the wife of National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell in which she appears to endorse Palestine Action, a group proscribed in the country as a “terrorist” organisation.

“God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action,” Sarah Helm, a writer who is married to Powell – Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s national security adviser – wrote on X on Thursday.

She was responding to a post defending Irish novelist Sally Rooney, who this week announced her books would no longer be sold in the United Kingdom over her plans to use her royalties to support Palestine Action.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson on Friday said Helm’s post is “being assessed to determine whether any further police investigation may be required”.

A government spokesperson cited by the Reuters news agency said the views expressed in Helm’s post “are held by an individual who does not represent the government in any capacity”.

‘Absurdly authoritarian ban’

UK-based activist group Defend Our Juries defended Helm for defying what it called an “absurdly authoritarian ban on Palestine Action”.

“We know of 36 people who have been arrested and had their homes raided for similarly expressing support for Palestine Action on social media,” said a spokesperson for the group.

“We hope Sarah will not face the same treatment for standing up for free speech and Palestinian lives.”

The UK government outlawed Palestine Action in July 2025, after activists from the group broke into a Royal Air Force base and sprayed red paint on two aircraft to protest against UK military support for Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. Being a member or a supporter is punishable by up to 14 years in prison.



Since the ban went into effect, police have arrested more than 3,500 people in the UK for alleged support of the group, many of them for holding up placards, according to rights group Amnesty International.

Palestine Action has contested its proscription, but the Court of Appeal upheld it in June.

The UK’s new Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband last month said the government was “looking at” the Palestine Action ban, adding that he did not believe mass arrests resulting from its proscription were “anyone’s intent”.

World.title: How Iran messaging highlights cost of war ahead of US midterm elections
World.content:
Through statements in English, Iranian officials are emphasising gas prices and issues with the US economy.

In messages that appear to be directed at the American public, Iran has been highlighting the cost of the war that the United States and Israel launched against the country ahead of the United States midterm elections.

Iranian officials have published articles in state-affiliated outlets stressing the disastrous impact of the war on oil prices and the US economy, while Iran’s chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has actively targeted US officials about rising costs and military spending.

Sina Toossi, a senior non-resident fellow at the Center for International Policy, said Tehran is looking to increase the political cost of the war for Trump by trying to talk directly to the American public.

“It’s not necessarily that they’re trying to get Democrats in power or manipulate US politics in a certain direction, other than just overall increasing the costs on this issue of the Iran war, and just playing that game of information warfare and getting out their own narrative and propaganda as well,” Toossi told Al Jazeera.

Trump’s Republican Party is looking to retain control of the Senate and House of Representatives in next month’s midterm vote. But the Democratic Party, which largely opposes the war with Iran, is mounting a strong challenge across the congressional electoral map, including in areas that have been conservative strongholds for decades, such as Texas.

On Wednesday, Ghalibaf shared a news story on inflation rising to 3.7 percent last month along with a collage of negative headlines on the US economy.



The social media post also featured a comic strip from the Road Runner cartoon showing Wile E Coyote building a catapult that misfires and launches a boulder at him.

“Let’s ‘play the percentages’. Not in odds, but in the % increases,” Ghalibaf wrote in a message to US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has been leading the sanctions campaign against Iran.

Bessent said last month that he represents “the house”, likening the economy to a casino while addressing the national debt and bond market.

Ghalibaf’s remark referred to the increase in inflation, underscoring that the cost of living keeps rising due to the war despite Bessent’s assertions.

Days earlier, he shared an image of a ghost shaped like a bell curve, with diesel prices rising and housing affordability and consumer confidence falling.

Since the start of the war on February 28, Iran has disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, sending energy prices soaring. In the US, the price of diesel is at an all-time record of $6.33 per gallon (3.8 litres), according to the American Automobile Association, and gas is $4.33, up from less than $3 before the war.

Iran has intensified its attacks on vessels around the strait in recent days after Trump and his aides repeatedly stressed that the waterway is under US control.

The uptick in energy prices has fuelled overall inflation in the economy, leading the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates last month at a time when Trump has been calling for them to be cut to stimulate economic activity.

In a letter to the American public on September 29, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) accused Trump of lying about the cost of the war and the state of the US economy, dismissing the president’s claims that oil prices would soon nosedive.

“Countries around the world have lost their faith in the US economy. Demand for American bonds has plummeted. In fact, countries are starting to offload their US bonds. Soon, the dam will break, and the economy will implode, causing, unfortunately, great pain for Americans for many many years,” the IRGC said.

“Americans need to wake up. They need to wrest control back from corrupt politicians. Now is the time, as the American political system is at its weakest.”

The US midterm elections are seen as a turning point in the conflict – not because of their potential outcome, but because of what Trump might do after the vote.



Trump has suggested that he would either strike a deal with Iran or return to a full-scale war after the November 3 legislative elections. He has also dismissed the idea that the vote will have any impact on his Iran policy.

“They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election. What they don’t realise is that I’m not running,” Trump said at the United Nations General Assembly last month.

“I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence to the election. When it comes to Iran, it doesn’t even enter my mind. The only thing that does is that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.”

If the Democrats gain control of Congress, they can push for measures to curb Trump’s ability to continue the war, including through withholding funding for the military campaign.

But Toossi said there is a debate within Iran on the potential impact of a Democratic victory in November.

While some point to foreign policy hawks among the Democrats to argue that little would change, others say a midterm defeat would make him politically vulnerable and likely constrain his war powers.

“I don’t think they’re hedging their bets either way, and I don’t think it necessarily affects their overall strategy of increasing the costs [of war] regardless of whatever happens in November,” Toossi told Al Jazeera.

World.title: Ukraine president targets Trump, Putin at EU summit
World.content:
NewsFeed Ukraine president targets Trump, Putin at EU summit

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Russia’s ambitions extend beyond eastern Ukraine, saying its drone attacks threaten NATO. Speaking after an EU summit in Belgium, he also took a jibe at US President Donald Trump for saying he is harder to deal with than Putin.

World.title: US records 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows
World.content:
The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has recorded 4,410 measles cases so far in 2026, an increase of 330 in a week, and has dispatched an investigator to the state of Pennsylvania to help contain the country’s largest outbreak.

CDC figures also show 451 measles-related hospitalisations nationwide this year. Children and teenagers aged five to 19 account for 42 percent of cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older, who make up 41 percent. Seventeen percent of cases were among children under the age of five.

Pennsylvania reported 1,222 cases across 42 counties as of Wednesday, including 86 new infections since October 9, according to the state health department. The outbreak has led to 225 hospitalisations and five confirmed measles-associated deaths. State officials are actively investigating a sixth reported death.

The CDC is sending a so-called “disease detective” from its Epidemic Intelligence Service to work with state health officials on the Pennsylvania outbreak. The deployment follows Pennsylvania’s request for federal assistance, known as an Epi-Aid.

Pennsylvania has expanded vaccination efforts in affected communities. State health centre staff have administered more than 5,900 measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine doses at 202 pop-up clinics since the outbreak began in late April.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on October 5 as measles cases rose in nearby Pennsylvania. The order is effective until November 4 and expands the number of healthcare professionals authorised to administer vaccines and allows nurses greater flexibility to order measles testing.



Measles vaccination coverage among US kindergarteners fell from 95.2 percent in the 2019–2020 school year to 92.4 percent in 2025–2026, according to data from the CDC. The agency estimates that about 280,000 kindergarteners are at risk because of gaps in vaccination coverage.

World.title: Ukraine advances in occupied Donetsk as Trump hands Putin diesel deal
World.content:
Ukraine’s ‘Operation Vivaldi’ reclaimed more occupied territory in Donetsk during a week when Trump sided with Russia.

The United States’s relationship with Ukraine came under extraordinary strain during the past week, as US President Donald Trump lifted some oil sanctions against Russia and was feared to have restricted Ukraine’s access to US intelligence and satellite services, hobbling its defences.

“It is a pity we are losing … a strong partner,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalist Piers Morgan, speaking of the US.

“It’s painful when President Trump chooses one side, not our side,” he said. “This is not [the] right side of history.”

Trump on October 9 invited Russia to sell 1.8 million tonnes of diesel to the global market by the end of the year, to help bring down transport prices.

That effectively reversed the Lindsey Graham Act, which Trump had signed into law days earlier. The law gave him the ability to punish countries buying Russian oil with secondary sanctions.

Ukraine’s partners did not share intelligence that five ballistic missiles were headed towards Kyiv on October 13, Zelenskyy said, without naming the US. Those missiles struck Kyiv’s Thermal Power Plant number 4, one of the capital’s biggest, resulting in power outages.

Russia then pounded Ukraine’s electricity infrastructure on October 14, when Ukraine reported it had restricted use of SpaceX’s satellite navigation services, which it uses to defend itself.

Over a 24-hour period, Russia launched 850 drones and 39 missiles, striking 30 energy targets across 19 regions of Ukraine, despite the fact that Trump had declared an energy ceasefire on October 11.



“This level of blatant disregard for the United States by Russia has not been seen before,” Zelenskyy said.

Starshield, the military element of the Starlink satellite network owned by SpaceX, capped Ukraine’s use of its navigation services at 160 km/h (100mph).

This meant that Ukraine lost sight of its interceptors above that speed, making it difficult or impossible to stop Russian jet-powered Geran-4 drones, which fly at speeds exceeding 500 km/h (310mph).

Six in 10 Russian drones are now jet-powered, Zelenskyy said.

“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” wrote SpaceX owner Elon Musk.

Starshield services had begun to return to normal on October 15, sources at Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence said.

Ukraine is so heavily targeted by Russian aerial strikes that an outage in its ability to navigate interceptors for a prolonged period could be ruinous.

During September, its air force intercepted more than 4,700 drones and missiles of various kinds.

Starshield is equally important for Ukraine’s ability to hobble Russian offensive operations. Ukraine has wrought havoc with Russian supply lines for months, striking fuel trucks, bridges, ammunition warehouses and air defences.

During September alone, Ukraine’s military said it had struck 40 command posts and 50 logistics facilities.

The Unmanned Systems Forces of Ukraine’s data showed that strikes fell from a daily average of 2,300 to 1,678 on October 14 and 1,053 on October 15.

This was not the first such disruption of services under the Trump administration.

The US had also stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine in March, helping Russia reclaim its Kursk region, which Ukraine had counter-invaded.

Ukraine advances

Despite the setbacks this week, Ukraine has continued to win back territory.

Its Third Army Corps concluded a fourth phase of Operation Vivaldi in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region, reclaiming an additional 100sq km of territory (40sq miles), said Corps commander Andrii Biletskyi.

That brought the operation’s gains to 275sq km (100sq miles) and 16 settlements since August, and brought Russia’s overall gains this year close to nil.

The campaign was designed to push back against a Russian effort to seize the town of Lyman. A separate counteroffensive further south pushed back against an attempted Russian takeover of Dobropillya. Ukraine saw the two initiatives as an effort to surround the “fortress cities” of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk in a pincer movement.



Ukraine’s counteroffensives have drawn away Russian units directly facing Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, paralysing this part of the front.

“Russian forces averaged around 14 attacks per day in the Sloviansk direction in August 2026, five in September 2026, and three per day thus far in October 2026,” wrote the Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank.

“Russian forces averaged around three attacks per day in the Kramatorsk direction in August 2026, one in September 2026, and only an average of 0.3 thus far in October 2026,” the ISW said.

“We are stopping all enemy attempts to advance or infiltrate,” said Zelenskyy. “Ukraine’s positions on the front remain strong, and this year they are the strongest they have been in a long time.”

Zelenskyy said Russian forces outnumber Ukraine’s by six to eight times in parts of the front, and it appeared that they have recently received reinforcements.

Robert Brovdi, the commander of the Unmanned Systems Forces of Ukraine, said the personnel increase “translates into a significant increase” in Russian casualties.

During the first two weeks of October, Brovdi said, Russian casualties increased by 25 percent compared with the first two weeks in September and by almost 60 percent compared with the first two weeks in August.

In Dobropyllia, the Russian casualties were higher than anywhere else on the front, he said, 43 percent above September’s rate and double the rate in August.

Ukraine’s success is due in part to its production of domestically designed drones in partnership with European allies.

Ukraine’s Defence Ministry’s orders in 2026 were higher by half than in 2025, it said, and delivery volumes were almost four times what they had been last year.

While Ukraine respected Trump’s energy ceasefire for three days, it returned to striking Russian refineries on October 15.

It also continued to strike non-energy targets throughout the week.

Ukraine struck a facility manufacturing explosives and rocket fuel in Nizhny Novgorod on October 9, and a plant making additives for missile fuels in the Tver region.

On October 15, it destroyed four Sukhoi fighters and damaged another two at the Borisoglebsk airfield in the Voronezh region.

Ukraine also targeted three data centres owned by the Russian cloud services company Yandex, destroying or crippling those in Sasovo, Kaluga and Vladimir between October 8 and 11. It also struck a data centre owned by Sberbank on October 14.

The strikes caused Russians to lose online payment and other services.

World.title: Real Madrid demand resignation of La Liga chief after Goebbels comparison
World.content:
La Liga President Javier Tebas under fire for comparing Real Madrid TV channel to Nazi Germany’s Minister of Propaganda.

Share Real Madrid demand resignation of La Liga chief after Goebbels comparison on social media

Real Madrid are demanding the ‌‌resignation of La Liga President Javier Tebas after he compared rhetoric from ⁠⁠the club’s management ⁠⁠to the propaganda methods used by the Nazi Party in Germany.

Tebas wrote earlier on Friday on social media that “Real Madrid’s management directs an orchestra of ⁠⁠mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing”.

The LaLiga president was responding to articles by two journalists saying he and LaLiga were acting against Real’s interests.

Tebas added that the authors ⁠⁠in El Debate newspaper were amplifying a message on behalf of Real’s management.

Real Madrid’s demand for Tebas to immediately resign deepens a feud between the club and La Liga’s chief.

Last month, Real called for a new LaLiga president in response ‌‌to Tebas calling their complaints about refereeing decisions ‘a smokescreen’ for their shortcomings on the pitch.

Tebas on Friday criticised Real Madrid TV’s coverage of officiating at their matches.

“Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion and point fingers at the enemies,” he wrote.

“That method recalls propaganda mechanisms used by Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s Minister of Propaganda.

“The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with ⁠⁠an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase,” added ⁠⁠LaLiga’s president.

Real Madrid demand Tebas’s resignation as La Liga chief

Real Madrid released a statement later on Friday demanding that Tebas resign from his positions as LaLiga chief and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation.



The statement called it “intolerable and extraordinarily serious” that ⁠⁠Tebas used “a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television.

“Tebas’ repeated conduct ⁠⁠demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with ⁠⁠his institutional responsibilities,” said Real.

“It is unacceptable that he even takes advantage of questions, information or opinions from journalists unrelated to the club to direct his accusations at us, attributing to us actions of third parties for which ‌‌we bear no responsibility.”

The 64-year-old, who is elected by the 42 professional clubs in Spain’s top two tiers, has been La Liga president since 2013. In 2023, he was ‌‌re-elected ‌‌unopposed until 2027.

Real Madrid’s statement came hours after La Liga confirmed that they are one of the six clubs that will sit on the league’s Executive Committee this season.

World.title: Pope Leo to make public appearance Sunday, first since cancer surgery
World.content:
After undergoing lung surgery this week, pope can now ‘carry out normal daily activities ​with full independence’, say doctors.

Pope Leo XIV is making steady progress at the hospital after undergoing lung surgery earlier this week, according to his doctors, as the Vatican says he plans to appear before the public on Sunday.

The 71-year-old Catholic leader, who has been diagnosed with lung cancer, underwent an operation to remove part of his right lung on Tuesday.

He is now able to “carry out normal daily activities with full independence”, his doctors said in a medical update on Friday.

A blood test and chest X-ray earlier in the day confirmed his “steady improvement”, added the medical bulletin.

The update came as the Vatican shared the first images of Leo since his surgery, showing him celebrating mass and standing unaided in the Rome hospital where he is recovering.

The Vatican said Leo will deliver a traditional noontime prayer on Sunday, marking his first public appearance since the operation.

Preparations are also going ahead for his planned trip to South America in November, The Holy See added.

Leo’s cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy.

The Vatican did ⁠not say on Friday when the pontiff might be discharged from hospital, but previously indicated his recovery would take about a week.

The pope’s doctors have said his surgery was completed successfully, without complications. They have not yet disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis.



Chicago Cardinal Blase Cupich, seen as a close ally of ‌Leo, said he had been shocked by news of the cancer diagnosis.

He told Catholic magazine America he thought Leo had “downplayed” his health issue on Sunday, when the pope announced he needed surgery for a small, well-contained growth on his lung.

“When I heard they took ‌out ‌part of the lobe of the lung and that it was malignant, that was more shocking and more concerning,” said Cupich. “I think people are very concerned and even worried about this but hoping for the best.”

Leo is due to ⁠visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17. Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori had speculated that the trip might have to be delayed, ‌but in a sign that preparations were carrying on as normal, the Vatican released a list of journalists admitted to ‌cover ‌the visit.

Work on the trip is “going forward”, said a Vatican spokesman.

Leo also continued to work from the hospital on Friday, including speaking by phone with Russian President Vladimir Putin. During the call, the pope pushed for a ceasefire to allow aid and food into the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Vatican said.

World.title: Iran’s president condemns environmental impact of war in Middle East
World.content:
NewsFeed Iran’s president condemns environmental impact of war in Middle East

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has decried the ecological damage caused by conflict in the Middle East, calling it “environmental genocide.” He called for international solutions while addressing leaders at a UN biodiversity summit in Armenia.

World.title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role
World.content:
A Russian drone zips across the computer screen, startling the commanders keeping watch over the battlefield via a live stream in their bunker.

Cigarette in one hand, radio in the other, one of them calls in their own drone to bring it down and warns the soldiers below of the threat. The men are dangerously exposed, on the long walk across open ground from their front line positions. They are being replaced after three months forcing the Russians back.

This is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive which they say has liberated 277 sq km (106 square miles) in the eastern Donbas region in recent months.

The name reflects the offensive's four stages, or seasons - like the Italian composer's violin concerto. The successful assault blunted an attempted Russian pincer movement that threatened to encircle the key Fortress Belt cities still under Ukrainian control.

While Russia this month pummels Ukraine from the air, crippling its energy infrastructure and killing scores of civilians across the country, at the front, it is Ukraine that has made recent gains. Kyiv says it has inflicted heavy losses - 8,000 Russian casualties in Vivaldi alone, and close to 50,000 along the front in the month of September â and suffered few casualties in return.

World.title: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
World.content:
Dozens of masked settlers have attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank.

A BBC team witnessed one of several attacks in farmland near the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. A local official said the attacks had injured 12 Palestinians, including four dual Palestinian American citizens. A foreign journalist was also among those hurt.

Driving into the area early in the morning, we came across the first signs of the violence: a stream of cars carrying wounded Palestinian olive farmers racing out along the narrow stony track, piled high with olive picking equipment, as smoke rose from several fires nearby.

The bloodied face of Majdi Fheed peered out from the backseat of one car.

"We were getting our olive trees and almost 15 Jewish guys â¦ started attacking us with guns, with rocks, with special weapons. They hit me on my head [and] my neck â look, I am bleeding!"

Yaser AlKam, a council member from the neighbouring village of Turmus Aya told me Majdi - an American citizen - was attacked by settlers with nail-studded sticks, and needed treatment for deep wounds on his head. His elderly mother was also injured.

Another man ferrying the injured to hospital told us that settlers had attacked them with sticks while they harvested their olives, and had burned three cars â including one of his own.

"As soon as we got to the land and put our things on the ground, they started to come, so we ran away" said a woman next to him.

World.title: Zelensky says Ukraine has right to defend itself after Trump calls latest strikes a 'disgrace'
World.content:
President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he is "only standing up for Ukraine's interests" after scathing criticism from Donald Trump, who said Kyiv's new wave of strikes on Russian oil refineries was a "disgrace".

The US president, who recently made a controversial deal with Moscow to import diesel, also said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with than [Russian President Vladimir] Putin".

Zelensky, who has been angered by the diesel deal, said he could not accept it, because a gas agreement could come next. "If I don't stand up to this... who else will?" he said at an EU summit in Brussels.

Tensions between Washington and Kyiv have escalated over the diesel deal and curbs on Ukraine's battlefield satellite network.

Zelensky's trip to Brussels, following a visit to London, has come at the end of a bruising week. As he arrived at the summit on Friday, where EU leaders rallied around him in support, Zelensky said it was good to be back among allies. "Leaders, real leaders," he said, in a possible sleight to the US president.

At the summit, funding for Ukraine and helping it get through another freezing winter - its fifth since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 - topped the agenda.

The war will cost â¬155bn (Â£131bn; $174bn) next year, Zelensky told the European Council, with at least â¬70bn needed to come from the EU for defence and weapons.

Zelensky said that while Ukraine could produce up to three times more drones, it "simply [doesn't] have enough money for that".

A fundamental problem for Kyiv - which cannot be easily fixed - is the chronic lack of US-made Patriot missiles to defend its towns and cities.

Zelensky said he believed Europe did possess all the interceptors his country would need this winter but described them as being scooped up in a piecemeal fashion.

Zelensky also addressed Ukraine's frayed relationship with the US, saying there are "many people with good hearts in America" who want "to be allies, not to divide or humiliate Europe".

Trump has heavily criticised Zelensky for resuming strikes on Russian oil refineries earlier this week, because it could impact Moscow's ability to complete its part of the diesel deal, which will see 300,000 tonnes of diesel sent to "the American and global marketplace".

As both Russia and Ukraine continued attacking each other's energy infrastructure, Trump suddenly announced a ceasefire on the facilities last week.

Kyiv said it would stop the strikes if Russia did the same, but Moscow said it had never agreed to the deal and continued its attacks. After three days, Kyiv resumed its strikes.

World.title: Pope pictured for first time since surgery and cancer diagnosis
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been pictured celebrating Mass from hospital, in the first images of him released by the Vatican since he underwent lung surgery.

The 71-year-old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.

The images shared on Friday showed the Chicago-born Pope wearing a green robe while standing behind a makeshift altar on the tenth floor of the hospital.

Pope Leo "celebrated with the medical and nursing staff" and thanked workers for their service, the Vatican press office said.

World.title: India's 'cockroach' party founder detained ahead of protest
World.content:
Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of India's "cockroach" movement, and a few others were detained in Delhi as police tried to stop a protest demanding the resignation of the country's election chief.

Hundreds had gathered in Connaught Place, one of the capital's busiest commercial districts, waving Indian flags and shouting slogans despite a heavy security presence.

Police sealed off Central Park, the planned site of the protest, and deployed thousands of police and paramilitary personnel to prevent the gathering.

The Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) accuses India's Election Commission of manipulating voter lists to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling BJP. Both deny the allegation.

The group has held a series of protests in Delhi in recent weeks, with police repeatedly detaining its leaders and supporters. Friday's demonstration unfolded under similarly heavy security presence, though the police response was more restrained than during last weekend's sweeping crackdown.

Hours before the protest, police went to the house where Dipke was staying. In an exchange broadcast live on Instagram, he challenged officers who had come to caution him against holding the march, asking whether waving the Indian flag was against the law.

Hours later, the BBC saw officers surround Dipke as he approached his car and force him into a police vehicle. Some supporters tried to stop it from leaving.

It was Dipke's second detention in less than a week. Last Saturday, police had boarded his plane shortly after it landed in Delhi to prevent him from reaching another demonstration. He was released the following day.

The movement's two other main leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were also detained last weekend and later released. But on Wednesday, they were sent to jail for five days after returning to Jantar Mantar, a protest site near parliament that police had recently declared off-limits. Friday's march was partly intended to demand the release of Das and Ranka.

Dipke's detention means the movement's three main leaders are once again in custody.

The CJP said it had lost contact with him and accused police of taking him to an undisclosed location and denying him access to lawyers.

But they insist the arrests and detentions will not stop them. "They may detain three people, but how will they stop 30 tomorrow? How will they stop 300 leaders?" CJP spokesperson Mehr Pasricha told the BBC.

Police have not publicly confirmed the grounds for Dipke's detention or responded to the CJP's latest allegations.

Anish Gawande, the opposition politician who had been hosting Dipke, also questioned the police action.

"Detaining a lone man walking with the national flag in his hand is a bit of a joke," he said.

World.title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions
World.content:
A bipartisan group of US senators has signed a letter demanding an urgent investigation into disruptions to SpaceX's Starlink internet network in Ukraine.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said it had unexpectedly restricted how fast drones could fly while maintaining internet connection.

In the letter, sent to the US defence department inspector general, the senators express "grave concern" about reports of speed curbs between 12 and 14 October.

Asked whether the US might have had a role in the slowdown, a US official told the BBC "no such request was ever made by the president [Donald Trump]".

The letter, led by Jeanne Shaheen - a Democrat on the Senate's Foreign Relations Committee - calls for the inspector general to find out whether the restrictions were caused by the US defence department or its contractors.

It says "restrictions reportedly degraded Ukraine's ability to conduct defensive operations against Russian drone and missile attacks on civilian infrastructure".

Starlink, which is owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.

On Friday, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told a news conference in Brussels that Starlink services were still being restored in his country.

"Has the speed been fully restored to what it was before? No. Is the speed being restored now? Yes," he said.

The senators also say they are "deeply concerned" by reports of disruptions or "glitches" affecting intelligence-sharing and threat-warning capabilities relied upon by personnel operating in Ukraine.

"We are particularly alarmed by incidents in which U.S. diplomatic, military, and security personnel were unable to reach designated bunkers during Russian air raids," the statement says.

"Given the potentially deadly consequences, these incidents require immediate investigation," the senators add.

The letter's signatories include Republican Senators Thom Tillis, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and John Cornyn, alongside Senators Richard Durbin, Jack Reed, Richard Blumenthal and Christopher Coons from the Democrats.

World.title: Dad fined after son, 2, died in Cyprus hotel fall
World.content:
A father whose two-year-old boy fell from a fourth floor window of a Cyprus hotel has been fined â¬3,000 (Â£2,500) for causing his death.

Joshua Foster thought the window was closed when he placed his son on a sill to show him the view of a waterpark and "lost control" of him, Paphos District Court previously heard.

The toddler fell nearly 40ft (12.1m) at the five-star King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort on 12 July, the first day of the family's holiday in Chlorakas.

Foster, 37, from Essex, admitted causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act and was sentenced earlier.

He told reporters afterwards: "Thank you for the support. I'm looking forward to going home and being with my wife and daughter."

Later, the family said in a statement: "We are relieved that this process is now over, but for our family, the consequences of this tragedy will never end.

"Our son was deeply loved and will be forever missed. His loss is something we carry with us every day."

Foster, an auditor, arrived in Cyprus hours before the incident with his wife, two children and in-laws.

They enjoyed various activities and swimming, before getting ready for dinner in the evening.

World.title: Ship attack reports near Hormuz reach record high as oil exports slow
World.content:
The number of ships that have reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz has hit a record high, BBC Verify analysis of data from a UK maritime agency shows.

Twelve vessels were attacked between 5 and 11 October - the largest number of weekly strikes reported to the UK's Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency since the US-Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week saw 10 ships reporting attacks.

Six of the vessels were struck last Sunday, according to the UKMTO - a one-day high. So far this week, there have been four reported attacks.

As the number of strikes has risen, the recovery in oil shipments through the strait seen last month has slowed, industry data suggests.

BBC Verify collated incident reports published by the UKMTO on its website and created a timeline based on the first date cited in each report. This is approximate because some incidents use the date of the attack and some the date on which it was reported.

World.title: NUJ, Women’s Centre seek stronger media focus on gender-sensitive journalism
World.content:
The Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development has called for a structured partnership with the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), FCT Council, to strengthen journalists’ capacity to report women’s issues with greater accuracy, sensitivity and depth.

The Centre’s Director-General, Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi, made the call during a courtesy visit by the NUJ FCT Council, led by its chairperson, Grace Ike, to the Centre in Abuja.

Mrs Benjamins-Laniyi said journalists play a critical role in shaping public understanding of women’s development, advocating policies, and amplifying the experiences of women and girls.

She proposed periodic training sessions, media roundtables, and knowledge-sharing engagements to equip journalists with the skills and information needed to report on issues including women’s economic empowerment, leadership, gender-based violence, education, and social inclusion.

“Let us invest in the capacity of journalists to report gender issues responsibly and effectively,” she said.

According to her, the proposed partnership should move beyond expressions of goodwill to concrete commitments and measurable outcomes.

“As the 16th Director-General of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development, I extend a formal invitation to the NUJ FCT Council to become a strategic media partner in advancing the Centre’s mandate and strengthening the national movement for women’s empowerment,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She called for a formal media partnership framework to guide joint advocacy, public enlightenment, media engagement and the promotion of women-focused initiatives.

Mrs Benjamins-Laniyi also urged journalists to make women’s development a consistent part of national discourse rather than limiting coverage to occasions such as International Women’s Day.

She said issues affecting women should receive sustained attention across print, broadcast and digital platforms throughout the year.

The director-general further called for platforms that would give greater visibility to women entrepreneurs, rural women, young innovators, women with disabilities, community leaders and others whose contributions often receive limited public attention.

She proposed that the Centre and the NUJ designate focal persons to coordinate their engagement, identify priority activities and periodically review their progress.

“We should be able to look back at the end of each agreed period and point to specific achievements: programmes implemented, women reached, stories published, public awareness raised and opportunities created,” she said.

Mrs Benjamins-Laniyi said the partnership should also involve the media in shaping public conversations on women’s development, rather than merely inviting journalists to cover the Centre’s activities.

“The Centre has a mandate to empower women. The media has the power to amplify that mandate. Together, we can turn that power into progress,” she said.

Earlier, Mrs Ike said the NUJ FCT Council was visiting the Centre to declare a “partnership of purpose” focused on placing women’s stories, voices and contributions at the centre of national development.

Mrs Ike, the first female chairperson of the NUJ FCT Council, congratulated Mrs Benjamins-Laniyi on her appointment as the Centre’s 16th director-general and said the council was ready to collaborate with the institution.

She said Nigerian women had contributed significantly to the country’s families, economy, culture and democracy, but many of their contributions remained undocumented or poorly represented in the national narrative.

“Our theme is: Women in Journalism: Centring Women’s Stories, Voices and Contributions for National Development,” she said.

Mrs Ike said the media had a responsibility to amplify women’s voices, showcase their achievements, highlight challenges affecting them and promote conversations that advance equal opportunities and participation in national development.

She identified the Nigerian Women Hall of Fame, located within the Centre, as an important platform for preserving the contributions of Nigerian women.

She said the NUJ was willing to work with the Centre to document and tell women’s stories in a way that would inspire younger generations, particularly girls and young women.

The NUJ FCT chairperson also called for greater attention to grassroots women, rural women, women in informal employment, women with disabilities and young women whose contributions often receive little media attention.

She proposed regular features, interviews, and programmes on women’s leadership, enterprise, innovation, and community impact, as well as intergenerational dialogues involving veteran women leaders, emerging professionals, and young girls.

Other areas proposed by the NUJ include public conversations on women’s economic empowerment, digital inclusion, leadership, health, safety and rights, as well as joint capacity-building programmes for journalists on ethical and gender-sensitive reporting.

Mrs Ike said female journalists should also be given greater opportunities for professional development and leadership within the media industry.

She said journalists should ensure women are visible in reporting on governance, the economy, technology, security, education, health, climate change, culture, and other issues shaping Nigeria.

“Women are not merely beneficiaries of policy. They are experts, employers, innovators, caregivers, peacebuilders, taxpayers, voters, traders, farmers, researchers and leaders,” she said.

“Our reporting should connect women to information, opportunities, services and decision-making spaces. It should explain policies in clear language, expose barriers, highlight practical solutions and follow up on whether commitments improve women’s lives.”

Mrs Ike said the NUJ FCT Council would designate a liaison to coordinate its engagement with the Centre and commit to regular reporting on women’s contributions, development priorities and the implementation of policies affecting women.

She also proposed a follow-up meeting between both institutions to develop a realistic programme of joint activities.

The two institutions agreed that sustained collaboration between the media and the Centre could help amplify women’s voices, improve public understanding of women-focused policies and strengthen accountability for programmes designed to improve the lives of women and girls.

World.title: From 95,000 to 60,000 Pilgrims: How Nigeria lost Hajj seats, as citizens raise concerns
World.content:
For decades, Nigeria had some of the largest contingents in Saudi Arabia for the Hajj, the annual Muslim pilgrimage.

But within two Hajj cycles, the number of pilgrims fell sharply, leaving thousands facing the prospect of postponing a religious obligation they may have spent years preparing for.

The story, however, is more complicated than Saudi Arabia’s reduction of the country’s slots.

The slide from 95,000

Nigeria was allocated 95,000 slots for the 2025 Hajj. By May 2025, only about 64,188 pilgrims had registered, while fewer than 60,000 eventually travelled to Saudi Arabia through the government and licensed private tour operators.

In 2026, the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON) secured spaces for about 52,000 pilgrims, but fewer Nigerians still eventually travelled.

Several factors led to this situation, including late registration and payment by intending pilgrims, difficulties completing payments, delays in remitting funds, and the closure of the Saudi visa portal.

Saudi Arabia subsequently reduced Nigeria’s actual Masha’ir spaces for 2026 to 66,910, but the operational quota fell to 50,000.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

NAHCON repeatedly warned pilgrims and state pilgrims’ welfare boards to respect registration and payment deadlines.

Every underutilisation of allocations subsequently became an issue in Nigeria’s Hajj planning, with Saudi authorities reducing the number of Mashair spaces for the following cycle.

Some Nigerians who registered and paid for the 2025 Hajj could not travel, particularly those affected by the closure of the Saudi visa portal.

NAHCON said the visa issuance window closed, affecting 2,717 late-registration pilgrims, despite the Commission’s efforts to secure further extensions.

The Commission then began reconciling and refunding affected pilgrims.

By September 2025, NAHCON said it had reconciled refunds involving 19 states that had requested reconciliation.

The experience exposed the importance of completing registration, payment, biometric and visa processes within the deadlines set by both Nigeria and Saudi Arabia.

New NAHCON leadership

With the coming of the new NAHCON Chairman, Isma’il Abba-Yusuf, the Commission made early preparation a priority, consistently urging intending pilgrims to register and pay early while calling on state pilgrims’ welfare boards to intensify enlightenment campaigns.

NAHCON has also stressed the need for pilgrims and state authorities to understand and comply with new Saudi regulations, particularly the increasingly technology-driven Hajj process.

The emphasis on early registration and compliance was evident ahead of the 2027 Hajj.

Nigeria subsequently secured an additional 10,000 slots, raising its allocation from 50,000 to 60,000 pilgrims.

The development follows sustained discussions between NAHCON and Saudi authorities and provides more space for Nigerian pilgrims, while also placing greater responsibility on the Commission and state authorities to ensure the available slots are fully utilised.

From Arabi to Usman, then Yusuf

The contrast with the 2024 Hajj administration under Jalal Arabi is significant.

Under Mr Arabi, NAHCON completed visa processing and other preparations ahead of the airlift and moved Nigerian pilgrims efficiently through the Hajj operation.

But the administration ended amid an EFCC investigation into alleged mismanagement of the N90 billion 2024 Hajj intervention fund provided by the federal government.

Mr Arabi was subsequently removed by President Bola Tinubu.

Abdullahi Usman, a professor, succeeded him, but his tenure was marked by internal disagreements and controversies.

He resigned in February 2026 amid the crisis.

Ismail Yusuf, a former diplomat, subsequently took over, inheriting a commission facing not only internal restructuring but also a radically changing Saudi Hajj management system.

The pilgrims’ frustration

When PREMIUM TIMES spoke to some Nigerians, the concerns were shared across the country

Hassan Mohammed, who lives in Kaduna, said Nigeria should have done more to ensure that its traditional allocation was fully utilised.

“The painful part is that we had the opportunity to use the seats. We should not have allowed thousands of allocations to go unused,” he said.

Almustapha Ahmed, a Sokoto resident, said the reduction would particularly affect families that had spent years preparing financially for Hajj.

“Hajj is not something people decide to do overnight. Families save for years. When the allocation disappears, ordinary Nigerians bear the consequences.”

Rafiu AbdulRauf, who spoke from Oyo State, questioned whether NAHCON and state authorities acted early enough when the warning signs emerged.

“NAHCON and the states should have anticipated that Saudi Arabia would look at utilisation. The warning signs were already there.”

Garba Mukhtar, an indigene of Yobe State, said Nigeria must improve its administrative preparation.

“We cannot continue with late registration, late payments and administrative bottlenecks and then expect Saudi Arabia to keep reserving spaces for us.”

AbdulWahab Isiaka, who resides in Lagos, raised concerns about the growing political influence around Hajj administration.

“The political interest surrounding Hajj must not become more important than the pilgrim. The person paying for Hajj should be at the centre of every decision ” Mr Isiaka said.

But the concerns extend beyond the reduction.

Nigerians also want greater accountability over how allocations are distributed, how pilgrims are selected and how private operators are regulated.

Saudi Arabia’s new rules

Saudi Arabia is transforming Hajj administration through technology.

Pilgrim data, biometrics, visas, accommodation, transport and other services are increasingly being synchronised through digital platforms, including Nusuk-Masar.

The new system leaves less room for administrative delays. Missed deadlines, incomplete data, or failure to synchronise pilgrims’ information can result in lost spaces.

Saudi Arabia is also encouraging private operators to take on a greater role. Under the emerging model, NAHCON would increasingly serve as regulator and monitor, while licensed companies handle more operational responsibilities.

That transition could improve efficiency, but it also raises questions about consumer protection, pricing and accountability.

Can Ambassador Yusuf reverse the decline?

Mr Yusuf came in at perhaps the most consequential period in NAHCON’s history. His recent reforms have focused on early planning, digitalisation, transparency and professionalising Hajj operations.

He has also engaged Saudi authorities over Nigeria’s reduced allocation and sought additional places for Nigerian pilgrims.

Nevertheless, diplomacy alone may not restore the lost quota.

READ ALSO: NAHCON pushes sustainable Hajj fund management digital transformation at global forum

Nigeria must show it can register pilgrims early, pay on time, provide accurate data, and use every seat allocated to it.

The bigger question

Nigeria’s Hajj crisis is therefore not simply a story of 95,000 seats becoming 60,000. It is a story of a changing Saudi system, declining utilisation, administrative weaknesses, political interference and the urgent need for institutional reform.

For Mr Yusuf, the challenge is to restore confidence in NAHCON and ensure that Nigeria never again loses valuable Hajj opportunities because of avoidable failures.

For the Nigerian pilgrim, the demand is simpler: if Saudi Arabia gives a seat, Nigeria must ensure it is occupied.

World.title: United Nigeria Airlines plans N20 billion commercial paper issuance
World.content:
United Nigeria Airlines said it intends to raise N20 billion through commercial paper, which it described as the first of its kind by a domestic airline in Nigeria, as it seeks to strengthen its finances and fund expansion.

The proposed issuance is the first tranche of a N100 billion commercial paper programme, and will comprise two series with tenors of 270 and 364 days, according to a statement by the airline’s management on Friday.

Commercial paper is a short-term debt instrument companies use to raise funds for working capital and other business needs. Unlike equity financing, it involves borrowing that must be repaid based on agreed terms.

According to the airline, the proposed issuance is part of its strategy to strengthen its financial position while expanding operations across domestic, regional, and international markets.

Meristem Capital Limited will serve as the lead arranger, while Cordros Advisory Services Limited, Coronation Merchant Bank Limited, FCMB Capital Markets Limited, FSL Advisory Limited and Quantum Zenith Capital and Investments Limited will act as dealers.

United Nigeria Airlines said it has obtained credit ratings from two agencies for the proposed issuance.

According to the airline, Agusto & Co. assigned it an A3 short-term rating and a BBB- long-term rating, both with a stable outlook. DataPro assigned the airline an A1 short-term rating and a BBB long-term rating.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The ratings provide investors with an assessment of the airline’s creditworthiness, although they do not guarantee repayment or eliminate the risks associated with investing in the commercial paper.

The airline’s September 2026 investor presentation showed substantial growth in its financial performance over the past five years.

Revenue rose from N10.3 billion in 2021 to N90.8 billion in 2025, while profit after tax increased from N1.3 billion to N23.8 billion over the same period.

The company reported revenue of N95.6 billion in the first half of 2026.

It also said turnover rose to N19.4 billion in August from N14.1 billion in July, and it recorded a net profit of N1.2 billion in August.

The airline said it expects its financial performance to continue improving.

Fleet expansion planned

The airline said it currently operates ten aircraft, comprising Embraer ERJ-145s, Boeing 737-800s, Embraer E190S and CRJ900s, adding that it plans to take delivery of six additional aircraft before the end of the year.

United Nigeria Airlines serves fourteen destinations across Nigeria and Ghana, and said it has secured approval to operate as a flag carrier to six international destinations.

The planned fleet expansion is expected to support its efforts to increase capacity and extend its reach beyond the domestic market. However, the scale and timing of the expansion will depend on the airline’s ability to secure the necessary financing, take delivery of additional aircraft and meet applicable regulatory requirements.

The airline has also taken steps to expand its access to international travel distribution networks.

The company says it has signed agreements with Amadeus and Sabre, systems travel agents and other travel service providers use to access airline schedules and ticket inventory.

In April, United Nigeria Airlines joined the International Air Transport Association’s Multilateral Interline Traffic Agreement, which provides a framework for airlines to cooperate on passenger bookings and connections across their networks.

In June, the airline became a full member of the African Airlines Association, a continental body that promotes cooperation and the development of Africa’s aviation industry.

World.title: Tinubu nominates four new INEC National Commissioners, two Resident Electoral Commissioners
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has nominated four new national commissioners and two new resident electoral commissioners to fill vacancies at the Independent National Electoral Commission created by expiring tenures.

The Senate will scrutinise all the nominees.

However, the president reappointed Bala Bila, the national commissioner representing the North East.

The new national commissioners are Mustapha Aliu, who will replace Abdullahi Zuru as the North West representative; and Bashir Muhammed Umar, who will replace Muhammad Adamu as the North Central representative.

President Tinubu recommended Oluwatoyin Babalola, the resident electoral commissioner in Osun, as the new South West national commissioner. She will replace Cornelius Ajayi, whose tenure expires on 24 October.

The two new resident electoral commissioners are retired permanent secretary Samuel Akinleye, to represent Ekiti State, and Zahradden Sanusi, from Jigawa, who will replace Saidu Babura.

President Tinubu urged the Senate to expedite the nominees’ confirmation in view of the forthcoming general elections next January.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information and Strategy)

16 October 2026

World.title: Samsung Introduces Galaxy Tab S12 Series: The ultimate productivity powerhouse built for growth
World.content:
Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. has unveiled the Galaxy Tab S12 series — Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Tab S12+ — delivering Samsung’s most capable and versatile tablet experience yet. Packing breakthrough performance, long-lasting battery life, and the latest Galaxy AI into Galaxy Tab’s signature ultra-thin design, the new lineup turns complex workflows into effortless, everyday achievements whether it’s mastering skills, pursuing career goals or exploring creative passions.

Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Tab S12+ feature immersive displays and come bundled with the ergonomically designed S Pen for effortless note-taking and precise editing. With easy access to professional-grade apps and versatile accessories, users can pursue their passions and progress toward their goals with ease.

Combining portability with professional-grade power, the Galaxy Tab S12 series gives users instant access to powerful capabilities whenever inspiration strikes.

According to Lucas Lee, CEO Samsung Electronics West Africa, “The Galaxy Tab S12 series is made for purpose-driven individuals seeking tablet devices that match their ambition”.

Peak Performance in an Ultra-Thin Design

The Galaxy Tab S12 series combines powerful performance and long-lasting battery life into a thin and light design, making it easy for users to achieve more, wherever ambition takes them. At a remarkably slim 5.1mm, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is Samsung’s thinnest Galaxy Tab, while delivering the most powerful performance of any Galaxy Tab to date, supporting productive use throughout the day. For example, users taking an online course alongside a full-time job can catch up on a lesson during the commute, then work through course exercises on the large screen at a café or library later in the day.

Both models are built to go the distance, allowing users to keep going without losing momentum. On a single charge, the all-day battery lasts up to 23 hours on Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and up to 21 hours on Galaxy Tab S12+, supporting long stretches of productivity anywhere. When it is time to recharge, the battery goes from 0% to 100% in about 95 minutes with the 45W adapter — minimizing downtime so users can get back to what they were doing.

Beyond long-lasting battery life, the Galaxy Tab S12 series delivers the most powerful performance of any Galaxy Tab to date, keeping pace with even intensive tasks. The cutting-edge 3nm processor delivers up to 61% faster NPU processing, 19% faster CPU performance and 17% improved GPU power compared to Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra. In everyday use, that means users can take on more demanding tasks with increased speed and responsiveness. Whether rendering complex creative projects or watching a lecture while taking notes and asking AI for clarification — the experience stays responsive and fast with fewer interruptions to break their focus.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A newly designed 3D Vapor Chamber efficiently dissipates heat to support more reliable performance during demanding tasks, whether users are editing video or designing graphics for hours. Engineered for resilience and durability to withstand the elements and give users peace of mind, the Galaxy Tab S12 series also comes with IP68-rated water and dust resistance.

The Galaxy Tab S12 series comes with an expansive screen designed to help users think bigger and give ideas more room to unfold. Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra features a large 14.6-inch display, making it easy to explore complex topics andkeep multiple perspectives in view. The Galaxy Tab S12+ features a larger 12.6-inch display and slimmer bezels than its predecessor, offering more screen space without sacrificing portability. Both models feature Dynamic AMOLED 2X displays reaching up to 1,600 nits of peak brightness — delivering clear, vivid visuals indoors or out. The upgraded seamless Vision Booster now adjusts brightness in real time based on lighting conditions for comfortable viewing.

Sound gets a major upgrade as well, with 4-channel spatialaudio — twice as many channels as the previous generation — delivering a richer, more immersive experience whether users are streaming content, following a tutorial or editing.

Making Everyday Tasks More Intuitive and Effortless

Building on an industry-leading hardware foundation, the Galaxy Tab S12 series turns its large screen into a flexible workspace that makes it easy to keep up with different tasks without missing a beat. Running Android 17 with One UI 9and the latest Galaxy AI, it brings research, note-taking, creation and AI assistance into one place, giving users more freedom to explore new ideas, capture what matters and put what they learn into practice.

Thanks to the Galaxy Tab S12 series’ immersive screen, users can split the screen into up to three sections in Multi Window layout. For example, users can take notes in Samsung Notes on one side while playing a lecture and opening an AI assistant on the other. As key takeaways or questions come up, users can capture them with the S Pen directly in Samsung Notes, while Note Assist summarizes their notes – all without pausing the lecture.

Both models come bundled with an ergonomic S Pen, offering precise, intuitive input for note-taking, annotating materials, and sketching concepts. For a more structured, professional workstation, the Book Cover Keyboard Slimdelivers flexibility with comfortable viewing angles and an effortless typing experience.

The Galaxy Tab S12 series helps users bring information together and get real-time support the moment curiosity strikes. The Galaxy Tab S12 series comes equipped with a six-month trial of Google AI Pro, providing expanded access to Google’s most capable AI models from day one. Users can ask Gemini about anything unclear or dive deeper into subjects they want to explore the moment a question comes up. With Gemini Notebook, users can bring together notes, images, recordings, and files in one workspace and create summaries, podcasts, and even quizzes to make key information easier to understand.

As exploration expands into deeper research, Samsung Browser helps users stay focused without losing track of what they have already discovered. By understanding webpage content, context across multiple tabs, and browsing history, it can summarize information across open pages or surface a relevant source viewed days earlier – helping users spend less time searching through past tabs and more time capturing the key insights that matter most.

A Complete Ecosystem Designed to Take Skills and Creativity Further

The Galaxy Tab S12 series gives users the ideal place to put knowledge into practice, bringing together professional-gradeapps alongside other benefits to help them take their skills further.

Adobe Photoshop comes pre-loaded on the Galaxy Tab S12 series — a first for Android tablets — bringing pro-grade image editing and design to the tablet. The interface is optimized for tablets, and S Pen support makes it more intuitive to move ideas from hand to screen. Photoshop includes AI-powered features including AI Assistant and generative AI features powered by Adobe Firefly like Generative Fill and Image to Video, helping creatives edit faster and effortlessly. Exclusively for the Galaxy Tab S12 series, users receive four months of free access to the Photoshop mobile plan.

Notability, newly pre-loaded on Galaxy Tab, helps users capture their ideas, organize notes and build knowledge more efficiently with S Pen optimization and AI-driven study tools with a six-month free trial, plus 20% off the first subscription. Goodnotes delivers clean note-taking and organization with one year of free access and LumaFusionenables professional-grade video editing, offered at a 66% discount. And Notion supports flexible writing, planning and organization with one month of its Plus plan free. Clip Studio Paint brings precision drawing and painting tools for digital art with a six-month trial and 20% off the first subscription.

In addition to these apps, users can explore a broader range of options that support different needs.

MyScript Mathinstantly solves handwritten equations and shows the steps behind each one, while MyScript Notes summarizes handwritten notes into study materials with built-in AI tools to explain concepts or generate quizzes. Noteshelf 3 offers customizable layouts for capturing and organizing ideas, while ArcSite converts rough field sketches into precise CAD drawings.

Availability

The Galaxy Tab S12 series will be available from Oct. 14 at Samsung Experience Stores, authorized dealers, and partner retailers nationwide. The devices will be offered in two colors, Gray and Silver.

Built for lasting and confident use, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+ support up to seven times of OS upgrades and security updates.

For added peace of mind, Samsung Care+ offers comprehensive coverage tailored to users’ device needs, including fast repairs for accidental damage, extended warranty, and certified expert support available both at home and abroad. Additionally, Galaxy mobile phone users running One UI 9 can easily check the Samsung Care+ status of their Galaxy Tab and enroll through the Warranty and care menu in the Settings. It provides quick access to warranty information, self-diagnostics, repair requests, and remote support for connected devices—all directly from the mobile phone.

For additional information, visit Samsung.com.

Samsung inspires the world and shapes the future with transformative ideas and technologies. The company is redefining the worlds of TVs, digital signage, smartphones, wearables, tablets, home appliances and network systems, as well as memory, system LSI and foundry.
