World.title: Aircraft loses door mid-air, makes emergency landing in Abuja
World.content:
An aircraft operated by Triton Aviation made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on Thursday after its crew reported that a door had opened mid-air shortly after take-off.

The aircraft, a CL60 with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was departing Abuja for the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred.

According to a serious incident report, the aircraft took off from Runway 22 at 4:17 p.m. Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and, about three nautical miles from the airport, was climbing at 3,000 feet when the crew issued a distress call at 4:20 p.m.

The crew reported an open door in flight, prompting air traffic controllers to direct the aircraft back to Abuja for an emergency landing.

Airport fire and rescue personnel and the medical team were subsequently alerted and placed on standby in preparation for the aircraft’s return.

The incident report stated that at about 4:29 p.m. UTC, the crew asked the Abuja control tower to confirm whether the door was open.

The duty air traffic controller attempted to observe the aircraft with binoculars but could not establish the door’s condition because of the aircraft’s position.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The crew was informed that the controller could not visually confirm the situation.

The aircraft landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 4:34 p.m. UTC, about 14 minutes after the Mayday call.

After landing, the controller observed that the aircraft’s door was missing from the fuselage.

The aircraft was subsequently taxied to the international apron extension, where it was parked with the assistance of a marshaller.

Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media appears to show the aircraft’s missing door. In the footage, an unidentified man said some farmers found the door while returning from their farm in the Abuja area.

He suggested that it had fallen from an aircraft but did not provide further details about the discovery. The circumstances surrounding the reported discovery have not been independently verified as of the time of filing this report.

The cause of the incident and the circumstances surrounding the door’s detachment have not been established.

The number of people on board is also not immediately available.

READ ALSO: Benin runway excursion not crash or emergency landing Enugu Air CEO

The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) confirmed that the incident occurred and said investigators have been deployed.

“Yes, it happened. The investigators are there. We will be releasing an official statement shortly,” the bureau’s media team said.

The Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Michael Achimugu, also confirmed the incident but said the NSIB has jurisdiction.

However, Triton Aviation could not be reached for comment when this report was filed.

World.title: Fintech firm Onafriq to close Nigeria agent banking business
World.content:
Fintech firm Onafriq Nigeria Payments Limited has announced it will wind down its Nigerian agent banking business, Baxi, and refocus on pan-African payments.

In a statement on Friday, the company cited macroeconomic headwinds such as inflation and currency depreciation as key factors affecting trading volumes and operating costs and undermining the sustainability of its offline agent banking model.

South Africa-based Onafriq, with a footprint in Morocco, Mali, Kenya, and Tanzania among others, entered the Nigerian agent banking market in 2021 when it acquired the Baxi business (also known as Capricorn Digital Limited) and invested heavily through 2023 to strengthen and scale its agent network.

Operating conditions changed significantly for the firm beginning in 2024, with a sharp depreciation of the naira and broader macroeconomic pressures dramatically impacting its operations.

A rapid growth of instant account-to-account payments simultaneously changed the mix of transactions at agents’ POS.

According to Onafriq, increased competition in this segment, coupled with associated margin compression, further strained the business.

After reviewing its long-term strategy and the business’s sustainability, the group concluded that winding down the agent banking operation is the way to go.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We entered Nigeria with conviction and commitment, but did not achieve the outcome we set out for. Closing this business was a difficult decision to arrive at, one that affects colleagues, agents, and business partners across Nigeria who poured their hearts and soul into building out the Baxi network,” Dare Okoudjou, founder and CEO of Onafriq, said

“We are committed to honesty, fairness, and a well-managed transition for everyone impacted. Nigeria remains central to our mission, and we will continue to serve the market as a Payment Solution Service Provider through the Onafriq payments network and our card issuing services,” he added.

The closure will only affect employees whose roles are connected to the agent banking business. The company said every affected employee will be consulted, treated fairly, and supported through the transition.

Onafriq said agents onboarded via the Baxi payments platform have been transitioned to another principal bank, and it has asked them to transfer their funds to their preferred principal bank within 30 days.

“Onafriq’s teams are available to provide support and guidance throughout the process. The company will continue to honour its commitments to affected stakeholders and communicate openly during the transition,” the company said.

It added that the decision affects only its agent banking business in Nigeria and does not represent an exit from the Nigerian market.

“Onafriq Group remains strong, with continued growth across its cross-border payments network and card issuing services,” it said.

World.title: Bola Ahmed Tinubu: The most consequential president, By Jibrin Ibrahim
World.content:
This morning, we are at the public presentation of the book – Tinubu: From Renewed Hope to Despair; written by Abubakar Siddique Mohammed, Aliyu Sanusi, Alkasum Abba and Massoud Omar. The event was supposed to have taken place yesterday at Arewa House, Kaduna, a research institute run by Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. Due to “pressures from above”, the university cancelled the booking. The organisers then went around other hotels in Kaduna but they shut their doors claiming they had been warned. That is the state of our democracy today as civic space is closed down. Undaunted, the organisers decided to “bombard the headquarters”. As they closed doors in the provinces, they opted to go to the headquarters and have the event in Yar’Adua Centre. They have an important story to tell about our President, Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Bola Ahmed Tinubu is in a keen contest with Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida (IBB) in the race as the most consequential president in Nigeria’s post-independence history. He is in a keen contrast with his predecessor Muhammadu Buhari, the General that lived in Aso Rock for eight years but did not even try to govern the country. As I said on many occasions under the Buhari Presidency, when the president refuses to govern, others govern in his name because as we all know, there is no vacuum in politics. IBB had a profound effect on the culture of politics and statecraft in Nigeria but I doubt that his impact could have been as deep and profound as Tinubu’s. Do not take me up on my words, read the book that is being presented to the Nigerian public today and as the saying goes, one reading will convince you.

Tinubu’s claim, (and please don’t ask me the justification), is that it was his turn to govern Nigeria and many people assumed that he wanted to enjoy the excellent cuisine and soothing spirits of Aso Rock. I am an Ahmadu Bello University trained materialist in my methodology training so I know nothing about the world of sprits. For more on this matter of spirits, ask my good friend Dr Rueben Abati. Nigerians erroneously assumed he was there to enjoy his turn. What the country is realising today is that he came to change Nigeria by dismantling its democracy, disbanding federalism and establishing one-man rule. He did not start the process but he is working very hard to complete the job.

The Fourth Republic has been in place since 1999. Over that period, the country’s democratic process has been emptied of its essence. One way of understanding what happened to our democracy is to review how reckless political cabals have created a situation in which Nigeria faces a grave threat to its foundational constitutional principle of the separation of powers. Checks and balances between the branches of government have been imperilled. The separation of powers divides government responsibilities into three distinct branches—legislative (makes laws), executive (enforces laws), and judicial (interprets laws). This constitutional framework ensures a system of “checks and balances” that prevents tyranny, preserves individual liberties, and promotes governmental accountability.

Under President Tinubu, the legislative branch has been placed under near total control of the executive branch. The judiciary has lost both its independence and its integrity. The checks on the powers of the executive have been dismantled and he runs the government as he pleases without accountability or respect for the people’s welfare. Institutions have been compromised, weakened, and subordinated to the interests of the executive arm of government. This erosion of institutional independence has fuelled public distrust to its highest level in our history creating a crisis of political exclusion and impunity that is pushing violent extremism, organized crime, and communal conflict to a tipping point.

As Tinubu struggles to secure a second term to conclude his agenda of deepening the transition from “Hope to Despair”, it is important to understand his assets and skill set. While presidents from Shagari to Buhari had to rely on financiers and godfathers to finance their campaigns, Tinubu had the resources to fully fund his 2023 campaign himself and therefore had no stakeholders with voice in the system. Now that he owns the treasury, there is no cabal to bring some diversity and multiple voices to the table. There are only people who work for him at his pleasure. Our arrogance as democracy defenders that even the military dictatorships of Babangida and Abacha were stopped in their tracks of seeking to establish one-man rule is shattered by the reality of the iron-grip of the Tinubu control. I had written numerous articles in the past on how the National Assembly successfully fought off and gained its independence from the attempt to control them. Today, we have a National Assembly that is proud that it does not even discuss executive bills, it simply passes them without debate. Its only expectation is that it is well compensated financially.

The situation with the judiciary is worse. It has been undermined through corruption and for matters of no political relevance, the highest bidder wins automatically. When however, there is a political stake in a matter, the government position is the automatic winner. The Judiciary is complicit in dismantling the democratic process by its disregard for the rule of law. The Nigerian Bar Association that has a solid history in defending human rights and the rule of law has today lost its voice and raison d’etre.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The most serious problem confronting Nigerian democracy today is the active way the Tinubu Administration is using the powers of incumbency to ensure that there is no level playing ground for political parties. President Tinubu knows something about how opposition parties can come together, overcome their differences, create synergy around a single candidate, mobilise and defeat an incumbent president. He was a key player between 2013 and 2015, when opposition parties came together, negotiated, agreed on how the candidate would emerge and then went ahead to agree on a consensus candidate. The outcome of the consensus position that emerged was that for the first time in the history of this country, a sitting President was defeated at the polls and handed over power peacefully in 2015. Precisely because he knows the script, he has decided he is not going to sit and allow what he had done to another person be done to him.

The Tinubu political strategy since 2023 has been to apply slash-and-absorb tactics to opposition parties by actively encouraging factional crises within them and enticing key members to abandon ship and join the ruling party. This was not a sustainable tactic because there were limited positions within the ruling party, and giving the new entrants many goodies would mean depriving those within the party of these, which would become a crisis generating mechanism for the ruling party itself. This was indeed the context that encouraged opposition parties to strategize towards the establishment of a unified mega opposition platform to face the APC in the 2027 elections, the African Democratic Congress (ADC). By making opposition parties ungovernable, the ruling party assumes it can maintain its control until the elections. This cannot be guaranteed because there is a campaign and Tinubu is discovering today that there are too many negatives in his governance record so selling a second term might be impossible for the people who might abandon their leaders who had sold out.

The consequential impact of Tinubu rule is not only on our democracy. The book on Tinubu: From Renewed Hope to Despair provides detailed empirical analysis on destruction of our federal arrangement, national cohesion, lopsided infrastructural development, economic crisis and deepening poverty. Reading the book produces a constant chilling effect that there are no positives in Tinubu’s governing narratives, there are only negatives. Insecurity around the country has been spreading and deepening and the government’s only perspective seems to be to beg the Americans to come and solve our problems of insecurity. As security deteriorates, what is on offer is lopsided development. I had always been indignant at Buhari’s clannish approach to rule and ethnic favouritism.

The authors provide statistics showing federal appointments have today become the most lopsided in our country’s history. It does not stop there. Infrastructural projects are today concentrated in Lagos and the South West. Federal institutions are transferring key aspects of their organisational work to Lagos. The official policy appears to be to tear Nigeria at the seams. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s debt burden has been built to an unmanageable level. The numbers they provide tells the sad story of the policy reform that has multiplied levels of poverty and malnutrition in the country. While the government speaks of successful policy reform, what the people experience is the highest level of the development of misery. The authors draw attention to credible data sources that show universal policy reform failures.

Another consequence of Tinubu’s rule is the complete subordination of Nigeria’s interests to American hegemony. Since his inauguration, the President has been actively soliciting close ties and collaboration with the Americans. He has taken the option of succumbing to American imperialism at a historical moment when that crumbling hegemon is declining, indeed collapsing before our very eyes. We are becoming close friends with a country that recently acted as a brigand, sending a military force to kidnap President Nicolás Maduro of Venezuela and his wife. Why are we so close to a country that decided to completely wipe out the leadership of Iran to impose regime change only to find out that the Iranians do not tolerate hegemons but give them a sound beating.

A professor of Political Science and development consultant/expert, Jibrin Ibrahim is a Senior Fellow of the Centre for Democracy and Development, and Chair of the Editorial Board of PREMIUM TIMES.

World.title: FRC operated without board for over 13 years, nominee tells senate
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu’s nominee for chairman of the board of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Abdullahi Saidu, has told the Senate that the commission has operated without a board for more than 13 years, a situation he said has hindered its operations.

Saidu spoke on Wednesday when he appeared before the Senate Committee on Finance for screening alongside six other nominees.

He said the absence of a board had left the commission with significant institutional challenges, adding that the incoming board would have to rebuild its operations if confirmed.

Saidu said the commission was expected to establish offices in at least one location in each of the six geopolitical zones but currently operated only from Abuja.

He pledged to work with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to strengthen the commission and improve its capacity to discharge its mandate.

The nominee also disclosed that the commission lacked prosecutorial powers, explaining that it could investigate cases and forward its findings to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice for prosecution.

He said the proposed board would seek a review of the law establishing the commission to strengthen its independence and operational capacity.

Saidu further pledged to improve government revenue by strengthening the monitoring of operating surpluses generated by government-owned and other organisations covered by the commission’s mandate.

According to him, some revenue-generating organisations fail to remit the appropriate share of their operating surpluses to the Federal Government.

He said such organisations were expected to remit 80 per cent of their operating surpluses to the Consolidated Revenue Fund while retaining 20 per cent for their operations.

“Because the commission is not informed, so they just declare whatever they feel they want to declare,” he said.

Saidu assured the committee that, if confirmed, the board would strengthen monitoring to ensure that the appropriate revenues were declared and remitted.

He expressed confidence that the commission’s performance could improve within a year, provided it received the necessary support from the National Assembly and other stakeholders.

The screening was presided over by Senator Lere Oyewumi, vice-chairman of the committee, who represented its chairman, Senator Sani Musa.

Addressing the nominees, Oyewumi said managing the commission required specialised knowledge and preparation, noting that the assignment differed from other public service roles.

He urged them to participate in retreats with experts and undertake extensive reading to prepare for the responsibilities ahead.

Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West, moved a motion for Saidu and the other nominees to take a bow and leave, while Senator Sadiq Suleiman Umar, representing Kwara North, seconded the motion.

The other nominees screened alongside Saidu were Muhammad Asma’u, Muhammad Makama, Suleiman Gidado, Louis Ndukwe, Amechi Ugwele and Olaniyi Onikola.

The committee is expected to submit its report to the Senate for further legislative action.

World.title: 10 phones with 10,000mAh batteries or more
World.content:
Smartphones with 10,000mAh batteries or more are becoming an option for users who need extended battery life for gaming, streaming, outdoor activities and work on the go.

Unlike conventional smartphones, which often have batteries ranging from 4,000mAh to 6,000mAh, these devices offer substantially larger capacities that can reduce the need for frequent charging.

While most phones in this category are rugged devices designed for demanding environments, newer models are increasingly combining large batteries with features such as AMOLED displays, fast charging and 5G connectivity.

However, a larger battery often means a heavier and thicker phone. Buyers should also distinguish between models with exactly 10,000mAh batteries and those offering higher capacities.

Here are 10 smartphones with batteries rated at 10,000mAh or more.

1. REDMI Note 17 Pro Max 5G — 10,000mAh

The REDMI Note 17 Pro Max 5G is listed among the large-battery smartphones aimed at users who want extended battery life without choosing a rugged handset.

Its advertised specifications include a 10,000mAh battery, 100W fast charging, a 6.83-inch AMOLED display and 5G connectivity. These features position it as an option for users who want a large battery alongside the everyday functions of a mainstream smartphone.

Buyers should verify the model name and specifications with the manufacturer or retailer before purchasing.

2. realme P4 Power — 10,001mAh

The realme P4 Power is designed for users who prioritise battery endurance without giving up modern smartphone features.

It features a 10,001mAh silicon-carbon battery, an AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate, a MediaTek Dimensity 7400 Ultra processor and 80W fast charging.

The high-refresh-rate screen is suited to smooth scrolling and gaming, while the large battery provides substantial capacity for extended daily use.

3. realme Narzo Power — 10,001mAh

The realme Narzo Power is another smartphone in the large-battery category, combining a 10,001mAh battery with modern display and charging technology.

Its specifications include an AMOLED display, a high refresh rate and fast charging, making it an option for people who spend considerable time gaming, watching videos or using mobile applications.

As with other recently introduced models, availability and specifications should be confirmed for the buyer’s market.

4. POCO X8 Power — 10,000mAh

The POCO X8 Power has been listed in some 2026 smartphone specification reports as a large-battery device with a 10,000mAh capacity.

The model is presented as an option for users seeking extended battery life alongside everyday smartphone performance.

However, its official model identity, specifications and market availability should be independently verified before it is included in a purchasing shortlist.

5. Oukitel WP100 Titan — 33,000mAh

The Oukitel WP100 Titan stands out for its 33,000mAh battery, which is more than three times the capacity of a typical 10,000mAh phone.

Designed for demanding outdoor use, the rugged smartphone targets people who work in remote locations, travel extensively or spend long periods away from electrical outlets.

Its enormous battery makes it suitable for users who value endurance over a compact design. However, its size and weight make it less convenient for people who prefer lightweight everyday smartphones.

6. Ulefone Armor 29 Pro — 21,200mAh

The Ulefone Armor 29 Pro is a rugged smartphone designed for demanding environments, including outdoor activities and industrial work.

Its 21,200mAh battery provides considerably more capacity than conventional smartphones, making it attractive to users who need a device that can remain operational for extended periods.

The reinforced design also targets people who need greater physical durability than a typical consumer handset offers.

7. Oukitel WP300 — 16,000mAh

The Oukitel WP300 combines a 16,000mAh battery with a rugged design intended for outdoor use.

Its battery capacity makes it an option for people who frequently travel, camp or work in environments where charging facilities may be limited.

The phone prioritises durability and endurance over the slim profile associated with many mainstream smartphones.

8. Blackview BV9300 Pro — 15,080mAh

The Blackview BV9300 Pro is a rugged Android smartphone with a 15,080mAh battery.

It is designed for users who require a durable device for activities such as camping, construction work and outdoor travel. Its large battery reduces reliance on frequent charging, while its rugged construction makes it an alternative to conventional smartphones for demanding environments.

The model may appeal to buyers who want a substantial battery without moving to the exceptionally large capacities offered by devices such as the Oukitel WP100 Titan.

9. Oukitel WP35 — 11,000mAh

The Oukitel WP35 features an 11,000mAh battery, exceeding the 10,000mAh threshold while offering a rugged smartphone design.

It targets users who need extended battery life for outdoor activities, fieldwork and travel.

Its capacity makes it a practical consideration for people who want more endurance than a standard smartphone can typically provide, although its dimensions and weight should be considered before buying.

10. Oukitel WP200 Pro — 10,000mAh

The Oukitel WP200 Pro is a rugged Android handset listed with a 10,000mAh battery.

It is intended for users who want substantial battery capacity and smartphone functionality

World.title: 2027: Ndigbo with PVCs back Tinubu — Obidike
World.content:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Chief Obidike Chukwuebuka, has expressed confidence that Ndigbo will rally behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, urging eligible voters in the South-East to make their votes count.

Obidike, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Clarivo Oil and Gas, said the South-East could no longer afford to approach national politics solely from the standpoint of opposition, urging voters to assess the Tinubu administration based on infrastructure, representation, economic opportunities and federal presence in the region.

Speaking in an interview, he identified the establishment of the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) as a significant institutional response to the region’s longstanding demand for coordinated federal intervention and development.

He also cited the approval of the South-East Investment Company, an investment vehicle designed to mobilise capital and accelerate industrial and infrastructure development across the five South-East states, with initial funding of N150 billion.

According to him, the investment framework, alongside the SEDC, provides a platform for the region to pursue large-scale development beyond the limitations of individual political administrations.

Obidike further pointed to the Federal Government’s support for the South-East Vision 2050 development blueprint, a long-term regional framework intended to promote coordinated economic planning, industrialisation, infrastructure development and regional integration.

On road infrastructure, the APC chieftain cited the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway, describing it as one of the region’s most important economic corridors.

He also referenced the 107-kilometre Enugu-Onitsha Expressway project, being reconstructed under the Infrastructure Development and Refurbishment Investment Tax Credit Scheme, with MTN Nigeria involved in the project.

Other projects he highlighted included the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway, particularly the Umuahia-Aba section; the Enugu-Ninth Mile-Makurdi Expressway; the Enugu-Abakaliki Highway; the Okigwe-Owerri Road; the Onitsha-Owerri Road; the Aba-Ikot Ekpene Road; and the Owerri-Aba Road.

Obidike also highlighted what he described as increased federal attention to education and healthcare infrastructure in the South-East.

Among the projects he cited were the Federal College of Education, Bende, Abia State; the Federal University of Medical and Health Sciences, Item, Bende, Abia State; and the Federal University, Okigwe, Imo State.

He also pointed to the Federal Government’s approval for the upgrade of the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Enugu, as well as investments in medical facilities at the institution.

Obidike, who also chairs Clarivo Holdings Limited and Bidiks Nigeria Limited, said the central issue for voters in the South-East should be whether their political choices advance the interests of the people, rather than whether they support the party controlling the Federal Government.

He argued that supporting an incumbent president did not amount to abandoning regional interests, adding that the 2027 presidential election would provide an opportunity for voters in the region to reassess their political choices.

The APC chieftain expressed confidence that Ndigbo across the five South-East states, as well as those residing in other parts of the country, would rally behind Tinubu in the election.

He urged eligible voters to participate in the electoral process, stressing that the region should not allow the opportunity to secure greater federal attention, investment and development to slip away.

World.title: Trafficking: Titi Atiku laments Nigerian girls becoming ‘a nuisance’ abroad
World.content:
Titi Atiku

By Adegboyega Adeleye

The wife of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and Chairperson of the Board of Trustees of the Network Against Child Trafficking, Abuse and Labour, Chief Titi Atiku Abubakar, has decried human trafficking, saying Nigerian girls going abroad are becoming a “nuisance” in their host countries.

She spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the presentation of NACTAL’s review of the 2025 Trafficking in Persons Report released by the United States Department of State. Explaining why international partners supported Nigeria’s anti-trafficking work, she said they wanted Nigerian girls to remain in the country.

“Our girls are becoming nuisance in overseas countries. So that is why these partners are helping us,” Abubakar said.

She added that the partners were supporting both Nigeria’s anti-trafficking efforts and the girls themselves.

“They are supporting us, they are supporting the girls. They want them to stay at home and do whatever they want to do in their homes, in their country,” she said.

Abubakar, who is also the founder of the Women Trafficking and Child Labour Eradication Foundation (WOTCLEF), further urged civil society organisations to work together, saying NACTAL could not tackle trafficking, abuse and child labour without wider participation. She described the groups working with the network as frontline actors in the fight.

“NACTAL has about 286 foot soldiers, those are the CSOs that are working with NACTAL because NACTAL alone cannot do it. So we must bring everybody on board to help in this fight,” she said.

The immediate past NACTAL president and regional representative of the West African Coalition Against Trafficking in Persons and Smuggling of Migrants, Abdulganiu Abubakar, said the network’s review found that the contributions of the Nigerian government, development partners and civil society organisations were underrepresented in the US report.

He said NACTAL commissioned the review after the report’s release to examine its assessment of Nigeria’s efforts, particularly in victim protection, rehabilitation and shelter provision. Development partners, he said, had supported policy development, assisted victims and helped refurbish shelters run by civil society organisations and the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons.

Abubakar said about 10 NAPTIP shelters had received refurbishment support, but the interventions were not adequately reflected in the US report. He added that the work of more than 289 NACTAL member organisations and Nigeria’s role in regional anti-trafficking initiatives deserved greater recognition.

However, he acknowledged that Nigeria continued to face challenges in implementing anti-trafficking policies, including inadequate funding, weak political will and shortcomings in prosecuting cases, particularly high-profile ones.

“The government of Nigeria needs to do a lot in terms of funding. The political will and commitment should improve,” he said, urging the Federal Government to increase funding for agencies responsible for tackling trafficking and create an enabling environment for civil society groups and development partners.

NACTAL President Osita Osemene said he planned to expand the network from about 286 civil society organisations to 500 within three months and at least 1,000 within a year. He said the expansion would be accompanied by capacity-building programmes to strengthen support for victims and vulnerable groups.

“The fight against human trafficking is a collective responsibility, and everybody must come together to ensure that this fight is won,” Osemene said.

World.title: Obi of Onitsha raises alarm over rising poverty, insecurity
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

The Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Alfred Nnaemeka Achebe, has expressed concern over rising hardship in Nigeria, lamenting that more citizens are being pushed below the poverty line amid persistent insecurity and economic difficulties.

Achebe, in his royal message to mark the 2026 Ofala festival, titled “Celebrating 500+ Years of the Onitsha Monarchy,” cited a World Bank development update which stated that about 104 million Nigerians were classified as poor in 2023.

The monarch said the situation had been worsened by persistent insecurity in several parts of the country.

He recalled the recent visit by the leadership of the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria to President Bola Tinubu, during which the clerics raised concerns over national security and the severe economic hardship facing the majority of Nigerians.

Achebe said the issues highlighted by the bishops transcended political, religious and ethnic considerations and required urgent attention from the government.

“Hunger, unemployment, poor and inaccessible medical service, insecurity, and such other inadequate factors of human development, are pervading in the country. We plead with Mr President to give urgent attention to the fire situation on the ground,” he said.

On the 2027 general elections, the monarch observed that the attention of the political class was increasingly shifting towards political positioning at the expense of governance.

He urged stakeholders to intensify advocacy, mobilisation and public enlightenment to promote free, fair and credible elections.

Achebe also called on political parties to shun violence and conduct peaceful, issue-based campaigns that would enable voters to make informed choices.

Specifically, he urged people of the South-East to participate massively in the 2027 elections, warning that voter apathy would deepen the region’s political marginalisation and weaken its ability to influence decisions affecting its future.

According to him, the people of the region could no longer afford to stay away from the electoral process while complaining about inadequate representation.

“I call on the people of the South-East States to shake off their historical apathy towards elections. We cannot stay away from elections and turn around to complain of marginalisation. In democracy, all votes count. Therefore, we must come out and vote for our candidates,” the monarch said.

He also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to ensure free, fair and credible elections, stressing that the integrity of the electoral process was essential to strengthening public confidence in democracy.

The Obi appealed to President Tinubu to prioritise the challenges confronting Nigerians, insisting that the issues required practical solutions beyond political, religious and ethnic considerations.

He said the country’s leadership should focus on governance and addressing citizens’ needs, particularly as the next general elections draw closer.

On community development, Achebe spoke about the activities of the Onitsha Advancement Foundation (ONAF), an initiative established to implement programmes aimed at improving the welfare of the people.

He said that after five years of operation, the foundation needed a comprehensive review of its achievements, processes and overall impact.

According to him, the proposed review would help reposition the organisation, strengthen its programmes and identify areas requiring improvement to deliver better results.

World.title: 2027: BTO 4PBAT begins grassroots campaign for Tinubu
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

A support group, BTO 4PBAT, has launched a unit-to-unit campaign in Ondo West Local Government Area of Ondo State to mobilise grassroots support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027.

Flagging off the campaign, the group’s Director-General, Adesuyi Adojutelegan, described the initiative as a strategic move to consolidate the All Progressives Congress (APC) and secure victory for Tinubu in the forthcoming presidential election.

Adojutelegan charged party leaders, coordinators and members to intensify door-to-door mobilisation, stressing that electoral victory would depend largely on effective engagement with voters at the polling unit level.

He urged coordinators to communicate the achievements of the Tinubu administration, particularly in road infrastructure and economic reforms, as key messages during their engagements with residents.

The director-general also called on members to mobilise support for all APC candidates, including those contesting seats in the National Assembly and the Ondo State House of Assembly.

He said the group’s unit-to-unit strategy was designed to deepen voter engagement and strengthen the party’s prospects across the state.

Adojutelegan commended the Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, for his support for the group, describing him as a major pillar of its activities and financier.

“The Minister has been our pillar of support and financier. He has continued to stand firmly with us and shown uncommon commitment to the growth and stability of our group. His contributions have been unprecedented,” he said.

He described Tunji-Ojo as a prominent political figure in Ondo State, adding that his support for the APC and Tinubu’s re-election bid had encouraged party stakeholders across the state.

Adojutelegan urged members of the group and residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 elections.

“Your PVC is your voting strength. Ensure you have it to guarantee your participation in the forthcoming elections,” he said.

World.title: LAUTECH doctors suspend 50-day strike after Makinde’s intervention
World.content:
By Chioma Obinna

The Association of Resident Doctors (ARD), Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH) Teaching Hospital, Ogbomoso, has suspended its 50-day industrial action for an initial period of eight weeks following the intervention of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde.

The suspension takes effect on Saturday, October 17, 2026, with the resumption of full clinical duties, following government commitments to address the doctors’ demands.

The demands include payment of outstanding 2025 minimum wage arrears, implementation of the Revised Professional Allowance Table (PAT) and passage of the Medical Residency Training Act (MRTA) Bill.

The decision was reached at an emergency general meeting of the association on Friday, October 16, after members reviewed the outcome of a stakeholders’ meeting held the previous day at the hospital’s Gangway Hall, chaired by Governor Makinde.

In a letter of appreciation addressed to the Chief of Staff to the governor, the association expressed gratitude to Makinde for his intervention and commitment to resolving the issues that triggered the strike.

The letter was jointly signed by the ARD President, Dr Mustapha Adedapo; Public Relations Officer, Dr Abdulrahman Fofie; and Assistant General Secretary, Dr Oladayo Bada.

The association said the governor’s visit to the hospital and personal involvement in negotiations demonstrated the government’s commitment to addressing the concerns of healthcare workers.

“The presence of key government officials, members of the hospital board, the leadership of the State House of Assembly, and other stakeholders underscored the seriousness and sincerity of government in addressing the longstanding concerns raised by healthcare workers,” the letter stated.

Government sets deadlines for demands

On the outstanding 2025 minimum wage arrears, the government reportedly committed to making payment on or before mid-November 2026.

The governor also directed the establishment of a multi-stakeholder committee to develop modalities for implementing the Revised Professional Allowance Table within six weeks.

Regarding the Medical Residency Training Act Bill, the government committed to ensuring its passage on or before October 28, 2026, with assent expected within the first week of November.

The association described the commitments as significant steps towards resolving the dispute and improving the working conditions of resident doctors in the state.

“These commitments demonstrate His Excellency’s dedication to strengthening the healthcare system in Oyo State, improving the welfare of healthcare workers, and ensuring quality healthcare delivery to the people of the state,” it said.

Doctors give government eight weeks

Explaining its decision to suspend the strike, the ARD said members considered the governor’s intervention and ongoing efforts by the state government and hospital management to address their grievances.

“In recognition of the Governor’s goodwill and the ongoing efforts of the Government and Hospital Management toward resolving our demands, the Association resolved to suspend its fifty (50)-day industrial action for an initial period of eight (8) weeks,” the letter stated.

The suspension provides an eight-week window for the government to fulfil its commitments, while the association expressed optimism that the agreed timelines would be respected.

The doctors said their decision was based on the commitments made and the need to sustain constructive engagement with the relevant authorities.

The association assured the governor of its continued commitment to industrial harmony and the provision of quality healthcare services to residents of Oyo State.

“We are optimistic that the commitments made will be implemented within the agreed timelines and that this marks the beginning of a lasting resolution to the concerns of our members,” it added.

The ARD also requested that its appreciation be conveyed to the governor for what it described as his leadership and responsiveness to the welfare of healthcare professionals.

World.title: Insecurity must end before third decade, Defence Minister tells army officers
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

ABUJA — The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), has charged graduands of the Army War College Nigeria (AWCN) to translate the knowledge acquired during their nine-month professional military training into decisive action to strengthen national security and end insecurity.

Musa gave the charge on Friday, October 16, 2026, at the graduation ceremony of 99 participants of Course 10/2026 of the Army War College Nigeria in Abuja, where he served as Special Guest of Honour.

He said the true measure of their training would be their ability to deliver tangible results on the battlefield and improve the country’s security situation.

“Go out to the field and make the difference,” the minister charged the officers.

Recalling President Bola Tinubu’s directive at a recent National Security Council meeting that the fight against insecurity must not extend into a third decade, Musa urged the graduating officers to demonstrate the discipline, commitment and operational effectiveness required to achieve lasting results.

He reaffirmed that the Armed Forces of Nigeria remained professional and committed to their constitutional mandates.

The minister also stressed that hard work, dedication, integrity and proven performance must remain the basis for career advancement in the military.

He said only officers who demonstrated commitment and integrity should be entrusted with higher responsibilities, citing the career progression of the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Waidi Shaibu, as an example.

On modern warfare, Musa said military success no longer depended solely on the possession of expensive equipment, pointing to ongoing conflicts around the world as evidence of the growing importance of innovation and adaptability.

He urged all departments of the Armed Forces to embrace technological changes to improve operational effectiveness, stressing that innovation should not be regarded as the exclusive responsibility of engineers.

The defence minister also called on the military to support peaceful, safe and credible elections in collaboration with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies.

He said such collaboration was necessary to protect citizens from intimidation and prevent individuals or groups from undermining the electoral process.

Earlier, the Commandant of the Army War College Nigeria, Major General Umar Alkali, reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to producing competent military leaders capable of addressing the country’s evolving security challenges.

Alkali said participants of Course 10/2026 had completed 37 weeks of intensive professional military education, recording milestones that included the participation of the first female officers and the highest number of allied participants since the college’s establishment.

He identified indigenous technological innovation and inter-agency cooperation as critical to improving military effectiveness.

The commandant urged the graduands to uphold professionalism, integrity and sound judgment in advancing Nigeria’s national security objectives.

Highlights of the ceremony included the presentation of fellowship awards to the 99 graduands by the defence minister, as well as certificates and other awards.

A wounded officer among the graduands also received a special souvenir and a N5 million token in recognition of his courage.

The Chief of Army Staff presented merit awards, while the President of the Alumni Association of the Army War College Nigeria, Brigadier General O.A. Ogunleye (Rtd), formally inducted the graduands into the association.

The event also featured the unveiling and launch of the Army War College Nigeria journal, magazine and books, alongside the presentation of awards to distinguished eminent fellows and souvenirs to the special guest of honour.

Among the graduands were allied military officers from African countries, including South Africa and Cameroon.

The ceremony was attended by the Director, Army, Ministry of Defence, senior military officers, members of the diplomatic corps and other dignitaries.

World.title: El-Shaddai Covenant Ministries Celebrates At 40
World.content:
A leading Pentecostal church in Nigeria, El-Shaddai Covenant Ministries (ECM), has concluded plans for its 40th anniversary.

The celebrations hold at the El-Shaddai Cathedral at Plot 6441, Yakubu Gowon Way, Opposite NITEL Headquarters, by Old Airport Junction, in the ancient city of Jos, Plateau State, North-central Nigeria from Thursday, October 29 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

According to the church’s anniversary committee, the theme for the anniversary designed to celebrate the faithfulness of God and the evidence of divine help over the decades is: ‘See what the Lord has done.’

General Overseer of the ministry, Dr. (Mrs.) Temitayo James, explained that Jos is hosting the historic celebration because “that was where it all began”, adding that the ministry, headquartered in Lagos, had its humble beginnings in the ancient city.

The general overseer announced the anointed ministers of God to minister at the programme to include: Dr. Paul Enenche, Senior Pastor, Dunamis International Gospel Centre; Bishop O. C. Fred, Vice-Chancellor, Cornerstone University, Jos; Dr. John E. Akpami, General Overseer, Christian Teaching Centre Family Church, Kaduna; Pastor Ishaya Paul Demsa, Senior Pastor, Fountain of Life Ministries International (FOLMI), Jos; and Rev. Sunday O. Academe, Founder, Jesus Power Crusaders International Ministry.

Others are Rev. Omokayode Adeaga, Assistant General Overseer (Northern Region) and Revd. Oyeleke Ajiboye, Assistant General Overseer (Southern Region) of El-Shaddai Covenant Ministries.

Founded by Dr. James O. James of blessed memory, El-Shaddai Covenant Ministries, which started in the sitting room of the departed leader, with only his wife, children and a handful of friends at its maiden meeting in October, 1986, has grown with branches spread across Nigeria.

The ministry also announced that there would be a nationwide thanksgiving celebration on Sunday, November 8 in all its branches across Nigeria, as members and guests thank God for all He has done and will continue to do.

James invited current and former members, friends of the ministry and the general public to be part of the historic celebration.

World.title: N156bn Debt: Court Upholds UBA’s Receiver Appointment, Bars Diversion of Stallion Group’s
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

The Federal High Court in Lagos has upheld the appointment of a receiver/manager by United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc to recover an alleged N156.03 billion debt owed by Stallion Group, while restraining the defendants from diverting payments due to them from government agencies.

In a judgment delivered on Friday, Justice Daniel Osiagor upheld the validity of the mortgage arrangements securing the loans and affirmed UBA’s right to enforce its securities over the properties pledged against the facilities.

The judge held that the defendants did not dispute their indebtedness to the bank but challenged the amount claimed.

The court also affirmed the liability of the guarantors and upheld the appointment of Romeo Ese as receiver/manager, confirming his authority to take possession of the mortgaged properties and seek protective orders to safeguard the assets.

In another significant aspect of the judgment, Justice Osiagor restrained the defendants from diverting receivables due to them from government agencies, a measure aimed at preventing the diversion of funds that could facilitate the bank’s recovery efforts.

The court further held that the reconciliation of accounts between UBA and the defendants did not extinguish the underlying debt or invalidate the bank’s right to enforce its security.

Justice Osiagor also dismissed an objection by Barbedos, the 12th defendant, which challenged the mortgage arrangements on the ground that its consent was required before the transactions could be concluded.

The judge held that Barbedos had failed to establish any proprietary interest in the mortgaged property and, therefore, had no legal basis to insist that its consent should have been obtained before the mortgage was created.

The court also resolved the jurisdictional issue in UBA’s favour, affirming its competence to entertain the bank’s claims.

According to the proceedings, all the issues submitted for determination were resolved in UBA’s favour, with the court granting the reliefs sought by the bank.

The dispute dates back to October 2023, when UBA obtained interim orders from the Federal High Court to enforce its securities over assets belonging to Stallion Nigeria Limited and its subsidiaries.

The properties affected by the earlier orders included industrial and commercial assets in Lagos, Port Harcourt and Kano.

UBA had alleged that Stallion Group owed approximately N156.03 billion, prompting litigation involving several companies within the conglomerate and their guarantors.

In November 2023, Stallion Group disputed the bank’s account of the debt controversy, maintaining that it had made substantial repayments and was engaged in discussions with UBA over account reconciliation and restructuring.

The proceedings subsequently witnessed procedural disputes, including a request by counsel representing some of the defendants for the case to be transferred from the court of Justice Akintayo Aluko, who had handled earlier applications.

World.title: Don’t Scare Away Electorate Through Violence, Oyo Guber Candidate Warns Politicians
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Oyo State, Adegboyega Taofeek Adegoke, has admonished politicians and their supporters not to scare away the electorate through thuggery and violence ahead of the 2027 general election.

He stated this while speaking with journalists in Ibadan, and calling on the political parties and their candidates to talk to their supporters and followers to allow peace to reign, saying thuggery and violence will scare away voters.

He warned that no member of any political party can singlehandedly bring the candidates to government, adding that they will need the people, the electorate to win elections.

On Wednesday, members of Accord Party in the state had clashed with some hoodlums at Molete area leading to the death of one person, while many sustained various degree of injuries, a situation which also caused panic among the residents of the area in Ibadan, the state capital.

Also, the All Progressives Congress (APC) alleged that their convoy was attacked by thugs in Ibadan a few weeks ago.

The Oyo ADC governorship candidate said part of the problem is the high rate of youth unemployment, noting that majority of the state population is made up of youths that are not gainfully employed, promising that if elected governor, he will provide jobs for the youth in the state.

He called on all candidates in the 2027 elections in Oyo State to ensure that they maintain and allow peace to reign.

He also called on political leaders to measure what they say at the campaigns, saying they should avoid hate speeches but tell people what they want to do and how they want to achieve them.

He said: “Anytime I go out for campaign, I don’t go out with thugs. I don’t like violence, I don’t support violence. I preach peace always.

“We should talk to our supporters, our followers to allow peace to reign. We should not scare away the electorate because without them we cannot win elections. We cannot win election with our party members alone, we need the people.

“If our youth are fully engaged, they will not be available for thuggery and violence. I want to appeal to my colleagues, that we should not allow people to turn Oyo State to an avenue for attacks, an avenue for thuggery, where hoodlums will reign supreme. We don’t want that in Oyo State.

“Our campaign should be issue based. We should not incite the people. We should measure what we say. Don’t attack one another. Tell the electorate what you want to do and let them judge you.

“That is why I said my agenda is summarised in Nine Points – ‘SOLUTIONS’. So tell people what you want to do and avoid hate speech.”

World.title: PTDF Reaffirms Continuous Funding For Research Projects in Varsities
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

The Executive Secretary, Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), Prof. Shua’ibu Shehu Aliyu, has reiterated the Fund’s commitment to strengthening research, innovation and human capital development in Nigerian universities.

The secretary said the PTDF seeks not only to support academic excellence but also to promote researches that address real national and industry challenges.

Prof Aliyu, who made this assertion at the University of Benin, Benin City, during PDTF Professional Chair in Renewable Energy: Close Out ceremony on Thursday, noted that as Nigeria’s energy landscape continues to evolve, there is a growing need for research institutions to develop practical and commercially viable solutions in renewable energy and other emerging technologies.

Aliyu, who was represented at the occasion by Ereh Iyalla, Head Gas Division, PTDF, asserted that the seminar theme – Agrowaste to Fuel: Biodiesel Development, Opportunities and Challenges for Youth Employment to the 21st Century – was timely and highly relevant to Nigeria’s quest for sustainable energy, environmental protection, economic diversification and youth employment.

The paper was delivered by Chairholder, Prof. Kensington Obahiagbaon.

Aliyu noted that: “The focus on converting agricultural waste into biodiesel demonstrates the potential of research and innovation to transform challenges into opportunities. Beyond providing an alternative energy source, such innovations can support waste management, entrepreneurship, local technology development and employment opportunities for young Nigerians.

He stated further that: “As Nigeria’s energy landscape ontinues to evolve, there is a growing need for research institutions to develop practical and commercially viable solutions in renewable energy and other emerging technologies.

“We therefore encourage researchers to ensure that reseach outcome move beyond academic publications to technology development, demonstration, industry adoption and commercialization.”

Prof Obahiagbaon, a professor of chemical engineering, in his presentation, noted that the global dependence on fossil diesel has created twin problems of gas emissions and energy insecurity.

According to him, global energy crisis, climate change, and waste management burden have made agro-waste to fuel a critical pathway for the 21st century, adding that using agro-waste as biodiesel feedstock is a core principle of the circular economy. “It converts a liability into an asset: waste becomes fuel, and waste management becomes a revenue stream.”

Speaking on the challenges and future direction of biodiesel development in Nigeria, Obahiagbaon said feedstock availability and cost, ensuring a stable and affordable supply remain crucial.

He advocated the development of sustainable standard for biodiesel production.

The Vice Chancellor, University of Benin, Prof. Edoba Omoregie (SAN), in his opening remarks, noted that in the past six years of your existence of the chair, it has proven to be a start-up for the institution.

“We will continue to partner with graduates in every field of study.”

According to him, everyone knows the importance of renewable energy.

“We are involved in this effort to try to draw attention to renewable energy as a major finding source of energy. Because of the problem of climate change, we know that it is worth looking at renewable energy sources to be able to mitigate the impact of climate change.”

World.title: Cross River Secures $20m Investment for 4,000-Hectare Oil Palm Plantation
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The Cross River State Government has signed a concession agreement with ValueFronteira Limited for the development of a 4,000-hectare oil palm plantation in Ijiegu Yache and adjoining clans in Yala Local Government Area of the state, with the investor committing more than $20 million to the project over five years.

The project, which is expected to create thousands of jobs and boost agricultural production in six clans including Ijiegu, Wonye, Uchu, Ichui, Ukani and Ewor, is part of the state government’s agricultural transformation agenda aimed at strengthening food security, promoting rural development and improving livelihoods.

Speaking at a stakeholders’ meeting and site handover ceremony held in Ijiegu Yache, Cross River State, the Managing Director of ValueFronteira Limited, Maurice Ekpong, explained that the organisation would invest over $20 million within five years to establish the plantation.

He stated that the project would generate thousands of employment opportunities and significantly transform the economies of the host communities and Cross River State.

Ekpong’s announcement was welcomed by traditional rulers, community representatives, youths and women leaders, who expressed optimism that the investment would create jobs, particularly for young people, while improving economic activities and livelihoods across the communities.

The Clan Head of Wonye, HRH Mohie Damian Ododo, described the project as a dream come true, pledging the collective support of the clan heads for its successful implementation.

He also affirmed ValueFronteira as a corporate member of Yache land.

Other traditional rulers and representatives at the event included HRH Mohie Isaac Omaji, Clan Head of Ijiegu; HRH Mohie Innocent Okaiiba Aji, Clan Head of Ichui; HRH Mohie Ogar Idazor, Clan Head of Ukani; Augustine Obozor, representing Ewor Clan; and Pius Idagu, representing Uchu Clan.

In his remarks, the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor and Director-General of the Bureau of Public Private Partnerships, Dr. Francis Ntamu, assured stakeholders that the concession process was transparent and competitive, leading to ValueFronteira’s emergence as the preferred investor.

He disclosed that the project had received the full approval of the State Executive Council (SEC), adding that: “It aligns with the government’s drive to attract investment and strengthen critical sectors of the economy.”

He expressed the state government’s hope that the investment will contribute to positioning Cross River as a major agribusiness destination in Nigeria, while supporting its broader objectives of food security, rural development and economic empowerment.

“The development is expected to expand commercial agricultural activities in Yala, create employment opportunities and stimulate economic growth in the host communities,” Ntamu stressed.

The government delegation also included the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Environment and Solicitor-General of the state, Rosemary Onah, and Brian Ugbe, a Director in the Ministry of Agriculture, who represented the Commissioner for Agriculture.

World.title: NGX Group, Partners Advance Cross-Border Investment Collaboration Through Dangote Refinery Offer in Egypt, Ethiopia
World.content:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) and its partners are advancing cross-border investment collaboration among African capital markets, with engagements in Cairo, Egypt and Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, exploring how market infrastructure and institutional partnerships can improve investment access across the continent. Using the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE offer as a practical context, the discussions focused on connecting investors across jurisdictions and mobilising African capital for industrial development.

Held on Thursday, the engagements were hosted in Cairo by the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), in collaboration with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), and in Addis Ababa by the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX). They brought together exchange leaders, financial institutions and other capital market stakeholders to explore practical approaches to improving market connectivity, broadening investor participation and mobilising African capital for productive investment.

Speaking during the discussions, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, Temi Popoola, emphasized the importance of addressing longstanding structural barriers that limit investment flows across African markets. He noted that the continent possesses substantial pools of institutional capital, but stronger market infrastructure and cooperation are needed to connect these resources with investment opportunities across national borders. “Africa has substantial capital within its own markets, particularly across pension funds and insurance companies. The challenge is how to connect that capital to investment opportunities across the continent.

The Dangote Refinery offer provides a practical opportunity to address some of the infrastructure barriers to cross-border investment. Beyond a single transaction, it is about creating connections that enable African capital to finance African growth,” Popoola said.

President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, highlighted the refinery as an example of the scale of industrial investment required to strengthen Africa’s productive capacity, reduce dependence on imports and support long-term economic growth. He emphasised the importance of developing stronger channels through which African capital can support major industrial projects across the continent. He also commended NGX Group for its role in bringing African exchanges together around the initiative and acknowledged the participating exchanges for their collaboration.

Group Chairman of NGX Group, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, stressed that lasting progress would depend on sustained institutional cooperation and the development of market infrastructure that makes cross-border investment more accessible and efficient. “Our task is not simply to collaborate around one offer, but to develop lasting partnerships that support cross-border investment and capital formation across Africa. This requires cooperation among exchanges, regulators, financial institutions and businesses, alongside investment in the infrastructure and technology that make participation more accessible,” Kwairanga said.

At the Cairo engagement, Executive Chairman of the Egyptian Exchange, Omar Radwan, highlighted the potential for instruments such as Egyptian Depositary Receipts (EDRs) to provide a channel through which Egyptian investors could access selected African businesses. He expressed EGX’s readiness to work with Dangote Industries to explore a possible framework for such an arrangement.

President and Chairman of Afreximbank, Dr. George Elombi, reaffirmed the bank’s longstanding financing relationship with Dangote Industries and its commitment to supporting African industrial development. He highlighted the importance of mobilising African investment towards enterprises capable of contributing to the continent’s economic transformation.

In Addis Ababa, discussions focused on expanding investment opportunities for Ethiopian investors and strengthening Ethiopia’s participation in Africa’s evolving capital market landscape.

Chief Executive Officer of ESX, Yodit Kassa, welcomed the engagement, noting its significance for Ethiopian investors and the country’s growing capital market. “The Dangote Petroleum Refinery offer represents an important opportunity for Ethiopian investors to participate in the growth of one of Africa’s leading industrial enterprises. It also reflects the growing confidence in Ethiopia’s capital market and our readiness to work with leading institutions across the continent,” Kassa said.

The Cairo and Addis Ababa engagements followed earlier stops at the Nairobi Securities Exchange and the Botswana Stock Exchange, extending discussions on cross-border investment across multiple African markets. The discussions also highlighted the practical requirements for cross-border participation, including regulatory recognition, distribution, investor verification, settlement, custody and access to reliable information. The offer provides a real-world opportunity for exchanges, regulators, intermediaries and financial technology platforms to address these considerations and explore workable solutions within their respective regulatory frameworks. For participating markets, it also raises the question of how local savings can be channelled more efficiently into productive enterprises across the continent.

NGX Group remains committed to working with partner exchanges and financial institutions to strengthen market infrastructure, expand cross-border investment access and advance collaboration among African capital markets, contributing to the continent’s long-term economic and industrial development.

World.title: Beyond the NYSC Camp: Cross River’s rot, the locust years, and the demands of recovery
World.content:
Joseph Odok

The outrage over the dilapidated National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) Orientation Camp in Obubra is justified and overdue. Corps members have endured crumbling hostels, inadequate water, failing sanitation and facilities so degraded that the NYSC leadership has threatened or moved to suspend further postings. Capacity has collapsed from roughly 2,500 per stream to little more than 1,000, with hundreds seeking relocation. The state government’s swift decision to shut the camp for comprehensive overhaul and temporarily relocate orientation exercises to the University of Education and Entrepreneurship in Akamkpa is the correct, responsible response. Yet the camp is merely the most visible tip of a much larger iceberg of institutional and infrastructural decay that accumulated over years of announcements without delivery.​

That decay did not begin in 2023. It was deepened, accelerated and normalised during the eight years of Benedict Ayade’s administration. Those were the locust years: budgets of kinetic crystallisation, quabalistic densification, olimpotic meristemasis and quantum infinitum that promised first-world transformation while delivering near-zero performance. Signature projects (the Bakassi Deep Seaport, an international airport, Super High way, dozens of factories) were commissioned on billboards, in television studios and newspaper pages far more often than they appeared as functioning realities on the ground.

Of the much-trumpeted 38 factories, the overwhelming majority remained empty shells or stalled constructions years later. Tinapa, once a bold statement of ambition, was left to weeds and debt. The civil service grew demoralised; promotions stagnated for years; morale sank. Critical maintenance (desilting of drainage channels, upkeep of fire service assets) was neglected. Fire vehicles fell into disrepair or were effectively lost to the system without adequate replacement; today’s limited operational capacity is the product of remedial effort.of Governor Bassey Otu not inheritance.​

Floods and erosion that now regularly embarrass the state are not acts of God alone. They are the predictable consequence of years in which systematic desilting and drainage maintenance received deaf ears. The same pattern held for roads, erosion-control sites and public institutions. Projects were announced with fanfare and then left to rot or to the mercy of contractors who delivered substandard work. Most road were rather painted with tar and not asphalt and they decayed within time frame of their construction. Yala became a home of dust, Obudu and Bekwara roads are still a consequence of Ayade’s mess. Major parts of CRS were disconnected from the national grid with many communities no longer having access to electricity on a phantom promise of power plant that were nothing but avenue to loot the state. The cost of destruction is always lower than the cost of rebuilding. Cross River is still paying that price.

Those who raised these issues during the Ayade years were not always celebrated as patriots. Some were treated as enemies of the state. Critics faced arrest and prolonged detention on inflated charges. I spent 117 days in custody for the offence of speaking uncomfortable truths. Many residents, conditioned by the politics of “food on the table” and praise-singing, dismissed such criticism as personal hatred. Today some of the same voices who once defended or ignored the rot have discovered sudden rage against Governor Bassey Otu. The injustice lies less in the existence of legitimate impatience than in the selective amnesia that denies the scale of what was inherited and the direction of the current recovery effort.

A government reflects the mood of its people. Years of applause for grandiose budgets and digital inauguration ceremonies helped produce the decayed Cross River we now inhabit. The emerging public consciousness that refuses to allow leaders to sleep is healthier for democracy. It is already yielding concrete results. The rapid government intervention on the NYSC camp is one. The handling of the Denis Odama matter (where the governor directed the withdrawal of a complaint initiated by aides and secured the critic’s release) is another signal that this administration can still distinguish between accountability and vengeance.

Ongoing desilting exercises, efforts to restore fire service capacity after long neglect, recovery of Tinapa from years of limbo, road works across several corridors, and attempts to stabilise a demoralised civil service form part of a policy direction of recovery, consolidation and gradual development. These efforts sit on the foundation left by earlier administrations, including those of Duke and Imoke, and seek to reverse the damage of the intervening locust years.

None of this excuses slow delivery or substandard remedial work. Cross Riverians are right to demand higher standards. More federal transfers and improved revenue create an opportunity, yet the accumulated rot far exceeds what any single budget cycle can erase. Governor Otu must recognise the impatience of a people who have waited too long. He must cut waste deliberately, communicate more transparently about the use of public funds, and ensure that rehabilitation meets acceptable quality thresholds. Accountability and openness are not optional extras; they are the only durable foundation for the recovery agenda.

It is easier to destroy than to rebuild. The present outrage, if channelled constructively rather than as selective bitterness, can accelerate the rebuilding. Cross River deserves leaders who treat criticism as feedback rather than treason, and citizens who remember how the rot was allowed to deepen. The NYSC camp is a symptom. The cure requires sustained vigilance, honest reckoning with the past eight years of non-performance, and a government that matches the people’s rising expectations with visible, measurable, transparent action. That is the standard against which recovery must be judged.

. Dr Joseph Abang Odok, a Senior Lecturer, a Social Change Agent, a Lawyer and a Philosopher, writes from Lokoja

World.title: WACOT Renews Strategic Partnership with Edo Govt to Drive Agricultural Transformation
World.content:
Oluchi Chibuzor

WACOT Limited, has extended its agreement with the Edo State Government on fertilizer production through the Edo State Fertilizer and Chemical Company Limited (ESFCCL) in Auchi.

The partnership which commenced in 2017, reaffirms both parties’ commitment to boosting local fertilizer production, supporting smallholder farmers, and advancing Nigeria’s food security.

Speaking on the significance of the facility from an industry perspective, the President of the Fertilizer Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) and Director, Corporate Affairs, TGI Group Mr. Sadiq Kassim, said: “The Auchi facility is of strategic importance to Nigeria’s fertilizer industry and national food security. It is the only plant in the South-South with the capability to produce tailored, crop-specific fertilizer blends suited to the region’s soil requirements. The facility also has the capability to produce specialised chemical blends to meet the specific needs of the North-East, where security challenges have made establishing fertilizer production facilities particularly difficult.”

Also commenting on the renewed partnership, the Managing Director of WACOT Limited, Mr. Naveen Chaurasia, said: “The renewal of this agreement is a strong statement of our long-term commitment to Edo State and to Nigeria’s agricultural transformation. Since 2017, we have demonstrated that a well-managed public-private partnership can revive moribund assets and deliver real value.”

Speaking on behalf of the Edo State government, Commissioner, Ministry of Business, Trade and Investments, Omoh Anabor, added: “This agreement involving the Edo State Government, ESFCCL and WACOT Limited represents far more than a formal transaction. It is a strategic step towards positioning Edo State as a leading destination for investment and industrial growth. This partnership demonstrates our readiness to work with credible private sector partners to unlock economic opportunities, support farmers through improved access to agricultural inputs, strengthen food security, create jobs and enterprise opportunities across Auchi and the wider Edo State.”

World.title: Beach plans this Saturday? Here’s when the tides will turn
World.content:
Check Saturday’s high and low tide times before planning your activities along South Africa’s coastline. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Saturday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Spring tides can cause greater changes in water levels along South Africa’s coastline.

However, tides are only part of the picture. Wind, waves and swell and the shape of the seabed can also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.



When to expect the next spring tide at the coast

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual, changing conditions along the coast.

The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing.



High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides reveal more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Bernard Parker backtracks on split, infidelity claims amid club exit
World.content:
Bernard Parker backtracks on statement on his personal life. Images via Facebook

Days after dropping a bombshell about his personal life, including a confession alluding to cheating on his new baby mama, Bernard Parker has backtracked, calling for “privacy” and “discretion”

This comes as the former Bafana Bafana and Kaizer Chiefs player stepped down as head coach of TS Galaxy.

BERNARD PARKER BACKTRACKS ON BOMBSHELL CLAIMS

On Monday, 12 October, Bernard Parker dropped a bombshell statement on his official social media platforms about his personal life.



This included that he has split from his baby mama, Kacha Stepanovic, and was struggling with “personal addictions”. He also used the opportunity to apologise to the red-haired woman, alluding to infidelity in their three-year relationship. The news came as a surprise to the public, given that his last known relationship was his marriage to his wife, Wendy Parker.

A few days later, Bernard Parker did a 180 on his initial statement, effectively denying what he initially wrote.

He shared: “I am aware of statements circulating publicly concerning my personal circumstances and relationships. For clarity, any communication attributed to me should be treated as official only if it has been confirmed by me or issued through my authorised representative.

Bernard called for the public to “exercise discretion and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about my private life”.

He added that he was “attending to the matter privately and responsibly, with due consideration for the well-being and dignity of everyone concerned, particularly the children”

Bernard also deleted his reposts of several Instagram Reels, which spoke of lust, betrayal and a “miserable marriage”.



STEPPING DOWN AS TS GALAXY COACH

Meanwhile, Bernard Parker has been replaced by Esau Mtsweni, who steps in as TS Galaxy’s interim coach.

The surprise move was announced by club chairman Tim Suzaki, who claimed the move was football-related and not a result of Bernard’s personal life.

He told SABC Sport: “As a club, we’re also quite surprised when we saw the long statement coming from his social media account…Clubs and employers, in general, don’t get too involved in people’s personal affairs.

“You see and hear of them as and when they happen, you know.”

Suzaki alluded to Bernard Parker’s personal life “challenges”, adding: “He’s a man, he should find a way to resolve it. So that he could come back to football if he’s not within football”.
