World.title: 10-hour water outage set to hit Johannesburg suburb on Tuesday
World.content:
A close-up shot of a modern chrome bathroom faucet with water dripping from the tip. Image: Pexels

Johannesburg Water has announced a 10-hour planned water supply interruption that will affect residents in Village Deep, south of the Johannesburg CBD, later this month.

The utility will shut off water supply on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, from 7:00 until 17:00, to carry out planned maintenance in Region F.

Johannesburg Water shared the notice in its daily water supply system status update on 16 October.



Streets affected by the Johannesburg water outage

According to Johannesburg Water, residents and businesses on the following streets will have no water during the maintenance:

Eloff Street

Bitcon Road

Inglestone Road

Baldwin Road

Wright-Boag Road

Colyn Road

The utility said its teams will tie a newly installed 110mm water pipeline into the existing 100mm water reticulation network.

Johannesburg Water explained that the work will ensure the successful integration and commissioning of the upgraded infrastructure.

The utility said the project will bring improved service delivery, continuity of water supply and safety to customers once complete.

How residents can prepare for the water outage

Since the interruption will last for most of the working day, households in Village Deep may want to store enough clean water for drinking, cooking and basic hygiene before 7:00 on Tuesday.

Residents can fill bottles, buckets and containers the night before, and keep stored drinking water covered and in a cool place.



Filling a bucket or two for flushing toilets can also help households get through the day without running taps.

Businesses in the area that rely on water, such as restaurants, salons and car washes, may need to adjust their operations or make alternative arrangements for the day.

Once the supply returns, residents may notice air in the pipes or slightly discoloured water at first. Letting the tap run for a short while usually helps clear it.

World.title: SA’s Top three most-expensive schools: Worth the fees?
World.content:
The Top three most expensive schools in South Africa all cost over R400 000 a year for boarding and tuition. Is it worth splurging on your child’s education?

THE TOP THREE MOST EXPENSIVE SCHOOLS: FEES AND MORE

South Africa most expensive school is Hilton College, the all-boys boarding school, located near Howick in KwaZulu-Natal. The second most expensive school in SA is Michaelhouse, a boys’ boarding school, located in Balgowan in the Midlands in KwaZulu-Natal.

The third most expensive school is Roedean School for Girls, located in the suburb of Parktown in the city of Johannesburg. This is the most expensive girls’ school in South Africa.



So, how much does it cost to attend the Top three most expensive schools in South Africa?

HILTON COLLEGE

Hilton College fees for 2026 are R441 766 a year. That covers tuition, food and board, games, minor medical attention, use of the sanatorium, library and laundry.

It also covers core curriculum-based activities, including sport (apart from a few exceptions). Once you are accepted into the college, you will need to pay a non-refundable entrance fee of R110 441.50. This equals one term’s fees and is a contribution to the school’s development programme.



Extra fees of R594.25 a term covers items such as some dry cleaning, laundry bags, minor duplicating costs, newspapers, sunscreen, certain school plays and socials. Boys who take up golf, rowing or canoeing pay an additional fee to cover transport and equipment upkeep, according to an older version of the fee schedule.

MICHEALHOUSE

As of 2026, it costs R417 000 a year to attend. This is a 6.5% increase from the R392 000 it cost parents back in 2025. The R417 000 is inclusive of both tuition and boarding as Michaelhouse is a boarding-only school. To attend this school for five years of high school would cost roughly R2.1 million.

The R417 000 includes only tuition and boarding. However, there is still uniform, sport equipment, outings and pocket money to consider. The school prioritises academics, sports and cultural programmes. There is also a non-refundable registration fee of R950 as well as a debtors admin fee of R5 672 for those not paying via debt order. SA residents will also pay R81 250 as an acceptance fee and non-SA residents pay R208 500.



ROEDEAN SCHOOL FOR GIRLS

Roedean School for Girls cost R413 095 a year for 2026. This is an increase of 6.7% from R387 093 in 2025. This works out to around R34 400 a month. You can attend Roedean School for Girls without full boarding. The cost of day-school tuition is R233 104 for 2026. This makes the school the second most expensive day school in South Africa, next to Kearsney College, for boys located in Botha’s Hill, KwaZulu-Natal.

Additional costs include uniforms, sports kits, outings, tours and stationery. These different from school to school. Parents should check the school’s current fee schedule for the full prices.

ARE THE FEES WORTH IT?

One of the first things to look at when picking a school for your child is the pass rate. South Africa’s most expensive school, Hilton College, had not just a 100% pass rate in 2025 but a 100% Bachelor’s pass rate. across both the IEB and Cambridge exams. Each candidate had an average of 2.4 distinctions. There was a total of 116 matric candidates in 2025.



South Africa’s second most expensive school, Michaelhouse, had a 100% pass rate in 2025 and a 99% Bachelor’s pass rate. Roedean School for Girls had a 100% Bachelor’s pass rate as well. 307 total distinctions across 73 students, averaging 4.21 distinctions per candidate.

TIPS ON DECIDING WHETHER THE SCHOOL IS REALLY WORTH THE MONEY

Aside from the exeptionally high pass rates and Bachelor’s pass rates, these schools also offer a variety of extra curricular activities and sports. This makes the schools worthwhile depending on your budget. You can review the type of sports and activities offered in comparison to what your child desires and what you feel is important.

Other factors to consider include university and career destinations. You can request real data on where recent graduates go. If an expensive school places students in the exact same universities as a local public school that costs much less, you can evaluate which would work better for you.



TOP TWO MOST-EXPENSIVE SCHOOLS DO NOT FOLLOW THE NSC EXAMS

The Top three most-expensive schools in SA do not follow the National Senior Certificate (NSC) exams. Instead, Hilton College students write the The Independent Examinations Board (IEB) and Cambridge Assessment International Education. Michaelhouse students also write the IEB exams.

Roedean School for Girls students do write the NSC exams. However, because Roedean is an independent school, its matric students write the NSC exams as administered and assessed by the Independent Examinations Board (IEB) rather than the state Department of Basic Education.

The NSC exams are currently underway for public schools across South Africa.



MATRIC EXAMS UNDERWAY IN SOUTH AFRICA

The NSC exams, officially began on Tuesday 13 October and runs until 26 November. The Department of Basic Education (DBE) minister Siviwe Gwarube said that the exams have been off to a positive start in a statement.

“The commencement of the 2026 National Senior Certificate examinations is an important moment for our learners and the basic education sector. Every examination represents an opportunity for learners to demonstrate the knowledge and skills they have acquired over the years,” said Minister Gwarube.

“We encourage the Class of 2026 to approach each paper with confidence, remain focused and give their very best. As a nation, we have a collective responsibility to support our learners as they take this important step towards their futures.”



A record 962 832 candidates registered are registered for the NSC 2026 exams. 815 051 are full-time and 147 781 part-time candidates. No major irregularities were reported.

Take a look at what happens if a learner is sick during the NSC exams here. Do you have any questions or tips to share with the 2026 candidates? Let us know in the comments below.

World.title: City of Tshwane announces an eight-hour power outage on Tuesday
World.content:
The City of Tshwane has announced an eight-hour planned electricity supply interruption affecting several areas in Soshanguve next week.

The city’s Energy and Electricity Business Unit will cut power on Tuesday, 20 October, to carry out critical electricity infrastructure refurbishment at the W Substation in Soshanguve.

The city’s Communication, Marketing and Events Department issued the media alert on 12 October.



Areas affected by the Tshwane power outage

According to the City of Tshwane, the outage will run from 8:00 until 16:00 and will affect the following areas:

Soshanguve Block X

Soshanguve Block V

Soshanguve Block W

Parts of Soshanguve Blocks KK, SS and R

The city said technicians will also energise the 11kV underground cables connected to the newly refurbished W Secondary Substation in Soshanguve as part of the work.

The municipality described the refurbishment as proactive work that forms part of ongoing efforts to improve the reliability, safety and continuity of electricity supply in the area.

The city also referred to the maintenance as rescheduled work, which suggests it had planned the refurbishment for an earlier date.

City urges residents to prepare and stay safe

The City of Tshwane urged affected customers to make the necessary arrangements to minimise the impact of the planned interruption.

Residents may want to charge their phones, power banks and rechargeable lights before 8:00 on Tuesday. Households can also prepare meals and boil water ahead of time and keep fridge and freezer doors closed to help food stay cold for longer.



Small businesses that depend on electricity, such as spaza shops, hair salons and car washes, may need to adjust their trading plans for the day.

The city urged customers to treat all electrical installations as live throughout the duration of the interruption. Residents should not touch, repair or tamper with any electrical equipment or cables while the work is under way.

The city apologised for the inconvenience the work may cause.

How to report power outages in Tshwane

Residents who experience problems with their electricity supply can contact the City of Tshwane through the following channels:

World.title: Eskom announces an eight-hour power outage in Gauteng on Thursday
World.content:
Eskom has announced an eight-hour electricity supply interruption affecting customers in parts of Ga-Rankuwa in Tshwane next week.

The power utility will switch off electricity on Thursday, 22 October, to carry out emergency maintenance on its distribution network.

Eskom shared the notice in its Gauteng Cluster Connect newsletter, developed by its Gauteng Communication and Stakeholder Management team.



Areas affected by the Eskom power outage

According to Eskom, the outage will affect customers in the following areas:

Makau

Mothutlung

Rantol Zone 3

Electricity will go off at 10:00, and Eskom expects to restore supply by 18:00, provided the work goes according to plan.

The utility said it needs the interruption to perform essential maintenance on its distribution power lines.



Because Eskom has classified the work as emergency maintenance, households and businesses in these areas have less than a week to prepare for a full working day without power.

Residents urged to stay safe

Eskom advised customers to treat all electrical appliances as live at all times during the outage.

This means residents should not touch, repair or tamper with any electrical equipment or power lines while the work is under way, as supply can return at any moment.



Residents may also want to charge their phones, power banks and rechargeable lights before 10:00 on Thursday. Keeping fridge and freezer doors closed as much as possible will help food stay cold for longer.

Small businesses that rely on electricity, such as spaza shops, hair salons and internet cafés, may need to adjust their trading hours or make backup arrangements for the day.

Eskom thanked customers for their cooperation and apologised for any inconvenience the maintenance may cause.



The utility also cautioned that the planned maintenance may not go ahead as communicated if circumstances beyond its control arise.

World.title: Tributes pour in for Lions player Hyron Andrews died in France
World.content:
PARIS - South African second-row forward Hyron Andrews of Johannesburg-based side the Lions was found dead at a hotel in France on Friday, on the eve of his team's Champions Cup match against La Rochelle, local authorities told AFP.

A source close to the investigation said the 31-year-old lock was found in cardiac arrest in a shower cubicle that was locked from the inside.

The public prosecutor in La Rochelle, western France, confirmed that an investigation had been opened to determine the cause of death, which occurred on the island of Ile de Re, and said that an accidental death was currently the leading line of inquiry.

An autopsy is due to be carried out, the source close to the investigation said.

"This devastating news has sent shockwaves through the international rugby community," the Lions said in a statement.

"The former Sharks and Sale Sharks lock forward was a valued member of the Lions family, and his loss will be felt profoundly by his teammates, coaches, supporters and all who had the privilege of knowing him."

Andrews had only returned to his native South Africa earlier this year after two years with English Prem side Sale Sharks. He began his career with the Sharks franchise in Durban and represented his country at Under-20 level.

"We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family, having recently joined us this season," added Lions chief executive Rudolf Straeuli.

"On behalf of... everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to (his wife) Maighlin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect."

Playing in 'honour of Hyron'

The Lions said Saturday's match against La Rochelle would go ahead as planned "in honour of Hyron".

It is the first time the Lions have played in the Champions Cup, which brings together the best European and South African clubs. A moment's silence will be held ahead of all Champions Cup and second-tier Challenge Cup matches this weekend in memory of Andrews.

"Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness," said Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union.

"His untimely passing is a devastating loss, and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.

"The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maighlin and all those mourning his loss."

Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson also paid tribute to Andrews, who played 45 times for the club after initially joining as injury cover at the end of the 2023-24 season.

"Hyron was just a brilliant guy and a brilliant teammate. He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with," said Sanderson.

"He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him."

The tragedy comes exactly 10 years to the day since the sudden death of former Munster coach Anthony Foley, who died in his sleep aged 42 due to a heart rhythm disorder just hours before his team were due to play against Racing 92 in Paris in the same competition.

La Rochelle coach Ronan O'Gara was a member of the Racing staff when Foley, a former Ireland international teammate, passed away in October 2016.

Bordeaux-Bègles are set to begin their bid for a record-equalling third straight Champions Cup crown later on Friday when they visit Gloucester in the tournament opener.

World.title: 'Sportswashing' or investment? Rwanda F1 stirs debate and doubts
World.content:
KIGALI - Viewed by some as "sportswashing" and by others as an overly ambitious, grandiose project, the prospect of a Formula 1 Grand Prix in Rwanda has provoked reaction at home and abroad.

The government touts the initiative as a significant "investment in Rwanda's future", slated for sometime in the early 2030s.

On Tuesday, Kigali put on a glitzy ceremony to announce the "historic" agreement between Rwanda, the organisation that owns Formula 1, and the International Automobile Federation (FIA).

A landlocked country still widely associated with a horrific genocide in 1994, Rwanda has used sports to revamp its image, attract tourists and impress investors with its organisational efficiency.

The event promises glamour, replete with champagne-quaffing celebrities, set against the backdrop of Rwanda's verdant hills and rich wildlife, all broadcast to a global audience.

Formula 1 markets itself as the third most-watched sporting event on the planet, trailing only the Olympic Games and the FIFA World Cup.

However, the project has drawn dismay from some quarters, including Amnesty International, which immediately condemned it as an act of sportswashing.

The NGO accuses Kigali of "buying into the world's biggest sports to polish its image and deflect from its appalling human rights record".

This same criticism has been levelled against Formula 1 on several previous occasions.

In its pursuit of global expansion, the sport has forged numerous partnerships with governments with questionable rights records, including China and Azerbaijan.

Sports diplomacy

Last year, Rwanda became the first African nation to successfully host the World Cycling Championships.

Through its "Visit Rwanda" campaign, Kigali also sponsors several major European football clubs, including Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), as well as the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers.

However, while President Paul Kagame is credited with a strategic vision that has driven Rwanda's economic transformation over his decades-long tenure, he has faced repeated accusations from opponents of suppressing political dissent.

Reacting to the news, Kenneth Roth, the former director of Human Rights Watch, noted on X Rwanda's "invasion via its M23 proxy of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo".

The armed M23 group, backed financially and militarily by Kigali, has forcibly seized vast swathes of the DRC.

During the Kigali ceremony, Kagame said it was an "honour" to be selected for Formula 1.

He described it as an "investment in Rwanda's future" that would bring "jobs, skills, tourism and new business to our country and our region for decades to come".

But one foreign attendee voiced concerns, telling AFP in English: "I am really hoping Rwanda is not chewing what it cannot swallow."

Formula 1 is an expensive pursuit and far wealthier nations have already seen their ambitions backfire.

The Qatar model

India and South Korea, which built circuits specifically to host Formula 1, eventually withdrew as their financial losses mounted.

European organisers, including those in France and, more recently, the Netherlands, have encountered similar setbacks.

In comparison, Rwanda, despite its economic boom, remains a low-income country with a GDP per capita barely exceeding $1,100.

It ranks 159 out of 193 countries on the United Nations' Human Development Index, although it is steadily improving.

Critics question whether the hundreds of millions of dollars required to build a modern racetrack might be better spent on healthcare or education, not to mention the tens of millions of dollars F1 Grand Prix organisers typically charge host countries for the privilege of holding the event.

A source close to the FIA said Qatar was "supporting" the Rwandan project.

The Gulf country is also building a new international airport in Bugesera, 40 kilometres (25 miles) from Kigali, near where the racetrack will be constructed.

Jean-Guy Africa, CEO of the Rwanda Development Board, pointed to the "tremendous interest" from the private sector.

"You cannot miss out on the 100,000 people who will come. From a business standpoint, you stand to benefit," he told AFP.

While several Rwandans told AFP of their pride that their country will soon host the pinnacle of motor sports, Kigali entrepreneur Amon Niyigena, took a more pragmatic view.

"The economics of hosting F1 in Rwanda will not be for everyone, but for a tiny percentage of the already rich," he said.

AFP

World.title: Real Madrid say Tebas must resign over Goebbels comparison
World.content:
MADRID - Real Madrid called on Friday for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he compared the club's efforts to discredit referees to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.

Tebas said in a post on X on Friday that Real Madrid's in-house TV channel often suggested that referees attempt to prevent the club from winning.

The outspoken Spanish league chief said these tactics "recall propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels".

Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with "those propaganda techniques" and not with the ideology of the Nazis.

Madrid responded by saying in a statement that Tebas' claims were "deeply offensive (and) morally repugnant".

It added that Madrid believe he is unfit to represent Spain's leading clubs and that he should consider "immediate resignation".

Coach Jose Mourinho has also claimed that Madrid are consistently penalised by referees.

Tebas has frequently clashed with Madrid's president Florentino Perez, especially over the club's plans to join a European Super League in 2021.

World.title: NBA tells sportsbooks to ban certain bets and parlays: report
World.content:
NEW YORK - The NBA told sportsbook partners in a Friday memo to ban certain types of bets and parlays this season that gamblers used in recent wagering scandals, ESPN reported.

The prohibition includes a player prop parlay and bets on "under" for players that were part of federal gambling cases that included NBA players Terry Rozier and Jontay Porter, according to the report.

The league directed authorized gambling partners, including FanDuel and DraftKings, not to offer bets on such areas as the winner of a game's opening tip-off, players on missing specific shots and under bets for players expected to see under 12 minutes of playing time.

"There's a balance between ensuring that we are removing problematic bet types but also ensuring that we don't just move activity into the illegal market," NBA executive vice president Scott Kaufman-Ross told ESPN.

"Where we landed right now, we think, is the right balance of those two objectives."

Sportsbooks will be banned from offering lines with larger payouts on under wagers.

NBA agreements with sportsbook partners permit the league to restrict what wagers they offer.

Federal prosecutors said one bettor wagered $80,000 on the under for six statistical categories for Porter in a Toronto Raptors game during the 2023-24 campaign for a $1.1 million payout.

Porter admitted removing himself from the game to benefit bettors.

Prosecutors claim Rozier was involved in a similar situation while with Charlotte in 2023, although Rozier has pleaded not guilty and denied any wrongdoing.

In another memo to clubs, the NBA noted new integrity measures to begin this season, with former NFL star and retired FBI agent Charles Tillman leading training on sport betting rules and enhanced AI looking for unusual betting patterns involving the NBA.

The memo said the league seeks to better protect players, coaches and other personnel from threats or harassment from bettors.

World.title: US influence, AI and mistrust cloud Alberta independence vote
World.content:
TORONTO - The run-up to a referendum in Canada's Alberta region on a future independence vote has been clouded by US political influence and AI-manipulated online content, leaving experts concerned that the results will be contested no matter the outcome.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday that he expected foreign governments, the "United States included", would not get involved in Canadian elections.

But the US is already on the scene.

President Donald Trump has launched a trade war and repeatedly claimed that Canada should be incorporated into the United States.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called Alberta a "natural partner," while Canada's Globe and Mail newspaper recently detailed contacts between separatist leaders in the province and US Republican operatives.

Canada's foreign influence transparency commissioner said in September his office was "aware of concerns" about non-Canadian activities around the Alberta referendum. The minority New Democratic Party (NDP) has advocated for a parliamentary debate on the issue.

"None of these things can be taken in a vacuum," NDP Member of Parliament Heather McPherson told AFP.

Close Trump allies have also inserted themselves into the online independence conversation.

Last week, tech billionaire Elon Musk posted on X after francophone Quebec's separatist party win: "They would be better off. Alberta and Saskatchewan should separate too."

Brian McQuinn, the co-director of the Centre for Artificial Intelligence, Data and Conflict at the University of Regina told AFP it "would be folly" to discount the impact this could have in Canada.

Along with Americans, McQuinn says he also observed Russian-linked activity pushing the most extreme aspects of the independence debate.

This may not directly sway voters but will at least raise the temperature, he said.

"If the fire is big and you fan it, it really gets bigger."

- AI amplification -

World.title: Four arrested in Soweto drug lab bust
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Another suspected drug lab has been found in Meadowlands, Soweto.

Four suspects have been arrested at what the SAPS calls a mandrax drug lab.

Friday's discovery follows several similar cases in recent weeks, including a multimillion-rand mandrax lab uncovered in Krugersdorp.

Gauteng Organised Crime Investigations officers are combing the Soweto scene for further evidence.

World.title: Turkey's Salt Lake, life in the shadow of drought
World.content:
ISTANBUL - Turkey's second-largest lake has become a stark symbol of a growing water crisis, with drought and intensive groundwater use threatening an ecosystem that supports wildlife, industry and tourism.

Known for its stunning natural beauty, Tuz Golu, Turkish for Salt Lake, is a shallow lake that stretches across the heart of central Anatolia about 150 kilometres (100 miles) south of Ankara, the capital.

One of the world's most saline lakes, Tuz Golu is an ecologically significant area that is Turkey’s most important breeding site for flamingos and one of the region's key nesting grounds.

At sunset, hundreds of flamingos feed in the lake’s waters, their pink and red wings creating striking images against the vast salt flats.

World.title: Swiss solar-powered plane altitude record confirmed
World.content:
BERN - Swiss pilot Raphael Domjan beat the altitude record for a solar-powered electric plane in a 2025 flight that took him soaring to 9,640 metres, the World Air Sports Federation (FAI) confirmed.

The FAI governing body, holding its 120th general conference in Lausanne from Wednesday to Friday, validated the record attempt after verifying the flight data.

The SolarStratos plane made the landmark flight from Sion airport in southwest Switzerland on August 12 last year, taking advantage of warm air thermals to beat a 15-year-old record.

The previous certified altitude record for a solar plane was 9,235 metres (30,298 feet).

Domjan's flight lasted five hours and nine minutes.

"After several months of verification and certification, FAI ratification now gives this achievement full international recognition," the SolarStratos team said a statement.

"SolarStratos officially becomes the highest-flying crewed electric and solar-powered aircraft in history."

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: From 'Chogo' to senator? Winnie Odinga steps into her own political spotlight
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

From Raila Odinga’s shadow to her own political path, Winnie sets her sights on the Nairobi Senate seat in 2027. [Courtesy]

The hat was more than a hat. Literally.

As Raila Odinga’s body made its final journey home from India, his youngest daughter, Winnie, held tightly to his familiar cream-coloured fedora. It was one of the few things she could still protect, a small piece of a man whose presence had filled her life and Kenya’s political imagination for decades.

The image of Winnie carrying her father’s hat was deeply personal. The country was mourning a political giant, but she was mourning her father.

A year later, on the first anniversary of Raila’s death, Winnie has announced her intention to contest the Nairobi Senate seat in the 2027 General Election.

The timing is poignant. On a day devoted to remembering her father, she has declared her own political ambitions, signalling a shift from being one of the most recognisable faces of the Odinga family to a politician seeking a mandate in her own right.

“As Edwin Sifuna seeks a higher office, I see an opportunity in Nairobi, which is why I have decided I will vie for Senator of Nairobi County,” she said.

And just like that, the conversation shifted from the daughter who carried Baba’s hat to the politician who wants a seat of her own.

The last-born girl

To many Kenyans, Winnie is Chogo, the last-born child of Raila and Ida Odinga. The nickname carries the familiarity of family life, a reminder that behind the powerful surname is a daughter who grew up in a household where politics was never far from the conversation.

Her father was no ordinary political figure. His name could summon crowds, ignite debate and divide opinion. His decades-long career placed the Odinga family at the centre of Kenya’s political story.

Growing up as Raila’s youngest daughter meant sharing him with a country that claimed a piece of his time, energy and, eventually, his final goodbye.

Yet Winnie was not simply a spectator in her father’s political world. She worked around his campaigns and communications before stepping into politics herself, eventually winning a seat in the East African Legislative Assembly.

In November 2022, Parliament elected her to represent Kenya in the regional legislature, where she took office in December that year. Based in Arusha, Tanzania, she became part of the East African Community’s legislative institution, serving a five-year term running to 2027.

The EALA offered Winnie a political platform beyond her father’s immediate circle and an opportunity to participate in regional affairs. Her current tenure has also given her experience in legislative politics before her proposed move into elective politics at home.

The Nairobi Senate bid would take her into a different contest, one in which voters will have to decide whether her experience, ideas and political programme merit their support.

The hat she could not let go

For years, Raila’s trademark headgear had been part of his public identity, appearing at political rallies, meetings and public ceremonies. But in Winnie’s hands, it became something else: a personal possession tied to the final journey of a daughter and her father

She explained how protective she had been of it throughout the journey, describing it as one of the few things she could still hold on to.

The image captured a kind of helplessness that public figures’ families rarely get to show. Crowds could mourn Raila, politicians could speak of his legacy, and supporters could debate who would inherit his political movement. Winnie, however, had been left with the painful task of bringing her father home.

The symbolism of the hat has since acquired another layer. At a ceremony in Bondo earlier this month, elders placed a traditional hat on Winnie’s head in a symbolic gesture associated with the possibility of her carrying forward her father’s political mantle.

Winnie’s political journey has not started with this Senate announcement.

Her election to the East African Legislative Assembly placed her among Kenya’s representatives in a regional institution whose work concerns cooperation among East African Community partner states.

The role gave her a platform in regional legislation while her father remained a central figure in national politics.

The Senate is responsible for representing counties, participating in lawmaking on matters concerning counties and exercising oversight over revenue allocated to county governments. A Nairobi senator must therefore make a case on issues that touch residents directly, from public spending and service delivery to the accountability of county leadership.

The capital is also a demanding political terrain. Its electorate is diverse, its concerns immediate and its contests fiercely competitive.

A famous surname may open doors, but it cannot replace a convincing programme on jobs, housing, transport, healthcare and the management of public resources.

Winnie will have to demonstrate that she understands Nairobi beyond its place in her father’s national political story.

Can she translate the loyalty associated with Raila into support for her own agenda? Can she persuade voters that she is more than the daughter of a political icon?

Those questions will follow her into the campaign.

The Odingaism

Political inheritance can be both an advantage and a burden.

Raila’s name carries a formidable history of opposition politics, democratic reform and a loyal support base. It also invites comparisons that few politicians have to contend with.

Winnie’s challenge will be to honour that history without allowing it to become the entirety of her political identity.

Raila’s death left a space in the Orange Democratic Movement and among supporters who had looked to him for direction through decades of political contests. The question of who will carry his legacy has inevitably turned towards his family and the wider political movement he helped build.

Winnie’s Senate bid will require her to turn recognition into a political proposition that voters can interrogate. Her experience at EALA gives her a legislative starting point; the Nairobi contest will demand that she demonstrate how that experience can serve residents of the capital.

She must also navigate the expectations attached to her father’s name while making room for her own ideas, priorities and leadership style.

There is a temptation to see Winnie’s future entirely through the lens of inheritance. She is Raila’s daughter, the last-born known as Chogo, the woman who carried his hat and the politician whom some supporters hope will continue his legacy.

But she is also a woman making a decision about her own future.

The Senate bid offers her an opportunity to define what that future means, beyond the grief surrounding her father’s death and the weight of a name that has shaped Kenyan politics for decades.

The hat remains an unforgettable image from Raila’s final journey home. A daughter attempted to protect the last tangible thing she could hold on to.

The Senate will demand something different: a political vision, a campaign and the votes of Nairobi residents.

Chogo has announced her next move. Will Winnie Odinga turn the memory of Baba into a mandate of her own?

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
