World.title: Axel Kicillof: Governor at the Center of Peronism
World.content:
Axel Kicillof, right, with then Colombian President Gustavo Petro in Barcelona, Spain, on 17 April 2026 (Photo: Presidencia de Colombia, public domain, via Flickr and Wikimedia Commons)

ARGENTINA · PROFILE

Key Facts — The country Argentina is a federation whose largest province, Buenos Aires, is governed by Axel Kicillof, a Peronist economist.

— Why it matters Kicillof is the opposition figure the government now treats as its likely 2027 challenger, and he leads a camp that rivals Cristina Kirchner’s.

— Why now On Friday 16 October the government named Kicillof as the risk for governors, while his own movement keeps expanding across provinces.

— What happened Kicillof won the governorship in 2019 and again in 2023, and on 12 October his movement added backers in Mendoza and Córdoba.

— The numbers He took 52.4% of votes for candidates in 2019 and 44.94% in 2023, and his second term ends in December 2027.

— What it means for you US investors in Argentine assets are watching whether a Peronist with a record of state intervention becomes a serious 2027 contender.

— Still open Whether he runs, whether Cristina Kirchner’s camp backs him, and how the Peronists choose their candidate.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Axel Kicillof a 29.5% chance of winning the 2027 presidency and Javier Milei 49.5% (16 October, 2:15 p.m. ET).

— Power Index Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 61.2 points (October 2026 edition).

Axel Kicillof is the governor of Buenos Aires Province and the Peronist whom the government now points to as President Javier Milei’s likely rival in 2027. He has not said whether he will run for president, yet his own movement is spreading across the country.

Axel Kicillof in One Page

Kicillof was born in 1971 in the city of Buenos Aires and graduated with honours in economics from the University of Buenos Aires, his official biography says. He taught economic thought there and wrote books, including a 2007 title called “Volver a Keynes”.

He lives in the official governor’s residence in La Plata, the provincial capital, the same biography says. On 15 October he told an interviewer the province produces about 40% of national tax revenue, a claim Perfil reported as his own.

From Economics Professor to Minister

Kicillof took his first public posts in 2011, and his biography says he became Secretary of Economic Policy when Cristina Fernández de Kirchner began her second term. In that job he took what he calls a key role in the nationalisation of the oil company YPF, then held by Spain’s Repsol.

Fernández named him Economy Minister on 20 November 2013, MinutoUno recalled in its 2013 yearbook. The same report says he had long argued for strong state intervention in the economy.

He served until 2015, and his biography says he took part in the Paris Club deal and in the talks with so-called holdout creditors. The Paris Club is a group of creditor governments, and the holdouts bought defaulted Argentine bonds cheaply before suing for full payment.

In 2015 he was elected a national deputy for the city of Buenos Aires, according to his biography. From that seat he criticised the economic policy of then-President Mauricio Macri.

How He Won the Governorship

In October 2019 Kicillof won the Buenos Aires governorship with 52.4% of votes for candidates, against 38.28% for the Juntos por el Cambio ticket, the provincial electoral board’s final count shows. His opponent was the sitting governor, María Eugenia Vidal.

In October 2023 he won re-election with 44.94% of votes for candidates, ahead of Juntos por el Cambio on 26.61% and Milei’s La Libertad Avanza on 24.57%, the board’s count shows. Milei went on to win the presidency, which left Kicillof leading the province where Peronism stayed strongest.

Fuerza Patria, the Peronist alliance, led the alliance of La Libertad Avanza by 47.18% to 33.77% in the provincial legislative vote of 7 September 2025, Chequeado reported from the provisional official count with about 95% of polling stations counted. Kicillof was not on that ballot, which chose provincial lawmakers and councillors.

Article 123 of the provincial constitution allows one re-election and then requires a gap of one term, and La Nación applied that to Kicillof in 2024. His term therefore ends in December 2027, whatever he decides about the presidency.

Kicillof and the Kirchner Legacy

Kirchnerismo is the Peronist current of ex-president Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, under whom Kicillof served as minister. Infobae reports that she has a final six-year prison sentence and a lifetime ban from public office in the Vialidad case.

Her son Máximo Kirchner, a national deputy who leads the group La Cámpora, said on 24 September that his camp wants her to be the 2027 candidate, Perfil reported. Infobae reported on 14 October that he still backs her, saying “for now, my candidate is Cristina”.

Kicillof has led the Buenos Aires branch of the Peronist PJ party since February 2026, iProfesional reported. Máximo Kirchner heads the party congress, and the party document repeated its rejection of her conviction.

Infobae wrote on 14 October that relations between the two camps are at one of their tensest points. It said Carlos Bianco, who heads Kicillof’s provincial cabinet, left open that the governor would not subordinate himself to her leadership.

Kicillof’s circle wants to avoid a double command and build its own option for 2027, Infobae reports. The Kirchner camp wants him to recognise her leadership again, and people close to him say he will not do so openly.

Juan Grabois, a national deputy who leads the group Patria Grande, said that if Kirchner is not a candidate “it is obvious the candidate is Axel”. Infobae reports that Grabois is not part of Kicillof’s movement.

The Movement Built Around Him

Kicillof’s own vehicle is the Movimiento Derecho al Futuro, known as the MDF, launched in Buenos Aires Province on 22 February 2025. It was presented nationally on 19 September 2026 in Avellaneda with ten thematic commissions, El Destape reports.

On 12 October El Destape reported that the MDF had added figures from Mendoza and Córdoba after visits to Misiones, Chaco, Corrientes, La Pampa and Tierra del Fuego. At the Avellaneda launch Kicillof said “a national alternative is not built from an office”.

On Saturday 17 October, Peronist Loyalty Day, Kicillof is due to lead an MDF event in González Catán, in La Matanza, Infobae reports. The Kirchner camp plans a separate gathering outside her flat in Buenos Aires.

What He Says About Milei

At the university march on Thursday 15 October, Kicillof said Milei’s emergency decree known as DNU 70 and the university cuts run against what major powers do, Perfil reports. He argued that those powers are returning to protectionism and industrial policy.

Perfil also reports his own claims about almost seven years in office, including the equivalent of 1,000 new schools and 8,300 homes under construction. These figures come from Kicillof and were not checked against provincial records.

Cabinet Chief Diego Santilli replied on 16 October that governors should worry if Kicillof wins, as our report Santilli Warns Governors on Kicillof, 16 Oct explains. How the vote works and where polls stand is in Kicillof vs Milei: Argentina’s 2027 Election Explained.

What It Means for You

Perfil reported on 16 October that diplomats have asked to attend corporate events to gauge the business mood before 2027. It quoted an unnamed corporate leader who said “Kicillof is a direct return to the past”.

That is one business view, and Perfil adds that Kicillof’s recent New York tour made a candidacy look possible. For US holders of Argentine bonds and shares, his record of state intervention, from YPF to price programmes, is the reason investors watch him.

Nothing in a profile changes any rule for travellers or investors today, and no candidacy exists yet to price. The wider map of power is in Argentina Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026 and Who Dominates Argentina, Elites and Regions Explained.

What Is Not Known

On 15 October Kicillof said he will be “where I have to be” and did not confirm a run, Perfil reports. No source reviewed says whether he, Kirchner or a third name will lead the Peronist ticket.

Whether the ban on Kirchner holding office can be lifted is not known, though her defence is pursuing international bodies, Infobae reports. Her camp’s push therefore depends on a legal outcome that no source reviewed predicts.

The reports reviewed do not set out a national economic programme from Kicillof. No source reviewed gives a settled poll of how he would fare against Milei, so no one can say who leads today.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket’s market on the 2027 presidential winner priced Kicillof at 29.5% on Friday 16 October (2:15 p.m. ET), second to Milei at 49.5%. The trading volume on Kicillof is about US$136,000, out of roughly US$927,000 across the whole market.

His price stood at 32.5% through 15 October before sliding to 29.5% on 16 October, while Milei fell from about 55% to 49.5% and Sergio Massa, the former Economy Minister and 2023 presidential candidate, rose from about 7% to about 16%. Cristina Kirchner trades near 1.4% and Máximo Kirchner near 0.6%, far below Kicillof among Kirchner-linked names.

These are real-money bets, not polls, and the market does not explain its own moves. Thin trading in the smaller contracts can swing prices quickly.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Axel Kicillof?

He is the governor of Buenos Aires Province, an economist and a Peronist who was Argentina’s Economy Minister from 2013 to 2015. He won the governorship in 2019 and was re-elected in 2023.

Has Kicillof said he will run for president in 2027?

No, on 15 October he said only that he will be “where I have to be”. He is building the MDF movement and wants a wide opposition alliance.

Why is Kicillof linked to kirchnerismo?

He served as Economy Minister under Cristina Fernández de Kirchner and rose through her political camp. He is now in an open dispute with her son Máximo over who sets the direction of Peronism.

Can Kicillof run for governor again in 2027?

No, La Nación noted in 2024 that he is in his second term and cannot seek a third. His term ends in December 2027.

What is the Movimiento Derecho al Futuro?

It is Kicillof’s political movement, launched in Buenos Aires Province on 22 February 2025. It was presented nationally on 19 September 2026 and is adding local leaders in other provinces.

What does Kicillof mean for US investors?

Some business circles see him as a return to state-led policy, while his supporters stress his record on production and jobs. No candidacy exists yet, so the effect today is on how markets read the 2027 calendar.

World.title: Court Blocks Salvador Honour for Flávio
World.content:
A voter casts a presidential ballot on an electronic voting machine in Brasília. File photo, 2014. (Photo: Marri Nogueira/Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Friday, 16 October 2026, 2:37 p.m. ET · Source: Estadão and Folha de S.Paulo, citing a Bahia state court order

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, votes in a presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Friday 16 October, a judge in Bahia state barred the Salvador city council from handing Flávio Bolsonaro the city’s citizen title at his campaign rally on Saturday 17 October.

The ruling Judge Carla Graziela Costantino de Araújo said the timing could interfere with the runoff and set a fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000) for non-compliance.

What stays The honour itself is not cancelled, and the order does not cancel the rally, but the official handover must wait until the election process ends.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.6% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (16 October, 2:37 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 77% and Kalshi at 78% (Lula: 23% and 24% ), as of 16 October, 2:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open Councillor Cezar Leite, who proposed the honour, says he will appeal.

A Bahia state judge has barred the Salvador city council from giving Flávio Bolsonaro the city’s citizen title at his Saturday campaign rally, nine days before the Brazil election 2026 runoff. The ruling, signed on Friday 16 October, says holding the ceremony now could interfere with the 25 October vote.

Flávio Bolsonaro, a conservative senator for Rio de Janeiro and the candidate of the Liberal Party (PL), faces President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers’ Party (PT). Salvador is the capital of Bahia state in north-eastern Brazil.

What the Bahia Court Decided

Judge Carla Graziela Costantino de Araújo of Salvador’s 5th Public Treasury Court, which hears cases against public bodies, granted an urgent preliminary order, known in Brazil as a liminar. A retiree, Maria Lúcia Andrade da Silva, had filed a citizen’s lawsuit (ação popular) against the ceremony, Estadão reported.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The order says the handover must wait until the 2026 electoral process has ended for good. It also suspends the council’s plan to move its seat to the Farol da Barra, a lighthouse landmark in Salvador where the rally is held.

Failure to comply without justification carries a single fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000, at R$5.07 per US dollar, EODHD rate of 16 October). The fine applies from the moment the council is notified.

A hand presses the confirm key on a Brazilian electronic voting machine. File photo, 2021. (Photo: Superior Electoral Court of Brazil, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

Why the Judge Stepped In

The judge wrote that the timing and the venue could turn an official ceremony into an event with a promotional or partisan character in favour of a presidential candidate, Estadão reported. She also found that moving the council’s seat would need extra staff, security and temporary structures, at a disproportionate public cost.

The council had argued that giving honours is a political act within lawmakers’ discretion and that a block risked irreversible harm. The judge answered that postponing the handover harms neither the council nor Flávio, because it can take place after the election, Estadão reported.

What the Order Does Not Do

The ruling leaves the council’s resolution granting the title intact, so Flávio keeps the honour on paper. It does not cancel the campaign rally, only the official handover and the move of the council’s seat.

Councillor Cezar Leite of the PL, who proposed the honour, said he will appeal, Folha de S.Paulo reported. The council had already approved the title, so the dispute is about the timing of the handover and not the title itself.

What It Means for US Readers

Court rulings that touch the campaign can still shape the final days before the runoff. This one is narrow, since it moves a ceremony and does not remove a candidate’s rights or change any vote.

Investors in Brazilian assets and US-listed Brazilian shares can read it as a sign that courts are policing the line between public office and campaigning. The Brazil runoff poll tracker lists the latest surveys, in which the two candidates are close.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.6% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (16 October, 2:37 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has about US$184.8 million in total bets.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether an appeal will be decided before Saturday’s rally. It is also not known whether the ceremony will take place after the election, as the judge suggested.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did a Brazilian court block the Salvador citizen title ceremony for Flávio Bolsonaro?

A Bahia judge said handing over the title at a campaign rally days before the runoff could interfere with the election and give an official act a promotional or partisan character. She postponed the handover until after the election process ends.

Does the ruling cancel Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign rally?

No. It bars only the official handover and the move of the council’s seat to the Farol da Barra, Estadão reported.

What is the penalty if Salvador’s council ignores the order?

A single fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000) for unjustified non-compliance. The order applies from the moment the council is notified.

Can the decision be appealed?

Councillor Cezar Leite, who proposed the honour, said he will appeal. It is not yet known when or whether a higher court will rule.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October, nine days after this ruling. The candidates are President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

World.title: Cuba Power Outages After Santa Cruz Fire: What Next
World.content:
A large building lit up at night in Havana; file photo from February 2023, not taken at the time of the Santa Cruz del Norte fire (Photo: Bruno Rijsman, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

CUBA · WHAT NEXT

Key Facts — The country Cuba, a Caribbean island of about 9.4 million people, runs a state-owned grid that has collapsed completely eight times in 2026.

— Why it matters The grid has almost no spare capacity, so every plant lost raises the odds of longer outages and of another island-wide collapse.

— Why now A fire took out unit 1 of the Santa Cruz del Norte plant on Friday 16 October, and the Felton plant briefly went offline hours later.

— What happened The state utility Unión Eléctrica (UNE) forecast evening outages of 2,190 MW, with 740 MW available against demand of 2,900 MW.

— The numbers Thursday’s worst outage reached 2,094 MW at 7:30 p.m., above plan, and nine units were listed as broken down or in maintenance on Friday morning.

— What it means for you Plan for blackouts of 20 hours or more and for delays to travel, family and business plans tied to Cuba.

— Still open Whether the Guiteras and Santa Cruz unit 1 return soon enough, and Felton stays online, to avoid a ninth nationwide collapse.

— Power Index Cuba ranks 14th of 14 in Cuba ranks 14th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 22.5 points (October 2026 edition).

Cuba power outages look set to stay severe after the Santa Cruz del Norte fire, because unit 1 of that plant has no repair date and the grid has almost no spare capacity. The state utility UNE forecast evening outages of 2,190 MW for Friday 16 October, and the Felton plant went offline at 11:31 a.m. before apparently returning about an hour later.

For US readers, the risk is practical, since longer blackouts disrupt travel, hotels, family contact and any firm or aid group with Cuban partners. This piece looks ahead at what could worsen or ease the shortage over the coming days.

Where the Grid Stands After the Fire

At 6 a.m. on Friday the UNE reported 740 MW available against demand of 2,260 MW, an outage of 1,540 MW, before the fire began at 6:55 a.m., Martí Noticias and CiberCuba report. For the evening peak it forecast the same 740 MW against 2,900 MW of demand, a deficit of 2,160 MW and outages of 2,190 MW.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Cuba ranks 14th of 14 with 22.5 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (53); weakest: economic weight (0). Alignment group: Closer to Beijing. Some pillar data are incomplete for Cuba; see the index notes. WatchNo sovereign rating; economy contracting (-3.8%); incomplete data (‡). See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The 2,190 MW forecast equals about 75.5% of the 2,900 MW demand, which EFE called the highest rate since the UNE began publishing statistics in 2022, topping the 74% of 29 July, Infobae and OnCuba report. Thursday’s worst outage reached 2,094 MW at 7:30 p.m., above plan because of problems at Cienfuegos units 3 and 4 and Santa Cruz unit 2, the UNE said.

The UNE’s Friday morning list showed six units broken down, among them Santa Cruz units 1 and 2, the Guiteras, Felton unit 2 and Renté units 3 and 6, CiberCuba reports. Three more were in maintenance, and thermal generation limits alone came to 394 MW, the same outlet says.

The UNE announced at 11:31 a.m. that the Felton plant in Mayarí, Holguín, was offline, without naming the unit or the cause, CiberCuba and Periódico Cubano report. CiberCuba’s outage tracker later logged Felton back in line at 12:35 p.m., a notice we could not trace to a UNE post we could open.

That announcement came after the morning forecast, so the 2,190 MW figure does not reflect it, and 14ymedio recalls that Felton unit 2 has been out since a July 2022 accident. The UNE had published no new forecast by mid-afternoon in Havana, so the evening gap may differ from the morning figure.

The fire was controlled by about 9 a.m. and fully out by 10:24 a.m., according to the authorities quoted by 14ymedio, and the Energy and Mines Ministry said no one was injured. The UNE and state radio say an oil leak at the front of the rotor started it, a cause that only state sources have given.

What Could Make Cuba Power Outages Worse

A collapse needs a trigger, and OnCuba reports that the 18 September failure followed transmission faults that cut the west, with the UNE blaming the trip of a section of the 220 kV Matanzas-Cienfuegos line. The eight collapses of 2026 also came in clusters, with two inside a week in March, three in eight days in July and two in under 24 hours in August, OnCuba’s timeline shows.

Recovery is slow once the whole system drops, as the UNE linked Pinar del Río to Holguín only 28 hours after the 6 July collapse, OnCuba reported. After the 10 July collapse all provinces were reconnected almost 40 hours later, and the Guiteras did not restart after the 14 July one, OnCuba’s timeline shows.

The Guiteras in Matanzas went out again on Wednesday 14 October with a leak in a boiler economizer, after a steam leak had forced it off on 9 October, Periódico Cubano reports. The plant gave no restart date and must cool before repairs can begin.

OnCuba recalls that Guiteras exits set off national collapses in October and December 2024, and officials admit a large capital-maintenance debt there. A full overhaul that would stop the plant for months has been postponed repeatedly, most recently in late 2025, the outlet adds.

Partial failures add to the strain without counting among the eight collapses, and the UNE said an oscillation on 27 August cut the east from Holguín to Guantánamo, OnCuba reported. It took out Felton unit 1, Nuevitas unit 6 and Renté unit 6 at once, according to the UNE notice OnCuba cited, which is why the east is watched closely.

Fuel sets the ceiling, because Energy and Mines Minister Vicente de la O Levy says private imports meet under 3% of needs and no state company has a supply contract, OnCuba and Periódico Cubano reported on 14 October. The US fuel that does arrive goes to private businesses and has not ended the outages, he says.

What Could Ease the Shortfall

The UNE said units 2 and 3 at Santa Cruz del Norte were preparing to restart after the fire, 14ymedio reports. Unit 2 was listed as broken down and unit 3 as in maintenance that morning, and no restart time or output was given.

De la O Levy credited recent maintenance, new renewables and cooler weather after summer for restoring some capacity, Directorio Cubano reported on 12 October, and we could not check his original remarks. Evening demand is forecast at 2,900 MW, against the 3,200 MW or more that OnCuba put on demand in early August.

Past collapses were reversed within about two days, and Felton’s reported quick return on Friday shows that some plants can come back fast. The Guiteras and Santa Cruz returning together would narrow the gap fastest, though the sources give no date for either.

What to Watch Over the Next Days

Start with the UNE’s daily forecast, which shows whether Cuba power outages stay near 2,200 MW or climb. A result above plan, as on Thursday, is itself a warning sign.

Next watch the three big plants, the Guiteras, Felton and Santa Cruz unit 1, since each one lost widens the evening gap. Any trip of the 220 kV Matanzas-Cienfuegos line also deserves attention, as it preceded the 18 September collapse.

What It Means for You

Travellers should expect blackouts of 20 hours or more in many places, as CiberCuba reported for recent days, and should ask lodgings about generators or batteries. Ten airports have no jet fuel until at least 1 November, according to Periódico Cubano’s reading of aeronautical notices, so confirm flights before travelling.

Relatives and firms with Cuban partners should plan for interrupted operations and treat the UNE’s daily forecast as the best guide to each evening. The fire is reported in our news story Cuba Thermoelectric Plant Fire Hits Unit 1 and the wider causes in our explainer Cuba Energy Crisis Explained: Why the Grid Keeps Failing.

Earlier strain in the east is covered in Cuba Grid Splits in East as 1,680 MW Shortfall Looms, and the 18 September collapse in Cuba Grid Failure: Line Trips, Not Gunfire, Caused 8th Blackout of 2026. Airport fuel limits are covered in Cuba Airports Lack Jet Fuel Until 1 November.

What Is Not Known

It is not known when Santa Cruz unit 1 or the Guiteras will return, which Felton unit dropped out, or whether Felton is still online. The UNE had published no recalculated forecast in the sources we reviewed, and its evening report was not yet out when we checked.

The oil-leak cause comes only from the UNE and state radio, and nobody independent has confirmed it. No source gives a damage estimate, although CiberCuba says the images show severe damage to the unit and its roof.

Nothing in the sources shows whether a ninth nationwide collapse will happen, since the daily UNE forecasts we reviewed cover outages and not the risk of collapse. How much of the shortfall stems from US fuel pressure and how much from ageing plants is also not settled by the sources reviewed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will Cuba have another nationwide blackout?

No source says so, and the daily figures cannot forecast a collapse. OnCuba counts eight in 2026, often in clusters, so the risk is real while several units are out.

How big are the Cuba power outages after the Santa Cruz fire?

The UNE forecast outages of 2,190 MW for Friday evening, with 740 MW available against demand of 2,900 MW. The UNE had published no new forecast after Felton’s brief outage when we checked.

Which plants matter most over the next few days?

The Guiteras in Matanzas and Santa Cruz del Norte unit 1 are out, and Felton in Holguín dropped offline briefly on Friday. The 220 kV Matanzas-Cienfuegos line also matters, since a trip there preceded the 18 September collapse.

How long do blackouts last after a total collapse?

The UNE linked Pinar del Río to Holguín 28 hours after the 6 July collapse, and all provinces were back almost 40 hours after the 10 July one, OnCuba reports. OnCuba says the July recoveries were hampered by a lack of fuel.

What should travellers to Cuba do?

Ask lodgings about generators or batteries and expect long power cuts. Ten airports have no jet fuel until at least 1 November, so confirm flights before travelling.

Sources: CiberCuba on Felton, 16 October 2026; CiberCuba on the fire, 16 October 2026; CiberCuba on the aftermath, 16 October 2026; Periódico Cubano on Felton, 16 October 2026; Periódico Cubano on the Guiteras, 14 October 2026; Periódico Cubano on airports, 14 October 2026; Periódico Cubano on fuel, 14 October 2026; 14ymedio, 16 October 2026; Martí Noticias, 16 October 2026; OnCuba on the fire, 16 October 2026; OnCuba, 18 September 2026; OnCuba, 7 August 2026; OnCuba, 14 October 2026; Directorio Cubano, 12 October 2026; Infobae, relaying EFE, 16 October 2026; OnCuba, 27 August 2026; CiberCuba outage tracker, 16 October 2026. Grid figures come from the Unión Eléctrica (UNE) daily reports as carried by these outlets.

World.title: Brazil Poll Puts Flávio at 50.5%, Lula 49.5%
World.content:
Flávio Bolsonaro at the Senate presiding table during a plenary session on 9 July 2024, beside then Senate president Rodrigo Pacheco (Photo: Waldemir Barreto/Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Key Facts Published Friday, 16 October, 2:19 p.m. ET. Source: CNT/MDA survey, registered with the electoral court (TSE) as BR-00652/2026.

What happened The CNT/MDA poll, released on Friday 16 October, shows Flávio Bolsonaro with 50.5% of valid votes and Lula with 49.5% in the 25 October runoff.

The numbers In total voting intentions Flávio has 46.8% and Lula 45.9%, with 4.9% blank or null and 2.4% undecided. The margin of error is 2.2 points.

What changed In the 3 October CNT/MDA survey Lula led a runoff simulation 47.3% to 43.1%, so the 4.2-point gap has turned into a 0.9-point lead for Flávio.

Fieldwork 2,002 voters aged 16 or older were interviewed from 13 to 15 October, with 95% confidence.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.5% chance of winning the runoff and Lula 22.5% (16 October, 2:17 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 77% and Kalshi at 78% (Lula: 23% and 24% ), as of 16 October, 2:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

A new CNT/MDA poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, ahead of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, by 50.5% to 49.5% of valid votes in the Brazil election 2026 runoff. The survey was released on Friday 16 October, and the gap counts as a technical tie.

It matters because the vote on Sunday 25 October decides who runs Latin America’s largest economy, which affects Brazilian stocks, the real and trade with Washington. Our Brazil election polls lists every runoff survey so far.

What the CNT/MDA Runoff Poll Found

The National Transport Confederation (CNT), a Brazilian business group, commissioned the survey from the pollster MDA. MDA interviewed 2,002 voters aged 16 or older from 13 to 15 October, with a margin of error of 2.2 points, O Liberal reported.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Flávio Bolsonaro has 46.8% of total voting intentions and Lula 45.9%, with 4.9% blank or null and 2.4% undecided, according to Bahia Notícias. Valid votes, which leave out blank and null answers, split 50.5% to 49.5%.

The presiding table of the Federal Senate chamber in Brasília. File photo. Photo: Boaventuravinicius, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

How the Race Moved in Two Weeks

In the previous CNT/MDA survey, published on 3 October, Lula led a runoff simulation 47.3% to 43.1%, Bahia Notícias reported. In total voting intentions Flávio has gained 3.7 points and Lula has lost 1.4.

Other pollsters also show a close race. Datafolha had Flávio ahead 51% to 49% in valid votes on 15 October, O Povo reported, and Quaest had him at 46% against 44% in total votes on 14 October, according to O Liberal.

Brazil’s Federal Senate plenary in Brasília. File photo. Photo: Senado Federal - TV Senado, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

What a Technical Tie Means

A technical tie means the gap is smaller than the margin of error. With 2.2 points of error on each number, this survey cannot say which candidate is truly ahead.

Polls also differ in method and timing, so one survey is a snapshot of the days of the interviews. The trend across several pollsters says more than any single number.

What It Means for US Readers

If you hold Brazilian stocks, bonds or US-listed shares of Brazilian companies, a race this close can mean price swings until the result is known. The winner will also set the tone of Brazil’s relations with Washington on trade and tariffs.

Neither candidate is a certain winner, because every recent poll sits inside or near its margin of error.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, traders give Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.5% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (16 October, 2:17 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has about US$184.7 million in total trades, and Brazil election odds covers it in full.

Prices are bets, not polls, and they can move within minutes of a new survey. Kalshi, a market regulated in the US by the CFTC, also lists runoff contracts.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the late-week news, including the Senate vote to end the 6×1 work schedule, has moved voters, because the interviews ended on 15 October. The size of any shift will show only in the next surveys.

It is also unknown how many undecided voters, 2.4% in this survey, will turn out on 25 October or which way they will go. A poll measures opinion, and it does not forecast the result.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who leads Brazil’s latest runoff poll?

Flávio Bolsonaro leads the CNT/MDA poll released on 16 October with 50.5% of valid votes to Lula’s 49.5%. The gap is a technical tie.

What is the margin of error of the CNT/MDA poll?

It is 2.2 percentage points at 95% confidence, based on 2,002 interviews from 13 to 15 October. The one-point gap is inside that margin.

How did the CNT/MDA poll change since 3 October?

Lula led a runoff simulation 47.3% to 43.1% on 3 October. Now Flávio has 46.8% to Lula’s 45.9% in total voting intentions.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October, nine days after this poll was released. The winner takes office as president for a four-year term.

Who is behind the CNT/MDA poll?

The National Transport Confederation (CNT), a Brazilian business group, commissioned it and the pollster MDA carried it out. It is registered with the electoral court as BR-00652/2026.

World.title: Rodrigo Paz Pereira Profile: The Bolivian Facing Kast
World.content:
The Palacio Quemado, the presidential palace on Plaza Murillo in La Paz (Photo: P. Hughes, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BOLIVIA · PROFILE

Key Facts — The country Bolivia is a landlocked Andean nation whose trade depends on Chilean ports, and it has had no ambassadors in Chile since 1978.

— Who he is Rodrigo Paz Pereira is Bolivia’s president since 8 November 2025 and a former deputy, mayor of Tarija from 2015 to 2020 and senator.

— Why it matters Paz decides how far Bolivia opens to Chile on trade, mining and borders, and he is doing so while old claims over sea access still divide his country.

— Why now Chile’s President José Antonio Kast made the first state visit by a Chilean president to Bolivia in 71 years on Friday 16 October.

— What happened Kast and Paz met at the Palacio Quemado in La Paz, and Paz said afterwards that it was time to turn dialogue into concrete agreements.

— The numbers He won the 19 October 2025 runoff with 3,519,534 votes, or 54.96%, against 45.04% for his rival Jorge Quiroga.

— What it means for you A working Paz-Kast channel could ease cargo, mining and border rules for investors, while domestic critics limit how far Paz can move on sea access.

— Still open What the joint declaration says, whether ambassadors return and how the timber case and the sea claim are handled.

— Power Index Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 in Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 28.4 points (October 2026 edition). Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

This Rodrigo Paz Pereira profile looks at the man who received Chile’s President José Antonio Kast in La Paz on Friday 16 October, the first state visit by a Chilean leader in 71 years. Paz is an economist and former Tarija mayor whose father also led Bolivia, and he has staked his foreign policy on trade rather than old quarrels.

For US readers, his stance matters because Bolivian cargo, mining projects and border controls all run through Chile. The day-by-day account of the visit is in Kast Meets Rodrigo Paz in Bolivia Friday, and the history behind it in Chile Bolivia Relations: Kast Visit Explained.

A Rodrigo Paz Pereira Profile: Exile, Family and Schooling

Paz was born in 1967 in Santiago de Compostela, Spain, while his parents were in exile, BioBioChile reports. His father, Jaime Paz Zamora, was president of Bolivia from 1989 to 1993.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 with 28.4 points. Strongest pillar: military means (55); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (13). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (CCC+); economy contracting (-1.2%); inflation of 20%. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Eju.tv counts Paz as the fourth Bolivian president to follow his father into the office, after Adolfo Ballivián and the brothers Hernán Siles Zuazo and Luis Adolfo Siles Salinas. He studied economics and international relations, BioBioChile notes, and his mother, Carmen Pereira, is Spanish.

From Tarija Mayor to President

Paz was a deputy and a Tarija councillor before winning the Tarija mayoralty in 2015 against Evo Morales’s MAS party, BioBioChile reports. He governed the southern city until 2020 and later became a senator for Comunidad Ciudadana, the opposition force of former president Carlos Mesa.

In 2025 he ran for the Partido Demócrata Cristiano (PDC), a Christian Democratic party, with the former police captain Edmand Lara Montaño as his running mate. The electoral authority’s count gave the pair 3,519,534 valid votes, or 54.96%, against 2,884,661 votes, or 45.04%, for the Libre alliance of former president Jorge “Tuto” Quiroga in the 19 October 2025 runoff.

The electoral tribunal proclaimed the winners on Monday 27 October, eju.tv reports. Paz took the oath on Saturday 8 November 2025 in Plaza Murillo, La Paz, Teleamazonas reported that day.

How Paz Approaches Chile

Paz first met Kast, then Chile’s president-elect, in Panama on 29 January and called the talks “frank and fraternal”, 24 Horas reported. He said both countries should focus on present and future problems rather than past ones.

On 7 February he told the national chamber of commerce that he wants “a new stage” and is “looking at the future” rather than the past, and offered Bolivian territory and ports as a link between the Atlantic and the Pacific, according to a Brújula Digital report carried by eju.tv. He then travelled to Santiago for Kast’s inauguration on 11 March and proposed a joint effort on mining with Chile and Peru, Correo del Sur said.

Before Kast landed, Paz said that “the past was conflict, the present and the future must be development”, El Deber reported on Thursday 15 October. He added that children should not have to die over the accounts of the past.

The Pressure at Home

Former president Evo Morales said on Thursday that failing to negotiate the sea question at the meeting would be “treason to the homeland”, Opinión reported. Fernando Aramayo, Paz’s Minister of the Presidency, said on Friday that Bolivia will not renounce its historic maritime claim but must also pursue an economic agenda, El Deber reports.

Quiroga, the runoff loser, told Kast to present evidence, retract or apologise over the alleged drugs in Bolivian timber held in Chilean ports, La Tercera reported. That case is an allegation under investigation, and La Tercera says the inquiry is not finished.

What Paz Said After Meeting Kast

After the private meeting Paz wrote that “after decades, we have the opportunity to build a new stage in the relationship between Bolivia and Chile” and that “it is time to turn dialogue into concrete agreements”, Red Uno reported. La Tercera listed a mining memorandum, terms of reference to modernise the ACE 22 trade pact and fibre-optic, health and power-link initiatives as the documents on the table.

La Tercera wrote at the close of its edition that the signing and the joint declaration of the two presidents were still under way. No outlet we reviewed had published their contents by mid-afternoon in La Paz on Friday.

What It Means for You

For US investors, Paz is a president who has linked his political fortunes to trade routes and mining cooperation with a neighbour that controls Bolivia’s main ports. A signed text would show whether he can turn warm words into rules, while his critics at home cap how far he can go on the sea claim.

His economic record is set out in Who Is Rodrigo Paz? Bolivia’s President and His US Bet, and his place in the region in Bolivia’s Role in Latin America: Lithium, Mercosur, Allies, while no new border rule for travellers has been announced.

What Is Not Known

The contents of the joint declaration and of any signed memorandums are not yet public, so the practical result of the talks is unconfirmed. Whether ambassadors will return, and on whose initiative, is also not established.

It is not known how the timber case will be resolved or whether Paz will take the sea question beyond dialogue. The criticisms by Morales and Quiroga are political statements, not findings.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Rodrigo Paz Pereira?

He is Bolivia’s president since 8 November 2025, a former mayor of Tarija and senator. He is the son of former president Jaime Paz Zamora.

How did Rodrigo Paz win the presidency?

He won the 19 October 2025 runoff with 54.96% of valid votes against Jorge Quiroga’s 45.04%, the electoral authority’s count shows. He ran for the Partido Demócrata Cristiano with Edmand Lara Montaño as vice president.

What offices did Paz hold before the presidency?

He was a deputy, a Tarija councillor, mayor of Tarija from 2015 to 2020 and later a senator. He studied economics and international relations.

Where does Paz stand on Chile?

He calls for dialogue and trade and says the past should not shape the future. His government says it has not renounced Bolivia’s maritime claim.

What came out of the Paz-Kast meeting?

Paz called for turning dialogue into concrete agreements, and Chilean press listed a mining memorandum and trade-pact terms of reference. The contents of the joint declaration were not yet published at the time of writing.

World.title: National Police Service Commission Kenya: A Profile
World.content:
A Kenya Police traffic officer walks past a minibus on a busy road (Photo: Tmaokisa, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

KENYA · PROFILE

Key Facts — The country Kenya is an East African republic whose 2010 Constitution sets up independent commissions beside its ministries and courts.

— Why it matters The commission is the constitutional gatekeeper for appointments, promotions and discipline of police staff, so its limits shape how the service is run.

— Why now On 16 October 2026 the Court of Appeal limited its recruitment power to civilian staff, which puts its role and its members back in focus.

— What happened A nine-seat body chaired by Dr Amani Yuda Komora lost its appeal over recruiting uniformed officers, a case it fought beside the Law Society of Kenya.

— The numbers Nine seats, six filled by presidential appointment for single six-year terms and three held by the police commanders, since work began on 5 October 2012.

— What it means for you Partners should treat the Inspector-General as the door for uniformed recruitment and the commission as the door for civilian staffing and personnel policy.

— Still open Whether the commission appeals, and how it uses the powers the ruling leaves it ahead of the August 2027 general election.

The National Police Service Commission Kenya relies on for police hiring and discipline is a nine-seat body, and on 16 October 2026 its reach narrowed. The Court of Appeal dismissed its appeal over recruiting uniformed officers, The Star and Capital FM report.

For US readers, the profile matters because anyone working with Kenya’s police on training, vetting or complaints needs to know which office holds which power. Our explainer Kenya Appeals Court NPSC Police Recruitment Ruling Explained covers the judgment, and Kenya NPSC Mandate After Court Ruling: What Comes Next looks ahead, so this piece looks at the body itself.

Where the Commission Came From

Article 246 of the Constitution creates the commission, and Article 248(2) lists it as one of ten commissions in the chapter on independent bodies. Its website says it took over the police personnel function that the Public Service Commission used to handle.

The website traces the idea to the Alston, Akiwumi, Waki and Ransley reports, which blamed politicised appointments, transfers, promotions and discipline for a dysfunctional police service. It says the Ransley task force proposed a dedicated commission that would take charge of those functions.

The commission began work on 5 October 2012, after six commissioners were appointed by Gazette Notice No. 95 of 3 October 2012, its website says. Johnston Kavuludi was the first chairman, and the late Esther Chui Colombini the first vice-chairperson.

Capital FM reported on 2 October 2018 that the first commissioners’ six-year term had ended with only seven of nine seats filled, after vetting more than 5,900 officers since December 2013. The same report recalled that a human head was left in a box outside its offices on 30 August 2013 with a threat to chairman Kavuludi while vetting was under way.

Who Sits on the Commission Today

Article 246(2) gives the commission nine seats: six appointed by the President and three held by the Inspector-General and the two Deputy Inspectors-General. The commission’s own FAQ notes that five of the nine members have served or are serving as police officers.

Dr Amani Yuda Komora chairs it, and The Star reported that he was sworn in on Thursday 28 August 2025 with a pledge to restore harmony and teamwork. His biography on the commission’s website lists human resources posts at the Kenya Ports Authority and the Kenya Anti-Corruption Commission, and the vice-chairmanship of the Salaries and Remuneration Commission from 2018 to 2024.

Prof Collette Suda is vice-chairperson, and the website says she was a Principal Secretary for gender affairs before joining. She took the oath on 8 July 2025 with Peris Muthoni Kimani, a retired Assistant Inspector-General after 39 years, and Benjamin Juma Imai, who has more than 40 years in the Administration Police, according to the commission.

Angeline Yiamiton Siparo, who was sworn in beside Komora, and Edwin Cheluget complete the appointed members the website lists. Inspector-General Douglas Kanja and his deputies Eliud Lagat and Gilbert Masengeli sit by right, and the site names the Director of Criminal Investigations, Amin Mohamed, as a co-opted member.

The secretary and chief executive is Peter Leley, whom the commission appoints under Article 250(12), and his biography lists a stint as Uasin Gishu’s first County Secretary. The site gives its address as the sixth floor of CBK Pension Towers on Harambee Avenue in Nairobi.

How Members Are Appointed, Protected and Removed

Article 250(2) says each commissioner is identified under national legislation, approved by the National Assembly and appointed by the President. Under Article 250(6), appointed members serve a single six-year term and cannot be reappointed, so Komora’s term would run to about 2031 if counted from his oath.

Article 250(10) lets members elect the vice-chairperson, and Article 250(11) bars the chair and vice-chair from being of the same gender. Article 249(2) makes the commissions independent and free from direction or control by any person, and Article 249(3) gives each a separate budget vote.

Article 251 allows removal of a non-ex-officio member only for serious violation of the law, gross misconduct, incapacity, incompetence or bankruptcy. A petition goes to the National Assembly, the President may suspend the member, and a tribunal makes a binding recommendation that the President must act on within thirty days.

What the National Police Service Commission Kenya Can and Cannot Do

Article 246(3) tells the commission to recruit and appoint persons to hold or act in offices in the service, confirm appointments, and determine promotions and transfers. It must also exercise disciplinary control and remove officeholders, observing due process.

Its website lists further statutory tasks, among them setting human resources policy on the Inspector-General’s recommendation, advising on pay with the Salaries and Remuneration Commission, hearing appeals from officers and approving training curricula. It also says the commission refers civilian complaints to the Independent Policing Oversight Authority, the human rights commission, the prosecutor or the anti-corruption commission.

The FAQ says the commission does not deal with operational matters, which belong to the command of the Inspector-General and his deputies. The Court of Appeal’s judgment of 16 October 2026 placed uniformed recruitment with the police service, and the commission’s recruitment powers with civilian staff, The Star and Capital FM report.

Capital FM adds that the judges held the commission is not a national security organ under Article 239, and that the promotion, suspension and dismissal of sworn officers sit with the police service under the Inspector-General’s command. For what the commission can still do and what may follow, see the next-steps piece linked above.

What It Means for US Readers

The practical rule is two doors: the Inspector-General for uniformed recruitment and operations, and the commission for civilian staffing, personnel policy and complaints it refers onward. For the wider contest around the 2027 vote, see our explainer Who Runs Kenya in 2026, Ruto, Political Families, Regions, and for how Kenya reached its 2010 settlement see Kenya History Explained, From Origins to 2026.

Visitors and residents should note that this ruling changes who signs off hiring, not what officers do on the street. City practicalities are on our Nairobi page.

What Is Not Known

The full judgment and the text of the National Police Service Commission Act were not available to us, because Kenya Law returned access errors, so the list of statutory functions comes from the commission’s website. The sources reviewed do not say which of the six appointed members holds the seat reserved for a person qualified to be a High Court judge.

The sources also do not say whether the Director of Criminal Investigations and the other co-opted members vote. Nor do they say whether the commission or the Law Society will appeal to the Supreme Court.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Kenya’s National Police Service Commission?

It is the independent body created by Article 246 of the Constitution to handle appointments, promotions, transfers and discipline in the police service. It began work on 5 October 2012, according to its website.

Who chairs the NPSC?

Dr Amani Yuda Komora chairs it, and Prof Collette Suda is vice-chairperson. The Star reported that Komora was sworn in on 28 August 2025.

How many members does the NPSC have and who appoints them?

Article 246(2) sets nine members, six of them appointed by the President and approved by the National Assembly. The other three are the Inspector-General and the two Deputy Inspectors-General.

Can the commission command police operations?

No, because its website says operational matters belong to the command of the Inspector-General and his deputies. Its role covers human resources, discipline and related policy.

How can a commissioner be removed?

Under Article 251, only for grounds such as serious violation of the law, gross misconduct, incapacity, incompetence or bankruptcy. A petition goes to the National Assembly, and a tribunal makes a binding recommendation to the President.
